chunks.t:
nestjs-drizzle-crud is a NestJS Drizzle library. Extend one base class per table and get typed CRUD, filters, pagination and relations.

nestjs-drizzle-crud is a NestJS Drizzle library: you extend one base class per table and get a
typed CRUD service on top of Drizzle ORM. You configure the connection once, bind each service to
its Drizzle table, and every service can find, list, filter, paginate, create, update, soft delete
and bulk write rows on PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite. It does not hide Drizzle: your schema stays yours.

Who this is for, and what you need. 
NestJS developers who use Drizzle ORM, or want to, and are tired of writing the same findAll,
create and update code in every service. You need Node 20 or later, @nestjs/common and
@nestjs/core 10 or later, drizzle-orm from 0.28.0 up to (not including) 1.0.0, and
reflect-metadata 0.1.13 or 0.2. Add postgres 3 or mysql2 3 if you want the module to
open the PostgreSQL or MySQL connection for you.

One empty service class gives you the whole read and write surface, and configuration turns on
the rest:

- Reads. find, findOne, findAll with a { data, total, page, limit } envelope,
count and exists. See CRUD operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/crud-operations).
- Filtering. Column operators (gte, in, between, iContains and more), and, or
and not groups, and filters on related tables. See Filtering (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering) and
Relation filters (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relation-filters).
- Pagination. Offset pages with a capped limit, multi-column sorts, and keyset pagination
through findByCursor. See Pagination and sorting (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting) and
Cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination).
- Relations. Belongs-to, has-many and many-to-many, eager loaded with one batched query per
relation instead of one per row. See Relations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations).
- Writes. create, update, upsert, soft delete, restore, and mass writes that run in one
transaction. See Upsert (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/upsert), Bulk operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations) and
Soft delete (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/soft-delete).
- Safety. Column allowlists, tenant scopes, optimistic locking, and exceptions that map to
404, 409 and 400 without a custom filter. See Allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists),
Multi-tenancy (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy) and Errors (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/errors).
- Wiring. A generated controller, OpenAPI decorators, test helpers and an MCP server for
coding agents. See Controller factory (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/controller-factory) and
AI agents (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/ai-agents).

chunks.h: What does a service look like?
chunks.t:
A service is an empty class that names its row, DTO and filter types. forFeature binds it to a
table and builds it for you, so there is no constructor and no @Injectable().

UsersService now has every method in CRUD operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/crud-operations), typed against
User. The quick start (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/quick-start) builds the rest of the app around it.

Fact Value 
--- --- 
Databases PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1 (dialect: "postgresql", "mysql" or "sqlite") 
Documented version 
License MIT 
Runtime dependencies None. Peer dependencies only, three of them optional (postgres, mysql2, @nestjs/swagger) 
Node 20 or later 
Source GitHub, published on npm

chunks.h: When is it the wrong tool?
chunks.t:
- Most of your endpoints are reports. Window functions, CTEs and hand-tuned joins read better
as plain Drizzle. You can still add those as extra methods on the same service.
- Your writes are workflows. Multi-step domain operations belong in your own service code.
Use the package for the plain entities around them.
- You need another dialect. The dialect setting accepts "postgresql", "mysql" and
"sqlite" only, so SQL Server, Oracle and MongoDB are out.

Does nestjs-drizzle-crud replace Drizzle ORM?. 
No. It builds Drizzle queries from your own Drizzle tables. You keep your schema and migrations, and you can inject DRIZZLE_DB to run any Drizzle query yourself.

Which databases does it support?. 
PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite (including libSQL and Cloudflare D1). Full-text search is PostgreSQL only. The module builds the connection from a connectionString on PostgreSQL and MySQL; on SQLite you pass a Drizzle instance you built yourself. On D1, bulk writes are not available.

Do I have to write controllers?. 
No. createCrudController generates the list, get, create, update, delete and bulk routes for a service. You can also write a normal NestJS controller and call the service methods yourself.

Does loading relations cause N+1 queries?. 
No. A belongs-to relation is joined into the main query, and has-many and many-to-many relations load with one batched query per relation for the whole result, whatever the row count.

Is it free to use in a commercial project?. 
Yes. The package is MIT licensed and has no runtime dependencies of its own.
The library is built and maintained by Avytrix Technologies (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/built-by-avytrix).

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.h: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.t:
Drizzle aggregates in NestJS: count() rows, group by a column with countBy, and relation counts per row with options.counts. SUM needs a custom method.

Drizzle aggregates in NestJS are three counting tools on your service. count(filters) returns how many rows match. countBy(column, filters) runs one GROUP BY and returns the count for each value of a column. options.counts puts the number of related rows on each row under _count, with one grouped query per relation and no N+1. SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX are not built in: write those as a custom service method.

Counts only. 
The package aggregates with count( ) and nothing else. For a sum or an average, see how do I get a SUM or AVG? below. The examples use an AuthorsService (has-many posts, many-to-many tags) and a PostsService (belongs-to author).

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.t:
Three methods and one option, all counting.

API Returns Query 
--- --- --- 
count(filters?, options?) number One SELECT count( ) 
countBy(column, filters?, options?) Array<{ value, count } One GROUP BY column 
options.counts on a read _count: { relation: n } on each row One GROUP BY per relation, for the whole page 
findAll total number (or null with withCount: false) One count( ) beside the data query 

To skip the total count of a list, see how do I skip the count query? (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting#how-do-i-skip-the-count-query)

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.t:
Call count(filters?, options?). It takes the same filters as findAll and returns a number.

Filters, options.search, the tenant scope (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy) and soft delete apply, so soft-deleted rows are not counted unless you pass withDeleted: true (or onlyDeleted: true to count only the trash).

c.s:
await this.postsService.count({ status: 'published' });
// 15

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I count rows per column value?
chunks.t:
Call countBy(column, filters?, options?). It returns one entry per value, largest group first, ties ordered by value.

It is one query:

Two more rules:

- The column must be in filterableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) when that list is set, since grouping exposes its values the way filtering does.
- The type of value is a generic: countBy<string ('status') returns CountByRow<string [].

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I add relation counts to each row?
chunks.t:
Pass options.counts with the relation names. Each row gets a _count object.

counts works on find, findOne, findAll, findByCursor, and on the rows a write returns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations-on-writes). From a query string,?counts=posts,tags sets it. See parse query strings into filters (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing).

c.s:
const page = await this.authorsService.findAll({}, {}, { counts: ['posts'] });
page.data[0]._count; // { posts: 10 }

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.t:
With one SELECT key, count( )... WHERE key IN (...) GROUP BY key per relation, for every row of the page at once, and the relations run concurrently. A page of 50 authors with counts: ['posts', 'tags'] is the data query, the count query and two grouped queries, never one per row.

Relation type What is counted 
--- --- 
Has-many Related rows that are not soft-deleted. 
Many-to-many Links in the join table whose target row is not soft-deleted. 

When select narrows the columns, the key the count groups on is added back, so the counts still attach.

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.h: Can I count only some related rows?
chunks.t:
Yes. Pass an object instead of a list. Each value is a filter on the related table, or true for all of them.

The filter accepts everything a filter (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering) does, groups included.

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.t:
These are the limits, and each one is a 400 when broken:

- Only has-many and many-to-many relations. Counting a belongs-to, or a relation that is not configured, is a 400.
- The relation must be in loadableRelations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) when that list is set.
- Counts are top level: posts, not posts.comments.

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I get a SUM or AVG?
chunks.t:
Write a method on your service with Drizzle's own aggregate helpers. Your methods can use this.config.db, the Drizzle instance the service runs on.

A custom query does not get the package's soft delete, tenant scope or allowlists for free, so add the deleted_at IS NULL condition (and your tenant column) yourself, as above. Drizzle's sum returns a string, which is why the result goes through Number.

chunks.p: Count, group by and aggregates in Drizzle
chunks.t:
Does countBy count soft-deleted rows?. 
No. Soft-deleted rows are left out unless you pass withDeleted: true, the same as count.

Does options.counts run one query per row?. 
No. It runs one grouped query per relation for every row of the result at once, so a page of 50 rows with two counted relations adds two queries.

Can I count a belongs-to relation?. 
No. A belongs-to has at most one row, so counts on it is a 400. Only has-many and many-to-many relations have a count.

Does the package have sum, avg, min or max?. 
No. It only counts. Write a custom service method with Drizzle's sum, avg, min or max over this.config.db.

Can countBy group by a related column?. 
Yes, for a top-level belongs-to relation written as relation.column, such as author.name. A has-many or many-to-many column is a 400.

NestJS Drizzle MCP server for AI agents
chunks.h: NestJS Drizzle MCP server for AI agents
chunks.t:
Run the NestJS Drizzle MCP server with npx so Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot can read the package docs, and add the AGENT.md rules file to your repo.

The NestJS Drizzle MCP server ships inside @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud: run npx -p @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud nestjs-drizzle-crud-mcp and any MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI and others) can list, read and search the package docs while it writes code. The package also ships a rules file, AGENT.md, with templates that load it into the file your agent reads. Neither adds a dependency to your app.

Read-only by design. 
The server only reads the markdown files inside its own installed package. It never connects to
your database and never writes anything.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle MCP server for AI agents
chunks.h: What are the server's stable facts?
chunks.t:
Fact Value 
--- --- 
Package version 
Command (bin) nestjs-drizzle-crud-mcp 
Transport stdio: JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line 
Runtime dependencies zero; the server is plain Node with no MCP SDK 
Node.js 20 or later, like the package 
Tools list_docs, get_doc, search_docs 
Documents agent-guide (AGENT.md), readme (README.md), changelog (CHANGELOG.md) 

The server reports the installed package version in its initialize reply, so it always serves the docs for the version you run.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle MCP server for AI agents
chunks.h: How do I run the MCP server?
chunks.t: It starts and waits for JSON-RPC messages on stdin. You do not run it by hand day to day: your agent starts it from the config below.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle MCP server for AI agents
chunks.h: How do I add it to my agent?
chunks.t:
Register it once per project. Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Cline use the same mcpServers shape:

Or add it from the CLI:

VS Code keeps the entries under servers instead of mcpServers:

Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Cline take the same mcpServers block as Claude Code in their own MCP settings file. Zed uses a context_servers entry in its settings.json with the same command and arguments.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle MCP server for AI agents
chunks.h: Which tools does the server expose?
chunks.t:
Three, defined in src/mcp/server.ts (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/blob/main/packages/nestjs-drizzle-crud/src/mcp/server.ts):

Tool Arguments Returns 
--- --- --- 
list_docs none Each document with its top-level headings. Start here. 
get_doc doc, optional section A whole document, or every section whose heading contains section (case-insensitive). 
search_docs query, optional limit (default 5, max 20) The best-matching sections across all three documents, best first, each cut to 1,500 characters. 

doc is one of agent-guide, readme or changelog. A typical agent turn is search_docs({ query: "has-many eager loading" }), then get_doc({ doc: "agent-guide", section: "Relations" }).

A tool failure, such as an unknown tool name, comes back as a result with isError: true, so the client shows it to the model instead of dropping the turn.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle MCP server for AI agents
chunks.h: Which rules file does my agent read?
chunks.t:
Copy the template that matches your tool into your project root:

Agent File in your project root 
--- --- 
OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Zed, Cline, Windsurf, Jules AGENTS.md 
Claude Code CLAUDE.md 
Gemini CLI GEMINI.md 
Aider CONVENTIONS.md, then aider --read CONVENTIONS.md 

Each template is a pointer, not a copy. Besides comments, it holds one line:

AGENT.md ships inside the package and stays the single source of truth, so an upgrade updates the rules with it. If your agent does not resolve @ imports, paste the contents of AGENT.md in place of that line, or run the MCP server so the agent fetches the guidance itself.

Using several agents on one repo? Copy the template to each filename, or keep AGENTS.md and make the others a one-line pointer to it.

c.s:
cp node_modules/@avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/AGENTS.template.md ./AGENTS.md   # most tools
cp node_modules/@avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/CLAUDE.template.md ./CLAUDE.md   # Claude Code

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle MCP server for AI agents
chunks.h: What is in the rules file?
chunks.t:
AGENT.md is written for an agent about to add an endpoint. It covers the facts agents most often get wrong:

- A service is normally an empty subclass of SqlBaseCrudService, and the table goes in forFeature, not in the service.
- Filters are objects, such as { age: { gte: 18 } }, and findAll returns { data, total, page, limit }.
- Which exception maps to which HTTP status code, and how allowlists, scope and soft delete work.
- A definition of done, so the agent stops when the endpoint is complete.

It exists to prevent the two most common mistakes: hand-writing repository code the base service already has, and injecting the database into a service.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle MCP server for AI agents
chunks.t:
Does the MCP server add a dependency to my app?. 
No. It is a bin inside nestjs-drizzle-crud with zero runtime dependencies, so installing the package is all it needs.

Can the MCP server touch my database?. 
No. It only reads AGENT.md, README.md and CHANGELOG.md from its own installed package and answers over stdio.

Which transport does nestjs-drizzle-crud-mcp use?. 
stdio, with one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per line. Your MCP client starts the process and talks to it directly.

Do I need both the rules file and the MCP server?. 
No, either works alone. The rules file loads the guidance up front; the server lets the agent look things up as it goes.

NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.h: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.t:
A NestJS Drizzle filter allowlist limits the columns a client may filter, sort, select, search and write. Anything outside a set list is a 400.

A NestJS Drizzle filter allowlist is a per-entity list of the columns a client may filter on. nestjs-drizzle-crud has one for each part of a request: filtering, sorting, selecting, searching, loading relations and writing columns. You set them in forFeature, and a request that names anything outside a set list is a 400 Bad Request, both in the service and in parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing). An unset list allows everything.

Set these on every entity a client can reach. 
Without allowlists, a list endpoint that forwards the query string lets a client filter, sort and select on every column of the table, secrets included.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.h: How do I set the allowlists?
chunks.t: Add the keys to the entity's config in forFeature. Each one is a plain array of strings:

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.t:
Because every column you leave open is one a client can read or probe. Three examples:

Missing list What a client can do 
--- --- 
selectableColumns?fields=password_hash returns the hashes. 
filterableColumns?password_hash[startsWith]=a guesses a hash one character at a time. 
writableColumns A body with role: "admin" sets it, unless every DTO strips it. 

filterableColumns also takes full dotted paths for deeper relation filters (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relation-filters) (state.country.code) and governs countBy (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/aggregates). For nested writes, see Relations on writes (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations-on-writes).

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.h: What does an unset or empty list mean?
chunks.t: An unset list allows everything, which is how 3.3 behaved. An empty list ([]) allows nothing. The one exception is writableRelations: unset, nested writes are off.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.h: What does a rejected request return?
chunks.t:
A 400 whose message names the list and the path. The service throws a Nest BadRequestException for the read lists and a ValidationFailedException for writableColumns:

List Message 
--- --- 
filterableColumns Filtering on "password_hash" is not allowed 
sortableColumns Sorting by "email" is not allowed 
selectableColumns Selecting "password_hash" is not allowed 
searchableColumns Searching "email" is not allowed 
loadableRelations Loading the relation "sessions" is not allowed 
writableColumns Validation failed: the column "role" is not writable 

See Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/errors) for the full response shape.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.t:
findOne(where) keys are not checked against filterableColumns, because findOne is usually a server-side lookup (findOne({ email }) during login). Its select and relations options are checked. The configured defaultSort is not checked either.

For any other trusted, server-side call, pass skipAllowlists: true:

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.h: Which columns can a body write by default?
chunks.t:
Everything except the columns the package manages itself. Without writableColumns:

- the soft delete column is ignored on create and update,
- the optimistic locking (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/optimistic-locking) version column is ignored on create and update,
- the primary key and the createdAt timestamp are ignored on update.

Ignored means dropped silently, so a PATCH body that echoes id back still works. An update that has nothing left to set is a 400 (Validation failed: there are no columns to update).

With writableColumns set, any column outside the list is a 400, the managed columns included. List the primary key there if your create path takes client supplied keys, such as uuids or natural keys. Keys that are not columns at all are ignored. The version column is never written from a body either way.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.t:
Validate bodies with DTOs. Keep ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true }) and real DTOs for request bodies. The allowlists are a second line, not a replacement.

Lock down writes. Set writableColumns on every entity with a public create or update route.

Lock down reads. Set selectableColumns and filterableColumns on every entity behind a list route, and leave secrets out of both.

Guard sensitive relations. Set loadableRelations when a related table holds data some callers must not see.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.t: Keep ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true }) and real DTOs for request bodies. The allowlists are a second line, not a replacement.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.t: Set writableColumns on every entity with a public create or update route.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.t: Set selectableColumns and filterableColumns on every entity behind a list route, and leave secrets out of both.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.t: Set loadableRelations when a related table holds data some callers must not see.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists
chunks.t:
Is the primary key always allowed?. 
For sorting and selecting, yes: every page sorts on it anyway. For filtering and writing, only when you list it.

Does an empty allowlist allow everything?. 
No. An unset list allows everything, but an empty array allows nothing, so filterableColumns: [] turns filtering off for that entity.

How do I bypass the allowlists for a server-side query?. 
Pass skipAllowlists: true in the call options. Use it only for trusted calls your own code builds, never for input from a request.

Does parseQuery use the same allowlists?. 
Yes. parseQuery rejects anything outside a set list with the same 400, and uses searchableColumns as the default search columns.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle filter and column allowlists

chunks.t:
Every public method on SqlBaseCrudService in nestjs-drizzle-crud, with its signature, return type, the errors it throws and the options it takes.

SqlBaseCrudService is the abstract class every nestjs-drizzle-crud service extends, and its public methods are the whole CRUD API: reads, writes, bulk writes, search and three helpers for controllers. Each method takes an optional SqlOperationOptions object last, returns a promise of plain rows, and throws an HttpException subclass, so Nest answers with the right 4xx status.

All four generics are required. 
The class is SqlBaseCrudService and none of the four has a
default. Pass all of them, and use CrudFilter for FilterDto when the filters come from a query
string.

chunks.h: What does the class signature look like?
chunks.t:
The class is generic over the row type and the three input shapes, and its constructor takes the merged entity config.

Generic Used by 
--- --- 
T The row type, usually typeof users.$inferSelect. Every method returns it. 
CreateDto create, massCreate, upsert and massUpsert. 
UpdateDto update and massUpdate. 
FilterDto findAll, findByCursor, count and countBy. Use CrudFilter (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/config-types#filter-sort-cursor-and-upsert-types) when filters come from parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing). 

You never call the constructor yourself. DrizzleCrudModule.forFeature builds the service and hands it the config, so a service is normally an empty subclass:

Method Returns Notes 
--- --- --- 
find(id, options?) Promise By primary key. null when the row is missing, soft-deleted or outside the scope. 
findOne(where, options?) Promise where is a Partial: a value is an exact, case-sensitive match, null is IS NULL, and an operator object works as in findAll. undefined values are skipped. A key that is not a column, or no condition left at all, is a 400 rather than an arbitrary row. 
findAll(filters?, pagination?, options?) Promise { data, total, page, limit }. With a literal withCount: false it returns UncountedCrudPage: total is null and hasMore is set (skip the count (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting#how-do-i-skip-the-count-query)). sortOrder defaults to "desc", and ORDER BY always ends with the primary key. An unknown filter key is a 400. 
findByCursor(filters?, pagination?, options?) Promise Keyset pagination: { data, limit, nextCursor, total? }. total only with count: true. See Cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination). 
exists(id, options?) Promise<boolean Runs find with only the primary key selected. 
count(filters?, options?) Promise<number Rows matching the filters and options.search. No pagination. 
countBy(column, filters?, options?) Promise [] [{ value, count }] per value of a column or a belongs-to relation.column, largest group first. One GROUP BY. The column must be filterable. See Aggregates (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/aggregates).

Every read takes withDeleted or onlyDeleted to include or only return soft-deleted rows (Soft delete (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/soft-delete)), and counts for _count on each row. On an entity with a scope (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy), a read only sees the caller's rows.

Method Returns Notes 
--- --- --- 
create(data, options?) Promise Runs validateCreate, beforeCreate, mapCreateDtoToEntity, the insert, then afterCreate. Sets the timestamps, the scope and the version. 
update(id, data, options?) Promise 404 when the row is missing. 400 (ValidationFailedException) when data has no column to set. Runs validateUpdate, beforeUpdate, mapUpdateDtoToEntity, the update, then afterUpdate. 
softDelete(id, options?) Promise<boolean Sets the soft delete column to now. 404 when the row is missing. 400 when soft delete is off for the entity. 
restore(id, options?) Promise Clears the soft delete column. 404 when the row is missing. 
delete(id, options?) Promise<boolean Hard delete. 404 for a missing row or a row in the trash; 409 (EntityInUseException) when other rows still reference it. 
forceDelete(id, options?) Promise<boolean Hard delete whether or not the row is soft-deleted. Runs the delete hooks. 
upsert(data, upsert?, options?) Promise ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on Postgres, ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE on MySQL. upsert is UpsertOptions: { conflictTarget?, update? }. See Upsert (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/upsert). 
attach(id, relation, relatedIds, options?) Promise Links many-to-many rows through the join table and returns the row with the relation loaded. See Relations on writes (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations-on-writes). 
detach(id, relation, relatedIds?, options?) Promise Unlinks the ids, or every link when relatedIds is left out. 
sync(id, relation, relatedIds, options?) Promise Makes the links exactly relatedIds.

Writes take options.relations and options.counts and return the rows with them loaded. With a versionColumn (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/optimistic-locking), update, softDelete, restore and delete take expectedVersion (or the version in an update body) and answer a stale one with a 409. With global hooks (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events) on, every write raises one before and one after event.

create, update and upsert apply writableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists). Without that list, both drop the soft delete and version columns from the body, and update also drops the primary key and the createdAt column.

Every bulk method runs in one transaction (or joins options.transaction) and rolls back on any failure.

Method Returns 
--- --- 
massCreate(data[], options?) Promise 
massUpdate(ids[], data, options?) Promise 
massSoftDelete(ids[], options?) Promise<boolean 
massRestore(ids[], options?) Promise 
massDelete(ids[], options?) Promise<boolean 
massForceDelete(ids[], options?) Promise<boolean 
massUpsert(data[], upsert?, options?) Promise 

Each one is a single statement for the whole set, plus one SELECT that checks the ids exist for the methods that take ids. bulkMode: "perItem" runs the single-row method per item instead, each in its own savepoint. A failure throws BulkOperationException, a 400 whose body is { statusCode, error, message, errors: [{ index id, status, message }] }. See Bulk operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations).

Method Returns Notes 
--- --- --- 
fullTextSearch(term, columns, pagination?, options?) Promise<{ data: T[]; total: number; page: number; limit: number } PostgreSQL only. to_tsvector('english',...) @@ plainto_tsquery('english',...) by default, ordered by ts_rank, then the primary key. options is FullTextSearchOptions: filters, relations, select and counts work as on findAll, language picks the configuration and queryMode: "websearch" uses websearch_to_tsquery. Page and limit always apply. An empty column list or an unknown column is a 400. Respects soft delete and scope. 

For a search inside a normal list, pass options.search to findAll or count instead. See Full-text search (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/full-text-search).

Method Returns Notes 
--- --- --- 
parseQuery(query, options?) ParsedCrudQuery Turns an HTTP query object into { filters, pagination, sort, options, isCursor,... } with this entity's relations, primary key and allowlists. See Parse query strings (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing). 
parseId(raw) Promise<unknown Parses a route id by the primary key column: ParseIntPipe for an integer, ParseUUIDPipe for a uuid, BigInt for a bigint, the string otherwise. Bad input is a 400. 
idKind() "int" \ "bigint" \ "uuid" \ "string" What the primary key column holds.
These are not callable from outside the service. Override the hooks in your subclass, and call the helpers from your own methods.

Member Signature Default 
--- --- --- 
validateCreate (data: CreateDto) = Promise<void Does nothing. Throw ValidationFailedException to reject. 
validateUpdate (id, data: UpdateDto) = Promise<void Does nothing. 
beforeCreate (data: CreateDto) = Promise Returns data. 
afterCreate (entity: T) = Promise<void Does nothing. 
beforeUpdate (id, data: UpdateDto) = Promise Returns data. 
afterUpdate (entity: T) = Promise<void Does nothing. 
beforeSoftDelete, afterSoftDelete (id) = Promise<void Do nothing. 
beforeRestore (id) = Promise<void Does nothing. 
afterRestore (entity: T) = Promise<void Does nothing. 
beforeDelete, afterDelete (id) = Promise<void Do nothing. 
mapCreateDtoToEntity (data: CreateDto) = Record<string, any A shallow copy of data. 
mapUpdateDtoToEntity (data: UpdateDto) = Record<string, any A shallow copy of data. 
executeSqlTransaction (operation: (tx) = Promise, existingTransaction?) = Promise Runs operation in existingTransaction when given, otherwise in a new db.transaction. 
bindLimit (db) = { limit: number; name: string } The most bound parameters one statement may carry, and the database's name for the 400: PostgreSQL and MySQL 65,535, SQLite 32,766, Cloudflare D1 100. Since 3.7.2. 
relationChunkSize (db) = number How many parent keys one batched relation or count query binds: the bind limit less headroom, so 64,535 on PostgreSQL and MySQL, 31,766 on SQLite, 90 on D1. A level with more keys is loaded in several queries. Since 3.8.0. 
getEntityName () = string The Drizzle table name, used in error messages. 
config SqlCrudConfig The merged entity config, including db and table for hand-written queries.

hooks: { skipBefore: true } or { skipAfter: true } in the options skips the before or after hooks for one call. See Hooks and validation (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/hooks-validation).

The transaction commits when the callback resolves and rolls back when it throws. See Transactions (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/transactions).

The last argument of every method. Every key is optional.

", description: "The context a function scope reads. Defaults to CrudContext.current()." },
skipScope: { type: "boolean", description: "Run this trusted call without the entity's scope." },
skipEvents: { type: "boolean", description: "Do not raise module-level events for this call." },
expectedVersion: { type: "number", description: "Optimistic locking: the version the caller last read." },
expectedVersions: { type: "Record<string, number ", description: "Optimistic locking for mass writes, keyed by the id as a string." },
}}
/ 

relations joins a top-level belongs-to into the main query and loads has-many, many-to-many and every nested level with one batched query each for the whole result, never one per row. See Relations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations) and Column selection (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/column-selection). The locks are described on Row-level locks (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/row-locks).

Does SqlBaseCrudService give default types to its generics?. 
No. All four generics, T, CreateDto, UpdateDto and FilterDto, are required. A subclass that passes only the row type does not compile.

Which methods throw EntityNotFoundException?. 
update, softDelete, restore and delete throw it (404) when the row is missing, and the mass versions report it per id inside a BulkOperationException. Reads never throw it: find and findOne return null and exists returns false.

What does findAll return with withCount set to false?. 
It returns { data, total: null, page, limit, hasMore }. The service fetches one row past the page to set hasMore and skips the COUNT( ) query.

Can I call executeSqlTransaction from a controller?. 
No, it is protected. Call it from a method on your service subclass, and pass { transaction: tx } to every CRUD call that should join the transaction.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Bulk insert, update and delete with Drizzle in NestJS. Each mass method is one statement in a transaction, and a failure lists every failed item.

For a Drizzle bulk insert or update in NestJS, call massCreate, massUpdate, massSoftDelete, massRestore, massDelete, massForceDelete or massUpsert on your service. Each one writes the whole set with one statement inside a single transaction. If any item fails, nothing is written and the call throws a BulkOperationException, a 400 whose body lists every failed item with its own status and message.

All or nothing. 
A bulk call that returns has written every row. A bulk call that throws has written none of them. You never have to clean up a half-finished batch.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Seven, one per single-row write:

Method Returns Notes 
--- --- --- 
massCreate(data[], options?) Promise One multi-row insert. 
massUpdate(ids[], data, options?) Promise The same changes applied to every id. 
massSoftDelete(ids[], options?) Promise<boolean Needs soft delete (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/soft-delete) on the entity. 
massRestore(ids[], options?) Promise Needs soft delete on the entity. 
massDelete(ids[], options?) Promise<boolean Hard delete. With soft delete on, an id already in the trash is a 404 entry. 
massForceDelete(ids[], options?) Promise<boolean Hard delete, including rows that are in the trash. 
massUpsert(data[], upsert?, options?) Promise See Upsert (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/upsert). 

Duplicate ids are written once. The rows come back in the order of the ids you passed. massSoftDelete and massRestore are a 400 BadRequestException when soft delete is not enabled for the entity.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: How many queries does a bulk call cost?
chunks.t:
A fixed number, whatever the number of ids:

Method Statements 
--- --- 
massCreate one multi-row INSERT... RETURNING 
massUpdate one SELECT to check every id exists, one UPDATE... WHERE id IN (...) per distinct SET (one, unless beforeUpdate returns different data per id; one shared sql expression object counts as one value) 
massSoftDelete, massRestore one SELECT, one UPDATE... WHERE id IN (...) 
massDelete, massForceDelete one SELECT, one DELETE... WHERE id IN (...) 
massUpsert one INSERT... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE 

So massUpdate over 100 ids is two queries, not two hundred.

Two exceptions on MySQL, which has no RETURNING: one more SELECT reads the written rows back, and massCreate of rows with auto-increment keys inserts row by row, because MySQL only reports the first id of a multi-row insert, then reads them all back with one SELECT (since 3.8.0; before, one per row). If every row carries its own primary key, massCreate stays one INSERT plus one SELECT.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: How many queries does a bulk call cost?
chunks.t: On SQLite the statements are the same as on PostgreSQL, but only with a driver that has async transactions, such as libSQL. On Cloudflare D1 and on synchronous drivers (better-sqlite3, bun:sqlite, sql.js) every bulk method throws a TransactionException that says why; SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1 (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/sqlite) has the details.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: What does a bulk call options object take?
chunks.t:
Every bulk method takes the same SqlOperationOptions as its single-row counterpart. These are the ones that matter most for bulk writes:

", description: "With a version column: the expected version per id, keyed by the id as a string. An id at another version is a 409 entry." },
"hooks.skipBefore": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Skip the before hooks for every item." },
"hooks.skipAfter": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Skip the after hooks for every item." },
skipEvents: { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Do not raise module-level events for this call." },
}}
/

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: What happens when one item fails?
chunks.t:
The whole call is rolled back and throws BulkOperationException. Every bulk method runs in one transaction, so no partial write is ever visible to a later read.

When the set statement fails, the package still needs to know which items caused it. It replays the batch one item at a time, each in its own savepoint, and reports the items that fail on their own. That replay only runs on the failure path, and it leaves nothing behind, even inside your own transaction:

- In the transaction the bulk method opened itself (no transaction option), the happy path sends no savepoint at all since 3.8.0: massUpdate is BEGIN, one SELECT, one UPDATE, COMMIT. When the set statement fails, that transaction rolls back and the replay runs in a fresh transaction that is rolled back too. Once a before event has handed the transaction to a subscriber, which may have written in it, the replay stays inside it, as below.
- In your transaction, the set statement runs in a savepoint and the replay inside an outer savepoint that is rolled back at the end, because on PostgreSQL a failed statement would otherwise abort your whole transaction. A failed bulk call leaves your transaction usable.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: What happens when one item fails?
chunks.t:
Two cases are worth knowing:

- Two rows of the same batch that clash only with each other (the same unique email, say) show up as the second of the pair, because the replay has already written the first.
- When no single item fails on its own, the statement's own error is thrown instead of a BulkOperationException.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: What does a failed bulk call return over HTTP?
chunks.t:
A 400 whose body names every failed item. massCreate and massUpsert identify an item by its index in the input array; the other methods use the id you passed:

Each entry is a BulkOperationItemError:

An error that is not an HTTP exception (a driver fault, say) appears as status: 500 with the message Internal server error, so SQL and parameters never reach the client. BulkOperationException extends Nest's BadRequestException, so if you let it propagate, Nest's default filter sends this body as is.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I handle BulkOperationException in code?
chunks.t:
Catch it and read errors, which keeps the original Error per failed item:

The errors property is for logging. The response body carries the safe summary.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: Do hooks run once per row in a bulk call?
chunks.t:
Yes. The per-service hooks run once per item, in array order; only the SQL is shared:

Method Per item, before the statement Per item, after the statement 
--- --- --- 
massCreate validateCreate, beforeCreate afterCreate 
massUpdate validateUpdate, beforeUpdate (after the existence check) afterUpdate 
massSoftDelete beforeSoftDelete afterSoftDelete 
massRestore beforeRestore afterRestore 
massDelete, massForceDelete beforeDelete afterDelete 
massUpsert validateCreate, beforeCreate none 

So massCreate([a, b, c]) calls validateCreate and beforeCreate three times, runs one insert, then calls afterCreate three times.

If a before hook throws for one item, that item is recorded as failed, the rest still run so every failure is reported, and nothing is written. If beforeUpdate returns different data for different ids, one SET cannot express it, so massUpdate writes those rows with one UPDATE each.

Module-level events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events) fire once for the whole call instead, with bulk: true and every id, before and after the statement and inside the transaction.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: Can I still run one query per item?
chunks.t: Yes, with bulkMode: 'perItem'. Each item then goes through the single-row method (create, update, delete and so on) in its own savepoint, as in 3.3. Use it when a per-item hook must see the rows written before it.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: Do bulk writes work with relations, scope and versions?
chunks.t:
- Relations. relations and counts load onto the returned rows with one query per relation for the whole batch. See Relations on writes (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations-on-writes).
- When the relations load. massCreate loads them inside its transaction, so a load that fails (a pool timeout, a dropped connection) rolls the rows back and a retry does not store them twice. massUpdate, massRestore and massUpsert give the same rows when run twice, so in a transaction they opened themselves they load after the commit and hold their row locks for less time. A failed load there answers with an error although the write is stored; retrying it is safe. The exception is a write whose values hold an SQL expression, such as `massUpdate(ids, { views: sqlviews + 1 }): run twice, it adds twice. Since 3.8.2 such a massUpdate or massUpsert loads inside its transaction like massCreate, so a failed load rolls the increment back and the retry adds once.
- Tenant scope. On a scoped entity (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy), an id of another tenant is a 404 entry and nothing is written.
- Versions. With optimistic locking (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/optimistic-locking), every written row's version goes up by one, and expectedVersions: { '1': 4 }` turns an id at another version into a 409 entry.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: How large can a bulk call be?
chunks.t:
As large as one SQL statement allows. Since 3.7.2 the service counts the bound parameters of every statement it builds and compares them with the database's own limit:

Database Bound parameters per statement 
--- --- 
PostgreSQL 65,535 
MySQL 65,535 
SQLite, libSQL 32,766 (SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER) 
Cloudflare D1 100 

A statement past the limit is a 400 that names its count and the limit, before it reaches the database: Too many values in one statement: 75003 bound parameters, and PostgreSQL takes at most 65535. Split the batch. The count is the real one, so everything adds up: rows times the columns actually written (timestamps and scope included) for massCreate and massUpsert, about three values per id for a versioned massUpdate with expectedVersions, the children of a nested create, the targets of attach and sync, and every list in an IN filter, OR'd lists together. The refusal is not replayed item by item, and the transaction rolls back.

On a server built with a different limit, override the protected bindLimit(db) method in your service.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.h: How large can a bulk call be?
chunks.t: One transaction holding thousands of row locks can also block other connections. For thousands of rows, split the array into chunks of a few hundred and call the bulk method once per chunk, accepting that each chunk commits on its own.

chunks.p: Bulk insert and update with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Is a bulk insert atomic?. 
Yes. Every bulk method runs in one transaction, so a failure rolls back the whole batch and nothing is written.

How do I know which row failed?. 
Catch BulkOperationException. Its response body lists each failed item by index (for massCreate and massUpsert) or by id, with the status and message that item alone would have produced.

Does massUpdate run one query per id?. 
No. It runs one SELECT to check the ids and one UPDATE... WHERE id IN (...), whatever the number of ids. When beforeUpdate returns different data for different ids, it sends one UPDATE per distinct result (since 3.8.0), so a hook that sets two values over 40 ids is two UPDATEs, not 40. Pass bulkMode: 'perItem' if you want the single-row method per item.

What HTTP status does a failed bulk call return?. 
A 400. Each entry in its errors array carries the item's own status, such as 409 for a duplicate or 404 for a missing id.

The nestjs-drizzle-crud changelog, every release since 3.0.0 with what was added, changed, fixed and deprecated, newest first, mirroring CHANGELOG.md.

The nestjs-drizzle-crud changelog lists every release since 3.0.0, newest first, with what each one added, changed, fixed and deprecated. It mirrors the CHANGELOG.md shipped in the npm package, follows Keep a Changelog (https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the package uses Semantic Versioning (https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html): a patch fixes, a minor adds, and only a major breaks the public API.

Read the Changed section before you upgrade. 
Each release's Changed list holds the behaviour or type changes existing code may rely on.
Feature pages describe current behaviour and this page is the history, so if the two disagree,
the feature page wins and the changelog entry is the bug.

The 3.0.x line is PostgreSQL-first. MySQL-specific paths (non-RETURNING restore, ER_DUP_ENTRY mapping, dialect locking) are tracked separately and unchanged in those entries.

3.3.1, 3.4.0, 3.5.0 and 3.5.2 were tagged but never published to npm. Their changes reached npm
in 3.5.1 (3.3.1 to 3.5.0) and 3.6.0 (3.5.2). The unscoped nestjs-drizzle-crud stops at 3.3.0.

Fixes from the 3.8.1 audit (G-01 to G-08). The tenant key check now lets the database compare keys,
so it follows each column's collation, and a malformed key or an ISO date string in a write body is
no longer a 500. No public API or override point changed, and no operation sends more statements
than in 3.8.1.

- The tenant key check, attach and sync leave the key comparison to the database. They join the
keys they were sent, as an inline VALUES list, against the related table in the same scoped
SELECT, so the column's type and collation decide which key matched. A citext or SQLite
NOCASE key of the caller's own tenant in another case is accepted again (3.8.1 refused it with
a 400), and on MySQL a key under a _bin collation that differs from another tenant's only in
case is refused. PostgreSQL text still compares exactly, and a uuid matches in any case. On
MySQL an integer or decimal key is compared in its column's type, so a BIGINT past 2^53 is
matched exactly. attach and sync link each target by its key as stored, so "ann@x.io" and
"Ann@X.io" on a citext column give one link.
- massUpdate and massUpsert load relations and counts inside their transaction when a value
holds a Drizzle sql expression. A load that fails then rolls the write back, so a retry no
longer adds views + 1 twice.
- A RangeError thrown while a statement's values are mapped (a custom type's own check, say) is
no longer reported as "Too many values in one statement". Only the call stack overflow of an
oversized parameter list is.

- A belongs-to key the column's type cannot hold ("nope" for a uuid) is a 400 in massCreate,
massUpdate and massUpsert, and in update inside a caller's transaction. It was a raw
22P02 or 25P02, a 500.
- Every write (create, update, upsert, the mass writes and nested rows) turns an ISO date
string or a number for a date-mode timestamp, date or datetime column into a Date, as
filters already did. It was a 500 TypeError (value.toISOString is not a function). A value
that is not a date, an Invalid Date included, is a 400 that names the column, in a write and in a
filter.
- massUpdate groups SETs by their raw values: a hook that returns null for one id and an
Invalid Date for another no longer gets both into one UPDATE. A Date and its ISO string are
two values, and byte arrays compare by their bytes.
- A massUpdate whose SETs all hold the same sql expression object, as in
`massUpdate(ids, { n: sqln + 1 }), sends one UPDATE` instead of one per id.
- The per-call scope memo ends with the public call that started it. Options a hook kept and passed
to a later call reused the old memo, which grew with each call and resolved a context object
mutated in place to its old tenant.

- The 3.8.1 entry now says the 404 ahead of a refused value holds outside a caller's transaction,
and that a mass write with an SQL value was not safe to retry. The bulk operations page says when
such a write loads its relations and that one shared sql object is one UPDATE.
- The multi-tenancy page says the database compares the keys. The CRUD operations page, the README
and AGENT.md say date strings are parsed on writes.

Fixes from the 3.8.0 audit (D-01 to D-11). Three of them close gaps in tenant isolation: a scope
handed from one service to another, a batch key that differs from another tenant's only in case,
and nested children that skipped the key check. No public API or override point changed.

- Text keys compare exactly in the tenant key check, attach and sync: "US" and "us" are
two keys, as they are two rows on PostgreSQL and SQLite. Before, every key was lowercased, so a
batch holding both could point a row at another tenant's "us" and get a 201 where "us"
alone was a 400. A uuid column still ignores case, and so does MySQL, to follow its default
collations, which match "us" to a stored "US" and cannot hold both as distinct keys.
- On a scoped entity, a nested create checks the belongs-to keys of the rows it writes (a
belongs-to parent, has-many children, new many-to-many targets) against the caller's tenant,
using the nested relation's own relations. A child key to another tenant's row is the same
400 ForeignKeyViolationException as a key to a missing row, and nothing is written. It was a
201. A child key that no nested relation declares is still left to the database's foreign key.
- massSoftDelete and massDelete put deleted_at IS NULL in the WHERE of their write, as the
single-row writes have since 3.8.0. A row soft-deleted between the existence check and the
write is a 404 entry and the batch writes nothing, instead of being stamped again or
hard-deleted. massForceDelete still removes a row in either state.
- massCreate loads relations and counts inside its transaction again. A load that fails
rolls the rows back, so a retry no longer stores them twice. The other mass writes still load
after the commit, where a retry gives the same rows, except for a write whose values hold an SQL
expression (`massUpdate(ids, { views: sqlviews + 1 })), which 3.8.2 loads inside too.
- update of a missing row with a value the database refuses (update(999, { views: "abc" }))
is a 404, as it was before 3.8.0, instead of a 400, outside a caller's transaction. Inside one
(options.transaction`) the failed statement has aborted the transaction on PostgreSQL, so the
answer stays the 400, which is the same for every tenant.

- The per-call scope memo is keyed by service and by the context it was resolved for. Options
handed from one service to another, the natural way for a subclass override to share a
transaction, carried the first service's scope: a service whose scope is null let a scoped
one read every tenant's rows, and a second service scoped by another column stored NULL in
it. Each service still runs its scope function once per call.
- An override of emitEvent or prepareUpdate keeps the guard read ahead of the write, like an
override of a before hook. An emitEvent override saw the before event for another
tenant's id before the 404.
- massUpdate with a beforeUpdate hook that returns NaN for one id and null for another no
longer writes NaN to both, and a Drizzle sql expression as a value (views + 1) works as
it does in update instead of failing with a circular TypeError (a 500).
- The tenant key check sends its SELECTs, one per relation, together instead of one after the
other.

- The multi-tenancy FAQ answered "No" to "Are eager-loaded relations filtered by tenant?", against
the section on the same page. It now says yes, when the related table has the scope columns.
The multi-tenancy and relations-on-writes pages say which nested keys are checked, and the bulk
operations page says when a mass write loads its relations.
- AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and apps/docs/AGENTS.md point at the changelog page where it
lives now, (support)/changelog.mdx.

Performance fixes from the 3.7.1 performance report. Calls return the same rows, in the same
order, with the same errors, in fewer statements and shorter transactions. The one visible
difference is under Changed: a row soft-deleted between the guard read and the write is now a 404
instead of a write. Inside SqlBaseCrudService the six mass writes share one skeleton, and so
do softDelete, restore and delete; no public API, override point or message changed.

- Full-text search takes a column that already is a tsvector, such as a generated, stored
column, and uses it as is instead of wrapping it in to_tsvector, so a GIN index on the column
serves fullTextSearch() and search.mode: "fullText". Before, such a column failed with
function to_tsvector(unknown, tsvector) does not exist. Next to text columns it is
coalesce(col, ''::tsvector); text columns keep the 3.7.2 vector, bare for one column and
coalesced for several. On 200,000 rows a search on the stored column with its index took
0.6 ms, against 600 to 900 ms computing to_tsvector per row without one. The full-text page
shows the index for each shape.
- A docs page, Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/indexes/),
lists the index each query shape needs: lower(col) (or citext, or caseSensitive: true) for
the default case-insensitive equality, the sort columns plus the primary key for cursor pages,
GIN for full-text search, pg_trgm for contains and search, foreign keys and both join
table columns for relations, partial indexes on deleted_at IS NULL, and the tenant column
first. It says when to use withCount: false or the cursor on a large table. The filtering
page now spells out that findOne compares strings with a plain, case-sensitive = while
findAll and count use lower() by default (unchanged; a default change waits for a major),
and the hooks page says where after hooks run: after the commit for a single write, inside
the transaction for a mass write.

- A row soft-deleted between the guard read and the write is no longer written: update and
softDelete only touch a live row, restore only a row in the trash, and delete no longer
hard-deletes a row that was soft-deleted meanwhile (forceDelete still does). Such a call is a
404 instead of a write, a false return or a "Failed to update entity" error, and one whose
row vanished with an expected version is a 404 instead of a 409.

- Keyset pages seek instead of filtering. findByCursor adds a bound on the first sort column
(col <= $1 descending, col = $1 ascending) ahead of the OR expansion, drops the IS NULL
branch for NOT NULL and primary key columns (nullable and relation columns keep it), and on
PostgreSQL compares (a, id) ($1, $2) as one row value when every column is NOT NULL and
sorts the same way. With an index on the sort columns and the primary key, page 9,000 of
200,000 rows went from 24.4 ms to 0.6 ms (created_at descending) and from 50.3 ms to 0.5 ms
(views ascending) on PGlite. A sort column the row already carries is no longer selected a
second time for the cursor. Pages, their order and cursors are unchanged.
- Single-row writes skip the read first. On PostgreSQL and SQLite, update, softDelete,
restore, delete and forceDelete send one statement whose WHERE holds the whole guard
(primary key, tenant scope, expected version, soft delete state) and read the row only when
nothing came back, to answer with the same 404 or 409 as before. The read still runs first
when something a caller can observe sits between it and the write (an overridden before 
hook, validateUpdate or mapUpdateDtoToEntity, or a before event), so hooks and events see
exactly what they saw before, and on MySQL. A missing row is still a 404 ahead of a bad body.
- Mass writes send no savepoint on the happy path when they open their own transaction:
massUpdate, massSoftDelete, massRestore and massDelete take 4 round trips instead of 8
(BEGIN, SELECT, the set statement, COMMIT), massCreate and massUpsert 3 instead of 5.
When the set statement fails, the transaction rolls back and the items are replayed in a fresh
transaction that is rolled back too, so BulkOperationException names the same items with the
same statuses and messages. Inside a caller's transaction, or once a before event handed the
transaction to a subscriber, the savepoints stay, so a failed item does not abort the caller's
PostgreSQL transaction.
- massUpdate sends one UPDATE per distinct SET when beforeUpdate returns different data
per id, instead of one UPDATE and a savepoint pair per id: a hook with two results over 50
ids is 5 round trips instead of 155. Rows still come back in the input order, after hooks run
in that order, and a failure still names every failing id.
- On MySQL, massCreate of rows with auto-increment keys reads the inserted rows back with one
SELECT... WHERE id IN (...) instead of one per row. The inserts stay one per row: MySQL only
reports the first id of a multi-row INSERT, and InnoDB does not promise the others are
consecutive.
- Relation loaders and relation counts split a parent key list that would not fit in one
statement. loadBelongsTo, loadHasMany, loadManyToMany and loadCounts send the keys in
chunks of 64,535 on PostgreSQL and MySQL, 31,766 on SQLite and 90 on Cloudflare D1, one query per
chunk, so a nested page whose level holds 70,000 keys loads in two queries instead of failing
with a 400 (3.7.2) or a 500 (before). Below that, it is one query per relation as before. The
chunk size is the new protected relationChunkSize(db).
- Fewer statements in a few calls. exists(id, options) is one SELECT and no longer loads
options.relations or options.counts it throws away (4 statements to 1 with two relations and
a count); they are still checked against the allowlists. A nested create skips the "already
linked?" read for its many-to-many ids. attach, sync and detach read the row once and load
the relation onto it, instead of reading it before and after (8, 9 and 6 round trips to 7, 8 and
5). A mass write that opened its own transaction loads options.relations and options.counts
after it commits, so it holds its row locks for less time; with a count filter, or in a caller's
transaction, they still load inside. The returned rows are the same.
- A scope function runs once per call instead of once per statement and relation: 5 times for
a findAll with three relations and a count, 7 for a massUpdate, now 1 each.
Fixes from the 3.7.1 audit. The batch limit now counts the statement the database receives.

Changed. - The bound parameter limit is checked per statement, against the database's own limit:
65,535 on PostgreSQL and MySQL, 32,766 on SQLite and libSQL, 100 on Cloudflare D1. The service
counts the parameters of every statement as Drizzle builds it, so two OR'd IN lists, the
version checks of a massUpdate with expectedVersions, the children of a nested create and
the targets of attach and sync all count, and a statement past the limit is a 400 that
names its count and the limit before it runs. Before, each input list was checked against
60,000 on its own: some of those calls still ended in a 500, a massCreate that would have fit
on PostgreSQL was refused (it counted four extra values per row), and on SQLite the cap sat
above the database's limit. The message changes from "Too many values in one call (n); the
limit is 60000" to "Too many values in one statement: n bound parameters, and PostgreSQL takes
at most 65535". bindLimit(db) is protected, for a server built with another limit.
MAX_BATCH_PARAMETERS, assertBatchSize and insertParameters stay for compatibility but are
deprecated and no longer used.
- On a scoped entity, create, update, upsert and the mass writes check every belongs-to key
they set against the caller's tenant when the related table has the scope columns, the way
attach checks its targets: one SELECT per relation for the whole call. A key to another
tenant's row is the same 400 ForeignKeyViolationException as a key to a missing row, so the
answer no longer tells them apart, and a missing row is refused even without a database
foreign key. Calls with skipScope: true and related tables without the scope columns are
not checked.
- On SQLite, contains, startsWith and endsWith with sql.caseSensitive: true compile to
GLOB and match case exactly. They used LIKE, which ignores ASCII case. The default
(case-insensitive) and the like operator are unchanged.
- On MySQL, connection.idleTimeout also sets mysql2's maxIdle to one below the pool size.
mysql2 only reaps idle connections when maxIdle is below connectionLimit, so the timeout
had no effect before.
- forRootAsync with more than one of useFactory, useClass and useExisting throws at
startup and names them. Before, useFactory won and the class was ignored.

they set against the caller's tenant when the related table has the scope columns, the way
attach checks its targets: one SELECT per relation for the whole call. A key to another

foreign key. Calls with skipScope: true and related tables without the scope columns are

GLOB and match case exactly. They used LIKE, which ignores ASCII case. The default

mysql2 only reaps idle connections when maxIdle is below connectionLimit, so the timeout
had no effect before.

startup and names them. Before, useFactory won and the class was ignored.

- On SQLite, a STRICT table refusing a value of the wrong type (extended code 3091, which
libSQL reports as UNKNOWN_SQLITE_ERROR_3091) and SQLITE_MISMATCH ("abc" for an
INTEGER PRIMARY KEY) are a 400 ValidationFailedException, not a 500. The dialect contract
checks the same mapping on every dialect.
- Filters inside options.counts get the same 32 level depth cap as a findAll filter. A very
deep one was a 500 (stack overflow).
- The filter depth check no longer overflows the call stack on an IN list of a few hundred
thousand items.
- A batch so large that Drizzle's own SQL builder overflows the call stack is the same 400 as
any other statement past the limit.
- Full-text search over several columns no longer drops rows that have NULL in one of them.
The vector was to_tsvector(cfg, a) to_tsvector(cfg, b), and x NULL is NULL, so
such a row never matched, in fullTextSearch() and in search.mode: "fullText" alike. Each
column is now wrapped in coalesce(column, '') when there is more than one. A GIN index on the
old multi-column expression no longer matches the query; recreate it with the coalesce (the
full-text search page has the exact CREATE INDEX). A single column is unchanged.

- AGENTS.md names the package @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud, and says that PGlite, the engine
of the unit and e2e specs, returns no rows above 32,767 bound parameters.

Fixed. - The error for an upsert on a scoped entity on MySQL now reads "upsert on a scoped entity needs
PostgreSQL or SQLite". It said PostgreSQL only, though SQLite supports a scoped upsert since 3.7.0.
-?fields= paths named __proto__, constructor or prototype are treated as plain names.
Before, they reached the select tree's object internals (CodeQL js/remote-property-injection).

- The error for an upsert on a scoped entity on MySQL now reads "upsert on a scoped entity needs
PostgreSQL or SQLite". It said PostgreSQL only, though SQLite supports a scoped upsert since 3.7.0.
-?fields= paths named __proto__, constructor or prototype are treated as plain names.
Before, they reached the select tree's object internals (CodeQL js/remote-property-injection).
SQLite support, MySQL connections built for you, and full-text search that works like findAll.

Added. - dialect: "sqlite" for SQLite, libSQL (Turso) and Cloudflare D1. Pass the Drizzle instance as
db. Writes use RETURNING, upsert uses ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE with the tenant guard, and
keyset pages follow SQLite's NULL order. LIKE gets ESCAPE '\', so %, _ and \ in a
search term match literally. Constraint errors map like the other dialects: UNIQUE 409,
FOREIGN KEY 400 on a write and 409 on a delete, NOT NULL and CHECK 400. Full-text search,
row locks and the array and JSON operators are a 400.
- On Cloudflare D1 and synchronous SQLite drivers (better-sqlite3, bun:sqlite, sql.js), the calls
that need an interactive transaction (mass writes, nested creates, attach, detach, sync)
throw a TransactionException that says why, before any statement runs. TransactionException
is no longer deprecated.
- connectionString works with dialect: "mysql": the module builds a mysql2 pool, wraps it
with drizzle-orm/mysql2 and ends it on shutdown. mysql2 is a new optional peer, loaded only
on that path.
- connection: { poolSize, idleTimeout, ssl } for the connection the module builds from
connectionString, on PostgreSQL (postgres-js) and MySQL (mysql2).
- forRootAsync takes useClass and useExisting, with a class that implements
DrizzleCrudOptionsFactory (createDrizzleCrudOptions()), next to useFactory.
- fullTextSearch() takes options.filters, and honours options.relations, options.select
and options.counts, the same as findAll. Before, they were ignored.
- language (the text search configuration, default "english") and queryMode ("plain", the
default, or "websearch" for websearch_to_tsquery) on fullTextSearch() options and on
search with mode: "fullText". A language that is not a plain identifier is a 400.
- New types: DrizzleConnectionOptions, DrizzleCrudAsyncOptions, DrizzleCrudOptionsFactory,
FullTextOptions, FullTextQueryMode and FullTextSearchOptions.

- New types: DrizzleConnectionOptions, DrizzleCrudAsyncOptions, DrizzleCrudOptionsFactory,

- MySQL: lock and forNoKeyUpdate add FOR UPDATE or FOR SHARE (forNoKeyUpdate becomes
FOR UPDATE). They used to be accepted and silently ignored.
- MySQL strict mode data errors (a missing required value, a value too long, out of range, of
the wrong type, a bad date, a failed check) are a 400 that names the column, instead of a 500.

- The default sql.useReturning is true for every dialect except MySQL, so SQLite gets it.
PostgreSQL and MySQL keep the values they had.

Fixes from the second audit. The first one is a security fix: upgrade if you use scope.

Security. - Related tables now follow the tenant scope. Loaded relations, the joins behind relation columns,
relation filters (some, none, every and nested columns) and counts only see related rows
of the caller's tenant when the related table has the scope columns. Before, a row pointing at
another tenant's row (a plain foreign key allows it) loaded that row, and a filter on it
answered questions about it.

Added. - createCrudController takes validation, the validator options for the bulk bodies. Pass the
same options as your global ValidationPipe.

Fixed. - PATCH /bulk validates data against dto.update, the check a single PATCH already had.
- Route decorators that wrap the handler now run. Before, the factory dropped the wrapped handler.
- Bulk ids are parsed like:id, so a bad id is a 400 before any statement runs.
- A filter nested deeper than 32 objects is a 400. A thousand nested not groups used to
overflow the stack and answer with a 500.
- A batch past the bound-parameter limit (60,000 values: rows times columns for massCreate and
massUpsert, ids for the id based methods, values in an IN filter) is a 400 that names the
limit, instead of a driver protocol error and a 500.
- A missing required value (23502) is a 400 that names the column.
- MySQL ER_DUP_ENTRY is a 409, and foreign key errors are a 400 on a write and a 409 on a delete.
- upsert no longer updates a row in the trash: the conflict writes nothing and is a 404.
- With useReturning: false, a scoped upsert no longer reads back another tenant's row.
- restore on a live row is a 404 before any hook or event runs. It used to succeed and bump
updated_at and the version.
-?relation[some]= and [none]= with no column need the relation, or one of its columns, in
filterableColumns.
- A nested child row cannot set its own generated primary key.

Fixed. - softDelete, restore, massSoftDelete and massRestore on an entity without soft delete,
and full-text search on MySQL (fullTextSearch() or search.mode: "fullText"), now throw a
BadRequestException. They were a plain Error, which reached the client as a 500.
- options.counts now applies the tenant scope to the related rows it counts, when the related
table has the scope column. Before, a parent's count included rows of other tenants.

Changed. - sortOrder now defaults to "asc" in findAll and findByCursor, so a bare
sortBy: "name" sorts the same way as?sortBy=name over HTTP. Pass sortOrder: "desc" to
keep the old order.

The MCP server runs with npx -p @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud nestjs-drizzle-crud-mcp.
