chunks.t:
The P2 features from the November 2026 audit (M10 to M18). Each one is covered by specs that run real
SQL against PGlite (test/pglite.integration.spec.ts), and the controller factory, scoping,
locking, OpenAPI document, counts and quantified filters also run over real HTTP in the example
app.

- Relations on writes. create, update, upsert, restore and every mass write take
options.relations and options.counts and return the rows with them loaded, through the same
batched loaders as a read: one query per relation for the whole batch. Ten rows from massCreate
with relations: ['author'] cost one INSERT and one SELECT.
- Nested create. With a relation listed in the new writableRelations allowlist, a create body
can carry it: an array for a has-many (one multi-row INSERT), an object for a belongs-to
(inserted first, its key set on the row), and ids or objects for a many-to-many (new targets in
one INSERT, links in one more). Everything runs in one transaction and needs RETURNING.
- attach, detach and sync for many-to-many relations: attach(id, 'tags', [1, 2]). Set
based (a fixed number of statements whatever the number of ids), already-linked ids are skipped,
and an unknown or soft-deleted target is a 400 with a 404 entry per id. Each returns the row with
the relation loaded.
- createCrudController(Service, options), a controller factory. It registers list (offset,
or keyset with?cursor=), trash, get, create, update, delete, soft delete, restore and four bulk
routes, all through parseQuery. The:id param is parsed from the primary key column
(ParseIntPipe for an integer, ParseUUIDPipe for a uuid) unless idType says otherwise. Routes can
be turned on or off one by one and take their own decorators, so guards and roles fit in. Bulk
routes are off by default. service.parseId(raw) and service.idKind() are public.
- OpenAPI for list queries. @ApiCrudQuery(source) documents page, limit, sortBy,
sortOrder, cursor, count, withCount, search, fields, with, counts, the trash flags
and one parameter per filterable column with its type. @ApiCrudList(source) adds the page
envelope with a row schema built from the table. @nestjs/swagger is an optional peer, loaded
only when one of these decorators runs.
- Tenant and ownership scoping. scope: (ctx) = ({ tenant_id: ctx.tenantId }) (or a fixed
object) is ANDed into every read, count, cursor page, countBy, fullTextSearch, relation count,
write, bulk write, upsert, soft delete, restore, force delete and attach/detach/sync, and written
onto every row a create or upsert inserts (and onto nested child rows that have the column).
Another tenant's id is a 404 everywhere. The context comes from options.context or from
CrudContext.run(...) / CrudContext.middleware(...), which keep it in AsyncLocalStorage for
the request. A missing context value fails closed with MissingScopeException (403); a resolver
that returns null, or skipScope: true, runs unscoped on purpose.
- Module-level events. hooks.enableGlobalHooks: true now does what it says: every service
raises a before and an after event on the injectable CrudEventBus for each write, bulk and upsert
included. Subscribe with hooks.subscribers in forRoot or by injecting the bus. A bulk call
raises one event with bulk: true and every id, so audit trails and cache busting stay set based.
A before listener that throws stops the write; an after listener that throws inside a transaction
rolls it back. skipEvents: true opts a call out.
- Optimistic locking. versionColumn: 'version' starts rows at 1 and adds one on every update,
soft delete, restore, upsert conflict and bulk write. An update, soft delete, restore or delete
that names a stale version (options.expectedVersion, or the version key in an update body) is a
409 StaleVersionException. Mass writes take expectedVersions: { [id]: version } and report a
409 entry per stale id.
- Relation counts and grouped counts. options.counts: ['posts'] (or { posts: { status:
'published' } }) puts _count: { posts: 3 } on every row of find, findOne, findAll,
findByCursor and the writes above, with one GROUP BY query per relation for the whole result.
Soft-deleted related rows are not counted. countBy(column, filters) returns [{ value, count }],
largest group first, for a column of the table or of a top-level belongs-to.
- withCount: false on findAll (and?withCount=false in the parser) skips the COUNT( ).
The envelope then has total: null and a hasMore flag, from fetching one row past the page.
- Deeper relation filters. A relation filter can go on through the related table's own
relations at any depth: { state: { country: { code: 'IN' } } }, or?state[country][code]=IN.
Below the first joined belongs-to, each level is an EXISTS subquery. Collections take some,
none and every ({ posts: { none: { status: 'draft' } } }), compiled to IN / NOT EXISTS
subqueries that never multiply rows, inside or / and / not groups and in count.
- New exports: createCrudController, CrudContext, CrudEventBus, ApiCrudQuery,
ApiCrudList, MissingScopeException, StaleVersionException, and the types
CrudControllerOptions, CrudControllerInstance, CrudRouteName, CrudRouteOptions,
CrudEvent, CrudEventPhase, CrudSubscriber, CrudWriteOperation, CrudScope,
CrudScopeValues, CrudContextValue, CollectionFilter, CollectionQuantifier, CountByRow,
CrudPage, UncountedCrudPage, RelationCounts, ApiCrudSource and ApiCrudQueryOptions.
New config keys: scope, versionColumn, events, writableRelations. New options: counts,
context, skipScope, skipEvents, expectedVersion, expectedVersions, and
PaginationOptions.withCount.
These change behaviour or types that existing code may rely on. Check each one before upgrading.

- findAll is overloaded on withCount. With a literal withCount: false it returns
UncountedCrudPage (total: null), without one CrudPage (total: number), and with a
withCount typed as boolean (which ParsedCrudQuery.pagination is) total is
number null. Code that passes q.pagination from parseQuery straight to findAll and then
does arithmetic on total needs a total!== null check. The runtime result is unchanged unless
withCount: false is passed.
- withCount and counts are reserved query parameters. The parser no longer treats them as
filters. A column with one of those names can still be filtered from code.
- Writes read options.relations and options.counts. They used to be ignored on create,
update, upsert and the mass writes. They are now checked against the allowlists (with
select and search) before anything is written, and loaded onto the result.
- A relation filter can name a relation of the related table, and a collection filter whose
keys are all some, none or every is a quantifier. Both used to be a 400 ("Unknown filter
column"). A related table that really has a column called some, none or every keeps the old
meaning.
- DRIZZLE_CRUD_CONFIG.hooks carries only enableGlobalHooks (a boolean); subscribers stay
on the raw config.

- hooks.enableGlobalHooks did nothing (BUG-21). It now wires the module's CrudEventBus into
every service.
- Nothing new. hooks.enableGlobalHooks, deprecated as a no-op in 3.3.1, is no longer deprecated.

The P1 features from the November 2026 audit. Every one is covered by specs that run real SQL
against PGlite (test/pglite.integration.spec.ts) and by e2e specs over real HTTP in the example
app.

- A query string parser. service.parseQuery(query) and the standalone parseCrudQuery(query,
table, options) turn?age[gte]=18&status=active&region[name]=Asia&or[0][code]=IN&sortBy=-name&page=2&limit=20&fields=id,name&with=region&search=jo
into { filters, pagination, options, isCursor }. Values are coerced by Drizzle column type:
integers and other numbers to number, bigint to bigint, booleans, dates to Date (an
invalid one is a 400), numeric checked and kept as an exact string, and text, uuid and enum left
as strings. An unknown column, relation, operator, sort column, fields entry or with path is a
400. It reads both Express 5's flat age[gte] keys and qs nested objects.
- Per-entity allowlists. filterableColumns, sortableColumns, selectableColumns,
searchableColumns and loadableRelations limit what a caller may filter, sort, select, search
and eager-load; writableColumns limits what create, update and upsert may write. Anything
outside a set list is a 400, in the service and in the parser. Unset lists allow everything.
skipAllowlists: true skips them for a trusted call, and findOne where keys are not checked.
- Trash view and purge. withDeleted: true and onlyDeleted: true work on every read (find,
findOne, findAll, findByCursor, count, exists, fullTextSearch). forceDelete(id) and
massForceDelete(ids) hard-delete rows whether they are soft-deleted or not.
- Upsert. upsert(dto, { conflictTarget, update }) and massUpsert(rows,...) insert or update
in one statement: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on Postgres, ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE on MySQL. A clash
on another unique key is a 409, bad input a 400, and the same key twice in one massUpsert
(21000) a 400.
- and, or and not filter groups. { or: [{ status: 'a' }, { author: { name: 'Bob' } }],
not: { tags: { name: 'x' } } }. Groups nest, hold column, relation and collection filters, work
inside a relation filter, and apply to count.
- New filter operators. notIn, between, startsWith, endsWith and contains (escaped,
case-insensitive unless sql.caseSensitive is on), iStartsWith, iEndsWith and iContains
(always case-insensitive), and on PostgreSQL arrayContains, arrayOverlaps and jsonContains.
A pattern operator on a non-text column, an array operator on a non-array column, or a PostgreSQL
only operator on MySQL is a 400.
- Keyset pagination. findByCursor(filters, { cursor, limit, sortBy, count }, options) returns
{ data, limit, nextCursor, total? }. The cursor is base64url JSON of the last row's sort values
plus the primary key, so pages stay stable under inserts and, with an index on the sort columns
(since 3.8.0), deep pages cost the same as the
first. It works with every sort, filter, relation and select, keeps timestamp microseconds and
follows the database's NULL ordering. The count only runs with count: true. A cursor that is not
valid, or was made for another sort, is a 400.
- Multi-column and relation sorts from the caller. sortBy takes a list: ['region.name',
'-name'] or [{ column, order }], and a comma separated string means the same. A dotted entry
sorts by a top-level belongs-to column, joined for the data query only. A collection column is a
400.
- bulkMode: 'perItem' keeps the 3.3 behaviour of one single-row call per item, in its own
savepoint.
- New exports: parseCrudQuery, and the types CrudFilter, FilterGroup, FilterOperators,
FilterOperator, FilterScalar, ColumnFilter, SortInput, CursorPaginationOptions,
CursorPage, CrudAllowlists, UpsertOptions, BulkMode, ParseCrudQueryOptions and
ParsedCrudQuery. The Drizzle helpers between, not and notInArray are re-exported.
These change behaviour that existing code may rely on. Check each one before upgrading.

- Mass writes are set-based. massUpdate, massSoftDelete, massRestore and massDelete cost
one SELECT that checks every id plus one UPDATE or DELETE... WHERE id IN (...), and
massCreate one multi-row INSERT, instead of one or two queries per id. The
BulkOperationException body is unchanged: when the statement fails, the batch is replayed item
by item inside a savepoint that is rolled back, only to name the failing items. Hooks still run
once per item, but the after hooks now run once the whole set is written instead of after each
item. Duplicate ids are written once. Pass bulkMode: 'perItem' for the old behaviour.
- Create and update ignore the columns the package manages. Without writableColumns, the soft
delete column is dropped from a create or update body, and the primary key and the createdAt
column from an update body. An update whose only key was one of these is now a 400 ("there are no
columns to update"). To write them on purpose, list them in writableColumns.
- PaginationOptions.sortBy is SortInput (string Array<string SortColumn ). Code that
passes a string is unaffected; code that reads sortBy back as a string needs a narrowing
check.
- between is an operator now. { col: { between: [a, b] } } used to be a 400 ("Unknown filter
operator").
- buildOrderBy takes a SortInput, and buildFilterConditions and buildCollectionFilter take
an optional options argument, for subclasses that call them.

- Mass operations cost a fixed number of queries (BUG-16). massUpdate over 10 ids was 20
queries; it is now 2.
- The soft delete guide's trash and purge recipes work (BUG-17). They used raw Drizzle because
findAll({ deleted_at: { isNotNull: true } }) always returned nothing; the guide now uses
onlyDeleted and forceDelete.

Fixes from the November 2026 audit. Every fix below is proven by a spec that runs real SQL against
PGlite (test/pglite.integration.spec.ts) and failed before the change.

- String filters on integer, uuid and enum columns no longer return a 500. Query strings send
every value as text, and with the default caseSensitive: false a filter such as
{ author_id: '1' } became lower(author_id), which Postgres rejects. lower() now only wraps
text, varchar and char columns; every other column compares with = and Postgres casts the value.
Relation and collection filters get the same fix.
- Date strings work on date and timestamp columns. { publishedAt: { gt: '2024-01-01' } } used
to crash inside the driver (value.toISOString is not a function). The string is now turned into
a Date; a value that is not a date is a 400.
- A soft-deleted belongs-to parent is no longer returned. The LEFT JOIN for an eager load or a
relation filter now carries deleted_at IS NULL in its ON clause, so the parent comes back as
null and { author: { name: 'Bob' } } does not match a deleted author.
- findOne can no longer hand back an arbitrary row. findOne({ email: undefined }) used to run
LIMIT 1 with no condition and return the first row in the table. It is now a 400, as is a key
that is not a column. null now means IS NULL instead of being skipped. An operator object works
as it does in findAll.
- A soft-delete or timestamp column the table does not have is caught at startup. With
camelCase keys (deletedAt: timestamp('deleted_at')) the default config used to break every read
with a SQL syntax error, and updatedAt silently never moved. The service now throws when it is
built, naming the key to use: softDelete.column is "deleted_at", but the table has no column
under that key. The column "deleted_at" is declared under the key "deletedAt"; set
softDelete.column to "deletedAt".
- One bad item in a bulk call no longer fails every item after it. Each item now runs in its own
savepoint, so massCreate([ok, duplicate, ok, ok]) reports the duplicate alone instead of two more
25P02 "current transaction is aborted" errors. The whole call still rolls back. The items still
run one query (or two) at a time; set-based bulk writes are planned separately.
- Bulk errors reach the HTTP response. BulkOperationException now answers with
{ statusCode, error, message, errors: [{ index id, status, message }] }, one entry per failed
item with the status that item alone would have produced. An error that is not an HTTP exception
shows as status: 500 with a generic message, so SQL never leaks.
- { isNull: false } means IS NOT NULL. The value used to be ignored. isNull and isNotNull
also accept the strings "true" and "false"; anything else is a 400.
- Filters the package does not understand are rejected instead of dropped. A new eq operator
is supported, a Date value is an equality match instead of an empty operator object, and an
unknown column, relation column or operator is a 400. Each of these used to return every row.
- Bad input is a 400 on reads too. Postgres 22P02 (wrong type, unknown enum label), 22007 and
22008 (bad dates) now map to ValidationFailedException on every path, including find,
findAll, count and fullTextSearch. fullTextSearch checks its column names (an unknown one
used to be a SQL syntax error), and update with nothing to set is a 400 instead of a raw
"No values to set".
- fullTextSearch always paginates. Without a pagination argument it returned every match while
the envelope said limit: 20. The resolved page and limit now always apply, and the data and count
queries run together.
- A partial pagination override keeps the other half. pagination: { defaultLimit: 5 } used to
replace the whole object, leaving maxLimit undefined and the query with no limit at all.
softDelete, timestamps, pagination and sql now merge one level deep at every config layer:
forRoot defaults, @CrudService, forFeature and the service constructor.
- Search and the ilike operator emit LIKE on MySQL, which has no ILIKE. MySQL's default
collations already compare case-insensitively.
- Pages are stable. The primary key is now always the last ORDER BY column, so rows that tie on
the sort columns, or a list with no sort at all, can no longer repeat or skip between pages.
- A row lock works with an eager belongs-to. Locks are now FOR UPDATE OF <base table (and the
same for share and no key update). Postgres used to refuse with FOR UPDATE cannot be applied
to the nullable side of an outer join.
- Nested collections key on their own table. A nested has-many or many-to-many used the root
service's primaryKey as its default parentKey, so a root keyed on uid loaded
author.posts as []. A nested level now defaults to its host table's own primary key column.
- Types in public signatures are exported. PaginationOptions, OperationOptions,
SqlSearchOptions, SqlSearchMode and BulkOperationResult come from the package root, along
with the new CrudFeatureConfig and BulkOperationItemError.
- CrudFeature.config is typed as CrudFeatureConfig instead of Record<string, any, so a typo in
a key no longer compiles.

These fixes change behaviour that existing code may rely on. Check each one before upgrading.
- An unknown filter key is a 400. findAll and count used to drop keys that were not columns,
so passing a whole query DTO through worked even with page or sortBy in it. Strip non-filter
fields first. The same goes for an unknown column inside a relation or collection filter, and for
an unknown operator. null and undefined values are still skipped.
- findOne with no usable condition, or an unknown key, is a 400. It used to return the first
row in the table.
- findOne({ col: null }) matches IS NULL. It used to skip the key.
- A configured soft-delete or timestamp key the table lacks stops the app at startup. This
includes the project defaults: with defaults.timestamps on (the default), every table needs
created_at and updated_at keys, or the entity must set its own keys or turn timestamps off
with timestamps: undefined. Before, a missing timestamp key was silently ignored.
- Every findAll and fullTextSearch ends with ORDER BY <primary key ASC. A list with no
sort configured used to come back in whatever order Postgres chose; it now comes back by primary
key.
- update(id, {}) is a 400, also when timestamps are on. It used to bump updated_at alone.
- { isNull: false } returns the non-null rows instead of the null ones.
- BulkOperationException has a different response body. message is unchanged; errors is
new. The errors property on the exception still holds the original errors.
- Read errors from bad input are 400s. find('abc') on an integer key used to be a 500.
- Row locks now carry OF <table. A subclass that relied on locking joined rows must take that
lock itself.

- sql.jsonSupport, sql.enableFullTextSearch, hooks.enableGlobalHooks and primaryKeyType.
Nothing reads them, so they have no effect. They are still accepted and will be removed in the
next major version. primaryKeyType is now optional. The docs no longer claim that jsonSupport
enables JSON handling or that enableFullTextSearch gates fullTextSearch().
- DatabaseConnectionException and TransactionException. Nothing in the package throws them.

Added. - Has-many, many-to-many and nested relations, all eager loaded without N+1. Declare
relations: { states: { table: states, type: 'hasMany', foreignKey: 'country_id' } } and pass
options.relations: ['states'] to find, findOne or findAll. Each has-many relation costs
exactly one extra query for the whole result set (WHERE country_id IN (...)), no matter how many
parent rows come back, and the relations run concurrently. A page of 50 countries with their
states is 3 queries: data, count, children. A parent with no children gets [], never undefined.
- Many-to-many through a join table. Declare
{ table: tags, type: 'manyToMany', through: countryTags, throughLocalKey: 'country_id', throughForeignKey: 'tag_id' }
and the collection loads in one batched query per relation
(SELECT... FROM country_tags JOIN tags... WHERE country_id IN (...)). The join-table key is
used to group the rows and stripped before they are returned.
- Nested relations, any depth, with a dotted path. Put a relations map on a relation and
address it with options.relations: ['states', 'states.cities'] or ['state.country']. Each
nesting level costs one more batched query for the whole level, so a page of 50 countries with
their states and every state's cities is 4 queries. Asking only for state.country pulls in
state automatically.
- orderBy on a collection relation. { type: 'hasMany', foreignKey: 'country_id', orderBy: [{ column: 'name', order: 'asc' }] }
orders the children in SQL. An unknown column is warned about and skipped, as with defaultSort.
- Collections are never joined. Filtering by a child column
(findAll({ states: { name: 'Kerala' } }), findAll({ tags: { name: 'himalayan' } })) compiles to
countries.id IN (SELECT... WHERE...), so parent rows are never duplicated and total and
pagination stay correct. Belongs-to relations keep using a LEFT JOIN.
- options.select now narrows relation columns with a dotted path, at any depth. 
select: ['id', 'name', 'region.code', 'states.cities.name'] projects only those columns, for the
base table, a joined belongs-to relation and a batched collection alike. Listing only relation
columns leaves the parent row complete. The parent key, the child foreign key and any key a nested
level needs are added back automatically, because the grouping needs them.
- An MCP server ships with the package. npx nestjs-drizzle-crud-mcp serves the package docs
(AGENT.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md) to any MCP client through three tools: list_docs,
get_doc and search_docs. It speaks JSON-RPC over stdio, still has zero dependencies, and works
with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Zed and Cline.
- AGENTS.template.md for every agent that is not Claude Code. It carries the same pointer to
AGENT.md and lists the filename each tool reads. CLAUDE.template.md is unchanged.
- Exported the RelationType ('belongsTo' 'hasMany' 'manyToMany'), RelationNode and
SelectTree types.

- Has-many, many-to-many and nested relations, all eager loaded without N+1. Declare
relations: { states: { table: states, type: 'hasMany', foreignKey: 'country_id' } } and pass
options.relations: ['states'] to find, findOne or findAll. Each has-many relation costs
exactly one extra query for the whole result set (WHERE country_id IN (...)), no matter how many
parent rows come back, and the relations run concurrently. A page of 50 countries with their
states is 3 queries: data, count, children. A parent with no children gets [], never undefined.
- Many-to-many through a join table. Declare
{ table: tags, type: 'manyToMany', through: countryTags, throughLocalKey: 'country_id', throughForeignKey: 'tag_id' }
and the collection loads in one batched query per relation
(SELECT... FROM country_tags JOIN tags... WHERE country_id IN (...)). The join-table key is
used to group the rows and stripped before they are returned.
- Nested relations, any depth, with a dotted path. Put a relations map on a relation and
address it with options.relations: ['states', 'states.cities'] or ['state.country']. Each
nesting level costs one more batched query for the whole level, so a page of 50 countries with
their states and every state's cities is 4 queries. Asking only for state.country pulls in
state automatically.
- orderBy on a collection relation. { type: 'hasMany', foreignKey: 'country_id', orderBy: [{ column: 'name', order: 'asc' }] }

(findAll({ states: { name: 'Kerala' } }), findAll({ tags: { name: 'himalayan' } })) compiles to
countries.id IN (SELECT... WHERE...), so parent rows are never duplicated and total and
pagination stay correct. Belongs-to relations keep using a LEFT JOIN.

select: ['id', 'name', 'region.code', 'states.cities.name'] projects only those columns, for the
base table, a joined belongs-to relation and a batched collection alike. Listing only relation
columns leaves the parent row complete. The parent key, the child foreign key and any key a nested
level needs are added back automatically, because the grouping needs them.

has-many requires foreignKey, many-to-many requires through, throughLocalKey and
throughForeignKey. Nested relations are validated too, and the message carries the full path

which read as bad data rather than bad config.

belongs-to configs are unaffected.

Found while probing the package over real HTTP from the drizzle-pkg-demo consumer
(scripts/probe.sh). PostgreSQL-first. Verified by 56 jest specs + 56 HTTP e2e assertions.

- Bad client input on create/update now maps to 400, not a raw 500. A value that is too
long for its column (Postgres 22001), fails a CHECK constraint (23514), or is numerically
out of range (22003) previously surfaced as an unhandled DrizzleQueryError → 500 Internal
Server Error. These are now translated to ValidationFailedException (400), mirroring the
existing unique-violation → 409 mapping. NOT-NULL/FK violations are intentionally left to bubble
(they usually indicate a programming/config error, not a recoverable bad value).

Correctness fix found while validating the package from a fresh NestJS consumer
(see drizzle-pkg-demo). PostgreSQL-first. Verified by 53 jest specs + 47 HTTP e2e assertions.

- Case-insensitive string filters are now EXACT, not wildcard patterns. A plain string
value in a findAll/count filter (e.g. { name: "foo" }) is documented as a
case-insensitive exact match, but compiled to ilike(column, value). So a value containing
%, _ or \ was silently treated as a LIKE pattern and returned non-matching rows
(e.g. { title: "a_b" } matched "aXb"; { title: "a%" } matched everything). It now compiles
to lower(column) = lower(value), so those characters are treated as literal data. The explicit
{ like } / { ilike } operators are unchanged for intentional pattern matching.

Residual-edge hardening found by an end-to-end HTTP probe of 3.0.1 (all LOW severity;
no behavior change to the happy path). Verified by 35 HTTP assertions on Neon + 49 jest specs.

- fullTextSearch now returns the same envelope as findAll, { data, total, page, limit }
instead of { data, total }. page/limit are the resolved (clamped) values; the query is
still only constrained when the caller passes pagination. Callers paginating search results
can now read back the page/limit they got.

- Invalid sortOrder now fails fast (400).?sortOrder=<anything but asc/desc previously
fell through to ascending silently; it now throws BadRequestException, mirroring the
unknown-sortBy check added in 3.0.1.
- Non-finite numeric filter operands return 400, not 500. A { gt: NaN } / { lte: Infinity }
operand on gt/gte/lt/lte (e.g. from an unguarded Number('abc') in a controller) reached
SQL and surfaced as an opaque DatabaseException (500). It is now rejected as
BadRequestException. Non-number operands (dates, strings) are unaffected.

Correctness pass: typed exceptions now map to real HTTP status codes, plus several read-path fixes.
(PostgreSQL-first.)

Fixed. - Exceptions extend HttpException so Nest maps them automatically:
EntityNotFoundException → 404, DuplicateEntityException → 409,
ValidationFailedException / BulkOperationException → 400,
Database / TransactionException → 500. Previously every error surfaced as a generic 500.
- Duplicate-key translation. A Postgres unique violation (SQLSTATE 23505, on either
err.code or the Drizzle-wrapped err.cause.code) is converted to DuplicateEntityException
(409), parsing the offending field/value from the driver detail.
- fullTextSearch excludes soft-deleted rows (added the IS NULL guard on the soft-delete
column to both the data and count queries, matching findAll/count).
- Pagination clamping. page < 1, limit <= 0, and limit maxLimit are clamped via a shared
resolvePagination helper. No more negative OFFSET or LIMIT 0.
- Unknown sort column fails fast. A caller-supplied sortBy not on the table throws
BadRequestException; an unknown column in a configured defaultSort is warned and skipped.
- restore() returns the restored row on the Postgres RETURNING path (no longer re-find()s,
which would have excluded the just-restored row via the soft-delete filter).

The release notes above cover the package. This list covers the docs pages themselves: every recent commit that changed one, newest first, read from git when the site was built.

Which versioning scheme does nestjs-drizzle-crud follow?. 
Semantic Versioning. A patch release fixes behaviour, a minor release adds features, and removing or renaming anything exported from the package root needs a major release.

When are deprecated options removed?. 
In the next major version. Deprecated settings such as primaryKeyType, sql.jsonSupport and sql.enableFullTextSearch still compile in 3.x but have no effect.

Which versions get security fixes?. 
The 3.x line. Versions before 3.0 do not, according to the security policy in the repository.

Where does this changelog come from?. 
It is a copy of CHANGELOG.md in the package, which is the single record of release history. The npm tarball ships the same file.

chunks.p: Select columns with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: Select columns with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
Select columns in NestJS with Drizzle: pass options.select to return only the columns you need, and use dotted paths to narrow eager-loaded relations.

To select columns with Drizzle in NestJS, pass options.select with the column names you want, and the query stops being SELECT. It works on find, findOne, findAll and findByCursor. A dotted entry such as 'region.code' narrows an eager-loaded relation, at any depth. Leave select out and every column comes back, which is the default.

Names are table keys. 
Each entry is the key in your Drizzle table object, not the SQL column name. The examples use a countries table with a belongs-to region and a has-many states, served by a CountriesService.

chunks.p: Select columns with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: How do I return only some columns?
chunks.t:
List them in select, the third argument of findAll (the second of find and findOne).

Over HTTP, parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing) reads?fields=id,name into options.select.

chunks.p: Select columns with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: Which columns can I ask for?
chunks.t:
Any column of the table, or a dotted path into a relation you also load.

Entry Meaning 
--- --- 
'name' A column on this entity's table. 
'region.code' The code column of the eager-loaded region relation. 
'states.name' The name column of every child in the has-many states relation. 
'states.cities.name' The name column one nesting level down. Paths can be any depth. 

A dotted entry only takes effect when the relation is also listed in options.relations. Without it, nothing is loaded and the entry does nothing.

chunks.p: Select columns with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: What happens with a name that is not a column?
chunks.t:
The service skips it rather than failing, so a typo returns fewer columns instead of an error. Two things make it a 400 instead:

- a selectableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) allowlist that does not list the name,
- parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing), which checks every?fields= entry against the table and its relations.

chunks.p: Select columns with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: How do I narrow a relation?
chunks.t:
Load the relation with relations and name its columns with dotted entries in select.

Why do some columns come back that I did not ask for?. The loader needs some keys to attach children to their parents, so it adds them back:

Key added When 
--- --- 
The parent key on the base row (the configured primaryKey, or the relation's parentKey when set) A has-many or many-to-many relation is loaded, or counted with counts. 
The foreign key on each has-many child row Always, because it maps the child back to its parent. 
The key a nested relation hangs on A relation of a relation is loaded. 

So select: ['name', 'states.name'] still returns id on the country and country_id on each state. The same applies at every nesting level: select: ['name', 'states.name', 'states.cities.name'] keeps states.id too, because the cities load needs it. Everything else you did not ask for is left out of the SQL.

A top-level belongs-to such as region rides along in the main query as a LEFT JOIN, so its key appears only in the ON clause and nothing is added to the base row.

chunks.p: Select columns with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: What if I only list relation columns?
chunks.t:
Then the base row is not narrowed at all.

That way select: ['region.name'] reads as "narrow the region", not "drop every country column".

chunks.p: Select columns with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: When is column selection worth it?
chunks.t:
When the rows are wide or the endpoint is hot.

Case Why it helps 
--- --- 
Wide tables Skipping a large text or jsonb column you do not render is the cheapest win there is. 
List endpoints A table view usually needs three columns out of fifteen. 
Hot paths Less data over the wire and less to hydrate, and a covering index can serve the whole query. 

exists(id) already uses this internally: it selects only the primary key.

Writes return the full row. 
select does not apply to create, update or restore. They return the full row through RETURNING, and relations loaded on a write come back whole.

chunks.p: Select columns with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
Does select work with findByCursor?. 
Yes. findByCursor takes the same options.select as findAll, and the cursor is still built from the sort columns even when you leave them out of select.

Why is the foreign key in my child rows?. 
The loader groups has-many children by their foreign key, so it always selects it. Remove it in your controller or DTO if the client should not see it.

Does a misspelled column name throw an error?. 
Not in the service: it is skipped. It is a 400 when a selectableColumns allowlist is set, or when the name comes through parseQuery as?fields=.

Can I narrow a nested relation?. 
Yes. Use a dotted path of any depth, such as states.cities.name, and load the same path with relations.

The nestjs-drizzle-crud config types, DrizzleCrudConfig for forRoot and SqlCrudConfig per entity, with every option, default and type the methods take.

nestjs-drizzle-crud is configured through two types: DrizzleCrudConfig, the project config you pass to forRoot or forRootAsync, and SqlCrudConfig, the merged per-entity config each service runs on. The module builds the second from the first, then layers @CrudService metadata and the forFeature config on top, so an entity only names the settings it changes.

Column settings take the table key. 
softDelete.column, timestamps.createdAt, timestamps.updatedAt, versionColumn and the keys
of a fixed scope name the key in your Drizzle table object (deletedAt for
deletedAt: timestamp("deleted_at")), not the SQL name. A key the table lacks throws when the
service is built, with the key to use.
The input to DrizzleCrudModule.forRoot(config), and what the forRootAsync factory returns. It holds the connection and the project defaults.

", description: "Optional. Passed to drizzle() when the module builds the connection from connectionString." },
"defaults.softDelete": { type: "boolean", default: "true", description: "Soft delete on the deleted_at column for every entity." },
"defaults.timestamps": { type: "boolean", default: "true", description: "Set created_at and updated_at on every entity." },
"defaults.pagination.defaultLimit": { type: "number", default: "20", description: "Page size when the caller passes no limit." },
"defaults.pagination.maxLimit": { type: "number", default: "100", description: "The largest limit a caller gets. Larger values are clamped." },
"defaults.sortOrder": { type: '"asc" "desc"', description: "Opt-in. Entities without a defaultSort sort by their createdAt column in this direction. Unset, there is no fallback sort." },
"sql.caseSensitive": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Exact string matches and startsWith, endsWith, contains follow this." },
"sql.useReturning": { type: "boolean", default: "dialect!== \"mysql\"", description: "Read written rows back with RETURNING. Forced off on MySQL." },
"sql.jsonSupport": { type: "boolean", description: "Deprecated. Has no effect." },
"sql.enableFullTextSearch": { type: "boolean", description: "Deprecated. Has no effect: full-text search works on PostgreSQL either way." },
"hooks.enableGlobalHooks": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Every service raises a before and an after event per write on the CrudEventBus." },
"hooks.subscribers": { type: "CrudSubscriber[]", description: "Subscribed when the bus is created. Without enableGlobalHooks they never fire, and the module logs a warning." },
}}
/

Provide one of db or connectionString; with neither, startup fails. A connectionString with dialect: "sqlite" also fails, because only PostgreSQL and MySQL connections are built for you.

See NestJS Drizzle module forRoot options (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-root) and Drizzle forRootAsync with ConfigService (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-root-async).

sql.jsonSupport, sql.enableFullTextSearch and primaryKeyType are deprecated and have no effect. They still compile so existing configs keep working, and they will be removed in the next major version. hooks.enableGlobalHooks was deprecated as a no-op in 3.3.1 and works again since 3.5.0: it turns on write events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events).

Each entity's config is the project defaults with three layers on top, each overriding the one before:

Layer Source 
--- --- 
1 forRoot / forRootAsync defaults, after the module fills in its own 
2 @CrudService(config) decorator metadata on the service class 
3 The config object in forFeature 
4 db and table, set by forFeature 

softDelete, timestamps, pagination and sql merge one level deep at every layer, so pagination: { defaultLimit: 5 } keeps the project maxLimit. Every other key, the allowlist arrays included, replaces the value from the layer before. timestamps: undefined turns timestamps off for that entity.

The resolved per-entity config. It extends CrudAllowlists. In forFeature you pass the optional CrudFeatureConfig form of it, and the module fills in dialect, db and table.

An allowlist that is unset allows everything; a request that names something outside a set list is a 400. See Allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists), Multi-tenancy (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy), Optimistic locking (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/optimistic-locking) and Global hooks and write events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events).

forFeature takes an array of CrudFeature, one per entity.

Every key of CrudFeatureConfig is optional. Before 3.3.1, config was typed Record<string, any, so a typo or a half-filled pagination compiled. See forFeature (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-feature).

One entry of relations. RelationsConfig is Record<string, RelationConfig and RelationType is "belongsTo" "hasMany" "manyToMany".

A relation missing its required keys throws when the service is built, nested relations included, with the full path in the message. See Relations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations).
The resolved eager-loading plan and the parsed options.select. Both are exported for subclasses that override the loader; normal use never touches them.

SqlOperationOptions is the last argument of every method; its keys are listed on the API reference (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/api#sqloperationoptions). Its search key is a SqlSearchOptions:

ilike matches each column with an escaped contains pattern and joins them with OR (plain LIKE on MySQL and SQLite). fullText is PostgreSQL only and compiles to to_tsvector(...) @@ plainto_tsquery(...), or websearch_to_tsquery(...) with queryMode: "websearch". language must be a plain identifier, optionally schema qualified; anything else is a 400.
The second argument of findAll and fullTextSearch.

chunks.h: Filter, sort, cursor and upsert types
chunks.t:
Added in 3.4.0. See Filtering (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering), Pagination and sorting (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting), Cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination) and Upsert (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/upsert).

CrudAllowlists is the seven allowlist keys of SqlCrudConfig, from filterableColumns to writableColumns. ParseCrudQueryOptions extends it with relations, primaryKey, searchColumns, allowTrash and ignore; it and ParsedCrudQuery are described on Parse query strings into filters (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing).

chunks.h: Page, count, scope, event and controller types
chunks.t: Added in 3.5.0. See Relation filters (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relation-filters), Aggregates (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/aggregates), Multi-tenancy (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy), Global hooks and write events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events), CRUD controller factory (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/controller-factory) and OpenAPI docs (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/openapi).

ICrudService is the interface SqlBaseCrudService implements: find, findOne, findAll, create, update, softDelete, restore, delete, the five mass methods, exists and count. It types options as OperationOptions, the older subset of SqlOperationOptions (transaction, relations, select, search, hooks).

Is schema required when I pass a connectionString?. 
No. schema is optional. When you give it, the module passes it to drizzle() as it builds the PostgreSQL or MySQL connection.

Do allowlist arrays merge across the config layers?. 
No. Only softDelete, timestamps, pagination and sql merge one level deep. An array set in forFeature replaces the one from @CrudService.

What happens if I set useReturning to true on MySQL?. 
The service turns it off when it is built and logs a warning, because MySQL has no RETURNING. Written rows are read back with a SELECT instead.

What is the default sort of findAll?. 
With no sortBy and no defaultSort, rows are ordered by the primary key, ascending. Set defaultSort per entity, or defaults.sortOrder in forRoot to sort by the createdAt column.

createCrudController is a NestJS CRUD generator for Drizzle. One call builds list, get, create, update, delete, trash and bulk routes from your service.

createCrudController(Service, options) is the NestJS CRUD generator for Drizzle in this package: it returns a controller class whose routes call your service. You get offset and cursor lists, get, create, update, delete, soft delete, restore, a trash list and four opt-in bulk routes. The id pipe follows the primary key column, so you stop copying the same controller for every table.

Before you start. 
You need a service registered with forFeature (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-feature). Every route goes through
that service, so allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists), scope (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy), soft delete,
optimistic locking (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/optimistic-locking) and events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events) apply exactly as they
do when you call the service in code.

chunks.h: How do I generate a controller?
chunks.t:
Extend the class the factory returns and put @Controller on your subclass:

Import the DTOs as values, not with import type. The factory hands the classes to Nest, and a type-only import is erased at build time.

Eight routes are on by default. The four bulk routes stay off until you turn them on.

Route Method and path Calls Status Default 
--- --- --- --- --- 
list GET / findAll, or findByCursor when?cursor= (or?after=) is present 200 on 
trash GET /trash findAll or findByCursor with onlyDeleted 200 on 
get GET /:id find, 404 when the row is missing 200 on 
create POST / create 201 on 
update PATCH /:id update 200 on 
delete DELETE /:id delete, or softDelete with deleteMode: 'soft' 200 on 
softDelete POST /:id/soft-delete softDelete 200 on 
restore POST /:id/restore restore 200 on 
bulkCreate POST /bulk massCreate, body is an array 201 off 
bulkUpdate PATCH /bulk massUpdate, body is { ids, data } 200 off 
bulkDelete POST /bulk-delete massDelete, or massSoftDelete with deleteMode: 'soft', body is { ids } 200 off 
bulkRestore POST /bulk-restore massRestore, body is { ids } 200 off 

A few rules hold across the table:

- Query strings. list and trash run the whole query string through parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing), so filters, sortBy, fields, with, counts, withCount and cursor all work. get, create, update, restore and the bulk writes read only?with=,?fields= and?counts= and ignore the rest.
- Trash. On an entity without soft delete, trash, softDelete, restore and bulkRestore answer 404 with This resource has no trash. The trash route turns allowTrash off, so?withDeleted= cannot widen it.
- Bulk bodies. ids must be a non-empty array and data must be an object. Anything else is a 400.
- Route order. The static paths (/trash, /bulk, /bulk-delete, /bulk-restore) are registered before /:id, so they never match as an id.

From the primary key column at request time, the way the matching Nest pipe would parse it:

Primary key column Parsing Bad input 
--- --- --- 
integer, serial ParseIntPipe 400 Validation failed (numeric string is expected) 
uuid ParseUUIDPipe 400 
bigint in bigint mode digits (with an optional leading -), then BigInt 400 
anything else, including numeric and decimal the string as is none 

The service exposes the same logic as service.parseId(raw) and service.idKind(), which you can call from your own controllers. Set idType: 'int' 'uuid' 'string' to fix the pipe when the class is built instead. It then shows on the route as a normal @Param('id', ParseIntPipe).
Every option is optional. The source is crud-controller.factory.ts (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/blob/main/packages/nestjs-drizzle-crud/src/controller/crud-controller.factory.ts).

chunks.h: How do I validate request bodies?
chunks.t:
Pass the DTO classes in dto. They become the parameter types of create and update, so a global ValidationPipe validates them the usual way. A global pipe cannot see inside the bulk bodies, so the factory validates them itself: each element of POST /bulk against dto.create, and data of PATCH /bulk against dto.update. Pass your global pipe's options in validation (such as { whitelist: true }) so the bulk routes apply the same rules. Bulk ids are parsed like:id, so a bad one is a 400.

Without dto, bodies reach the service unvalidated. writableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) still applies, so a body cannot write a column you did not allow.

c.s: app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, transform: true }));

chunks.h: How do I turn routes on or off?
chunks.t:
Set a route to true or false in routes. An object turns it on and carries decorators for that route alone:

Roles stands for your own role decorator. { enabled: false } works the same as false.

chunks.h: How do I add guards, interceptors or Swagger tags?
chunks.t: decorators applies method decorators to every route, before the per-route ones. classDecorators decorates the generated class. You can also decorate your subclass directly, which reads like any other Nest controller:

chunks.h: How do I document the routes in Swagger?
chunks.t:
Pass openapi. The factory applies ApiCrudList (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/openapi) to list, and ApiCrudList(source, { trash: true }) to trash:

Keep the entity config in one constant (projectsCrud) and spread it into both forFeature and openapi. The docs then list the same filterable and sortable columns the service accepts.

chunks.h: Can I add my own routes?
chunks.t:
Yes. The factory returns a class, so extend it and add methods. The service is on this.service:

To replace a generated route, turn it off in routes and declare your own handler for the same path. Do not override a generated method by name: the route metadata sits on the generated handler, so Nest would not route your override.

Are the bulk routes on by default?. 
No. bulkCreate, bulkUpdate, bulkDelete and bulkRestore are off until you set them to true in routes. The other eight routes are on.

What does DELETE /:id do on an entity with soft delete?. 
It deletes the row unless you pass deleteMode: 'soft', which makes it call softDelete instead. POST /:id/soft-delete always soft deletes.

Does the generated controller validate request bodies?. 
Only when you pass dto and run a global ValidationPipe. Without DTOs the body goes straight to the service, where writableColumns still applies.

Why does GET /trash answer 404?. 
The entity has soft delete turned off. The trash, soft delete and restore routes answer 404 with This resource has no trash in that case.

How do I add an endpoint the factory does not generate?. 
Extend the generated class and add a decorated method. The service is available as this.service.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
The Drizzle ORM NestJS CRUD methods every service inherits, from find and findAll to create, update, softDelete and mass writes, with errors.

For Drizzle ORM NestJS CRUD, every service that extends SqlBaseCrudService inherits the same
methods: find, findOne, findAll, findByCursor, count and exists to read; create,
update and upsert to write; softDelete, restore, delete and forceDelete to remove; and
mass versions that write a list in one transaction. Each method is typed against your row and
DTO types and throws NestJS HTTP exceptions, so a controller can return its result directly.

Missing rows: reads return, writes throw. 
find and findOne return null for a missing row, and your controller decides whether that
is a 404. update, softDelete, restore and delete throw EntityNotFoundException, which
NestJS answers with a 404 on its own.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: Which methods does a service have?
chunks.t:
These are the public methods of SqlBaseCrudService. T is
the row type, and every options argument is the SqlOperationOptions object listed in
the options table.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
Method Returns Notes 
--- --- --- 
find(id, options?) Promise By primary key. Hides soft deleted rows unless withDeleted. 
findOne(where, options?) Promise First row matching where: exact, case-sensitive values, null for IS NULL, or an operator object. undefined values are skipped. 
findAll(filters?, pagination?, options?) Promise { data, total, page, limit }. With withCount: false, total is null and hasMore is set. 
findByCursor(filters?, pagination?, options?) Promise { data, limit, nextCursor }, plus total when you pass count: true. See Cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination). 
count(filters?, options?) Promise<number Same filters and soft delete rule as findAll. 
countBy(column, filters?, options?) Promise [{ value, count }], largest group first. See Aggregates (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/aggregates). 
exists(id, options?) Promise<boolean One SELECT of the primary key; relations and counts in the options are not loaded. A soft deleted row counts as missing. 
fullTextSearch(term, columns, pagination?, options?) Promise<{ data, total, page, limit } PostgreSQL only, ranked by ts_rank. See Full-text search (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/full-text-search).

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
Method Returns Notes 
--- --- --- 
create(dto, options?) Promise Runs validateCreate, beforeCreate, the insert, then afterCreate. Sets the timestamps. 
update(id, dto, options?) Promise Checks the row exists, runs validateUpdate and beforeUpdate, updates, then afterUpdate. Sets updatedAt. 
upsert(dto, upsert?, options?) Promise Insert, or update on a conflict. See Upsert (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/upsert). 
softDelete(id, options?) Promise<boolean Sets the soft delete column. Needs soft delete on. 
restore(id, options?) Promise Clears the soft delete column and returns the row. Needs soft delete on. 
delete(id, options?) Promise<boolean Hard delete of a live row. 
forceDelete(id, options?) Promise<boolean Hard delete whether the row is soft deleted or not. 
attach, detach, sync Promise Change many-to-many links. See Relations on writes (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations-on-writes).

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
Every mass write runs in one transaction and writes all rows or none.

Method Returns Notes 
--- --- --- 
massCreate(dtos, options?) Promise One multi-row INSERT (row by row on MySQL when the database generates the keys). 
massUpdate(ids, dto, options?) Promise One UPDATE for every id, or one per distinct result when beforeUpdate returns different data per id. Rows come back in ids order. 
massUpsert(dtos, upsert?, options?) Promise One upsert statement for the batch. 
massSoftDelete(ids, options?) Promise<boolean Needs soft delete on. 
massRestore(ids, options?) Promise Needs soft delete on. 
massDelete(ids, options?) Promise<boolean Hard delete of live rows. 
massForceDelete(ids, options?) Promise<boolean Hard delete, soft deleted or not. 

Duplicate ids in a mass update, delete or restore are written once. Pass bulkMode: "perItem" to run each item through the single-row
method in its own savepoint instead. Bulk operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations) covers both modes.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
Method Returns Notes 
--- --- --- 
parseQuery(query, options?) ParsedCrudQuery Turns @Query() into filters, pagination and options. See Query parsing (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing). 
parseId(raw) Promise<unknown Parses a route id like the matching Nest pipe would. 
idKind() "int" \ "bigint" \ "uuid" \ "string" The primary key kind, read from the Drizzle column. 

executeSqlTransaction is protected: call it from a method on your service, not from a
controller. See Transactions (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/transactions).

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: How do I use them in a service and a controller?
chunks.t:
Call the inherited methods directly, and add your own methods to the service when a route needs
more than one call. This service adds two methods on top of the inherited ones:

relations: ["posts"] only works once the entity declares a posts relation; see
Relations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations). Drop it if yours has none.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
findAll returns one page and the total count in a { data, total, page, limit } envelope. It
runs the data query and the COUNT( ) query together, so a list costs two queries, plus one
batched query per eager loaded relation that is not a joined belongs-to.

The pagination argument takes these keys:

", description: "A column, a list such as [\"-created_at\", \"name\"] (a - prefix sorts descending), or { column, order } objects. \"region.name\" sorts by a belongs-to column." },
sortOrder: { type: '"asc" "desc"', default: '"asc"', description: "Direction for a single sortBy string with no prefix. Anything else is a 400." },
withCount: { type: "boolean", default: "true", description: "false skips the COUNT( ) query: total is null and hasMore is set." },
}}
/ 

With no sortBy, rows follow the entity's defaultSort, and the primary key is always added
last so pages never overlap. Note the sortOrder default: sortBy: "name" on its own sorts
descending. Pagination and sorting (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting) covers every rule, and
Filtering (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering) covers the filters object.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: Which exceptions does each method throw?
chunks.t:
Each exception extends a NestJS HTTP exception, so the default exception filter returns the right
status without any setup. They come from
src/exceptions/crud.exceptions.ts.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: Which exceptions does each method throw?
chunks.t:
Method Exception Status When 
--- --- --- --- 
find, findAll, count, exists ValidationFailedException 400 A value the column type cannot parse, such as "abc" for an integer id. 
findOne, findAll, count BadRequestException 400 An unknown column or operator, a bad sortOrder, a name outside an allowlist, or a findOne with no usable condition. 
create, update, upsert DuplicateEntityException 409 A unique constraint is violated. 
create, update, upsert ValidationFailedException 400 A value too long, out of range or failing a check, a column outside writableColumns, or an update with no columns to set. 
create, update, upsert ForeignKeyViolationException 400 A foreign key points at a row that does not exist. 
update, softDelete, restore, delete, forceDelete EntityNotFoundException 404 No row with that id in scope. For delete, a soft deleted row also counts as missing. 
update, softDelete, restore, delete StaleVersionException 409 Optimistic locking is on and the row is at another version. 
delete, forceDelete EntityInUseException 409 Other rows still reference this one. 
upsert EntityNotFoundException 404 On a scoped entity, the conflicting row belongs to another tenant. 
Every mass method BulkOperationException 400 One or more items failed. errors lists each one with the status it would have had alone; nothing is written. 
Every method on a scoped entity MissingScopeException 403 The scope needs a context value, such as a tenant id, that the call does not have.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: Which exceptions does each method throw?
chunks.t:
softDelete, restore, massSoftDelete and massRestore on an entity with soft delete off,
and fullTextSearch on MySQL or SQLite (or search.mode: "fullText" there), are a 400
BadRequestException. Errors (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/errors) shows the response
bodies and how to write a custom filter.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: How do delete, softDelete and forceDelete differ?
chunks.t:
softDelete hides a row by setting its deleted_at column, delete removes a live row, and
forceDelete removes a row whether it is soft deleted or not.

You call Row is live Row is soft deleted 
--- --- --- 
softDelete(id) Sets deleted_at, returns true 404 
restore(id) Returns the row, deleted_at stays null Clears deleted_at, returns the row 
delete(id) Removes it, returns true 404 
forceDelete(id) Removes it, returns true Removes it, returns true 

Reads skip soft deleted rows by default. Pass withDeleted: true to include them, or
onlyDeleted: true for a trash view. Soft delete (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/soft-delete) covers the column setting
and the trash routes.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: Which options does every method take?
chunks.t:
The last argument of every method is SqlOperationOptions. A method ignores the keys that do not
apply to it.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.h: Which options does every method take?
chunks.t:
", description: "Relation counts put on each row under _count." },
lock: { type: '"update" "share" "none"', description: "FOR UPDATE or FOR SHARE on the read, PostgreSQL only. Use it inside a transaction. See Row locks." },
forNoKeyUpdate: { type: "boolean", description: "Take FOR NO KEY UPDATE on the read, PostgreSQL only. Wins over lock." },
"hooks.skipBefore": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Skip the before hook of this call." },
"hooks.skipAfter": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Skip the after hook of this call." },

skipAllowlists: { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Ignore the entity's allowlists for a trusted server-side call." },
skipScope: { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Run a trusted server-side call without the tenant scope." },
context: { type: "CrudContextValue", description: "The context a function scope reads. Defaults to CrudContext.current()." },
skipEvents: { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Do not raise module-level events for this call." },
}}
/

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
Why does find return null instead of throwing a 404?. 
A read that finds nothing is not an error in the service, so find and findOne return null and the controller decides. The write methods throw EntityNotFoundException, which becomes a 404.

What does findAll return?. 
An object with data, total, page and limit. page and limit are the values actually used after clamping, and with withCount: false the total is null and hasMore is added.

Can I call delete on a soft deleted row?. 
No, delete treats a soft deleted row as missing and throws a 404. Use forceDelete to remove a row whether it is soft deleted or not.

Do mass writes stop at the first failure?. 
No. They check every item, then throw one BulkOperationException that lists each failed item with its status, and the transaction writes nothing.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS
chunks.t:
Can I send a date as an ISO string in a create or update body?. 
Yes, since 3.8.2. A JSON body carries dates as strings, so every write (create, update, upsert, the mass writes and nested rows) turns a string or a number for a date-mode timestamp, date or datetime column into a Date, as filters already do: { published_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" } stores that instant. A value that is not a date, an Invalid Date included, is a 400 that names the column: Validation failed: a date or time value has an invalid format: published_at.

Can I call executeSqlTransaction from a controller?. 
No, it is a protected method. Add a method to your service that calls it, and call that method from the controller.

chunks.p: CRUD operations with Drizzle in NestJS

chunks.t:
Drizzle cursor pagination with findByCursor: pass each nextCursor back for the next page. With an index on the sort columns, page 500 is as fast as page 1.

For Drizzle cursor pagination, call findByCursor(filters, { limit, sortBy, cursor }). It returns { data, limit, nextCursor }; pass nextCursor back as cursor to get the next page, until it is null. Each page is a WHERE on the sort columns of the last row instead of an OFFSET, so with an index on the sort columns plus the primary key, page 500 costs the same as page 1, and a row inserted on an earlier page does not shift the next one. This is also called keyset pagination.

When to pick it. 
Use findByCursor for infinite scroll, exports, sync jobs and lists that grow while people read them. Use offset pagination with findAll (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting) when the UI shows page numbers or jumps to page 7.

chunks.h: How do I walk a list with findByCursor?
chunks.t:
Start without a cursor, then pass each page's nextCursor until it comes back null.

Filters, options.search, select, relations, counts, the tenant scope, soft delete and row locks all work as they do in findAll (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting).

The rows, the limit that was used, and the cursor of the next page.

There is no page number: a cursor is a position, not an index. The count query is skipped unless you pass count: true, because counting is the slow part of a large list. With count: true, total is the number of rows that match the filters, not the number left after the cursor.

The cursor holds the sort values of the last row on the page, primary key last, plus the sort it was made for. The next query asks for rows that come after that position, starting with a bound on the first sort column so the database can seek to it in an index. With sortBy: '-views' on a not-null column:

Create an index on the sort columns followed by the primary key, here (views DESC, id); Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/indexes) has one for each sort shape. On 200,000 rows, page 9,000 took 0.6 ms with it, against 24 ms before the bound existed. When every sort column is NOT NULL (or the primary key) and they all sort the same way, Postgres gets one row comparison instead, which an index on (views, id) answers directly:

How each part keeps pages correct and fast:

c.s:
WHERE views <= $1
  AND (views < $1 OR (views = $1 AND id > $2))
ORDER BY views DESC, id ASC
LIMIT 51

chunks.t:
Part Why 
--- --- 
Primary key as the last sort column It makes every position unique, so no row is repeated or skipped. It always sorts ascending, whatever the direction of the other columns. 
Leading bound on the first sort column views <= $1 (descending) or views = $1 (ascending) lets the database start reading at the cursor in an index on the sort columns, instead of scanning every row before it. 
LIMIT limit + 1 The extra row says whether there is a next page. It is dropped from data. 
NULL handling NULLs follow the database's own order: last ascending and first descending on Postgres, the other way round on MySQL and SQLite. The comparison follows the same rule. A NOT NULL column or the primary key gets no IS NULL branch; a nullable column, or a column of a joined relation, keeps it. When the NULLs of the first column come after the cursor, the leading bound is left out so they stay reachable. 
Timestamps read as text A JavaScript Date keeps milliseconds and Postgres keeps microseconds. Reading the value as text keeps the microseconds, so a row is never shown twice. 
bigint values JSON cannot hold a bigint, so it travels as { "$b": "123" } and comes back as a bigint.

The cursor itself is base64url JSON, built in src/core/utils/cursor.ts (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/blob/main/packages/nestjs-drizzle-crud/src/core/utils/cursor.ts). The cursor eyJzIjoibmFtZTphc2MsaWQ6YXNjIiwidiI6WyJDaGFkIiw1MF19 decodes to {"s":"name:asc,id:asc","v":["Chad",50]}: the sort signature and the last row's name and id.

Opaque, not secret. 
Anyone can decode a cursor, so it only ever holds values the rows already show. Do not sort by a column you would not return to the caller.

chunks.h: What happens with a bad cursor?
chunks.t:
It is a 400 (BadRequestException). These all fail:

Cursor Message 
--- --- 
Not a string, not base64url JSON, or the wrong number of values Invalid cursor 
Made for a different sortBy or sortOrder The cursor was made for a different sort; start again without one 

Changing the sort mid-walk breaks the position, so start again from the first page.

chunks.h: How do I use cursor pagination over HTTP?
chunks.t:
With parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing), a cursor (or after) key in the query string starts a keyset walk and sets isCursor. An empty?cursor= means the first page.

One controller method can serve both kinds of list:

c.s:
GET /countries?limit=20&cursor=
GET /countries?limit=20&cursor=eyJzIjoibmFtZTphc2MsaWQ6YXNjIiwidiI6WyJDaGFkIiw1MF19
GET /countries?limit=20&cursor=&count=true

chunks.h: When should I use offset pagination instead?
chunks.t:
When the UI shows page numbers or jumps to a given page. Keyset pages only go forward from a known position. For infinite scroll, exports, sync jobs and any list that grows while people read it, use the cursor.

findAll (offset) findByCursor (keyset) 
--- --- --- 
Jump to page N Yes No 
Cost of a deep page Grows with the offset Same as page 1, with an index on the sort columns and the primary key 
Rows inserted while paging Can shift pages No effect on later pages 
Count query On by default (withCount) Off by default (count)

How do I know I reached the last page?. 
nextCursor is null. The service fetches one row past the limit, and when that row is missing there is no next page.

Can I change sortBy while paging with a cursor?. 
No. The cursor records the sort it was made for, and a cursor used with a different sort is a 400. Start again without a cursor.

Does findByCursor return a total?. 
Only when you pass count: true (or?count=true). The total counts every row matching the filters, not the rows left after the cursor.

Can I go back a page with a cursor?. 
Not with nextCursor alone. Keep the cursors you already used on the client if you need a back button, or use offset pagination with findAll.

Is the cursor encrypted?. 
No. It is base64url JSON that anyone can decode, holding the sort values of the last row and the sort signature.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.h: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.t:
A NestJS Drizzle CRUD service is an empty subclass of SqlBaseCrudService. forFeature injects the db and table, and you add custom methods.

A NestJS Drizzle CRUD service is a class that extends SqlBaseCrudService and declares four generics: the row type, the create DTO, the update DTO and the filter type. The class body is usually empty. DrizzleCrudModule.forFeature builds it with the Drizzle instance, the table, the dialect and the per-entity config, so every CRUD method works without code in the service.

No constructor, no @Injectable(). 
forFeature registers the service with a factory that calls new UsersService(config). A
constructor with other parameters breaks that call. Leave the constructor out and reach the
database through this.config.db.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.h: How do I define a CRUD service?
chunks.t:
Describe the table in Drizzle. The keys created_at, updated_at and deleted_at match the package defaults for
timestamps (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/timestamps) and soft delete (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/soft-delete), so users needs no extra
config.

Extend SqlBaseCrudService. This is the same shape as CountriesService in the example app
(apps/api/src/countries/countries.service.ts).

Register it with forFeature. forFeature needs DrizzleCrudModule.forRoot (or forRootAsync) in your root module. Per-entity
settings go in the optional config object; forFeature (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-feature) lists them all.

Inject it like any provider. The provider token is the class itself, so constructor injection works as usual.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.t:
The keys created_at, updated_at and deleted_at match the package defaults for
timestamps (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/timestamps) and soft delete (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/soft-delete), so users needs no extra
config.
