c.s:
export interface CreateUserDto { name: string; email: string }
export interface UpdateUserDto { name?: string; email?: string }

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.t:
forFeature needs DrizzleCrudModule.forRoot (or forRootAsync) in your root module. Per-entity
settings go in the optional config object; forFeature (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-feature) lists them all.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.t: The provider token is the class itself, so constructor injection works as usual.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.h: What do the four generics mean?
chunks.t:
All four are required: SqlBaseCrudService declares no defaults for them. Pass CrudFilter as the
filter type unless you want a narrower one.

", required: true, description: "The row type the methods return, usually typeof table.$inferSelect." },
CreateDto: { type: "type", required: true, description: "The body create(), massCreate() and upsert() accept." },
UpdateDto: { type: "type", required: true, description: "The body update() and massUpdate() accept." },
FilterDto: { type: "type", required: true, description: "The type of the filters argument of findAll() and count(). CrudFilter allows every operator." },
}}
/ 

FilterDto is only a type. It does not build a query, and it does not stop a key at runtime. Use
the filterableColumns allowlist (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) for that, and see Filtering (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering)
for the filter syntax.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.h: How do I add custom methods?
chunks.t:
Add them to the class. Inside a method you have every CRUD method on this, the resolved config on
this.config, and the Drizzle instance on this.config.db.

A raw Drizzle query skips everything the CRUD methods add: the soft delete predicate, the
tenant scope (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy), the allowlists and the hooks. That is why withPostCount
filters deleted_at itself.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.t:
The protected hooks are there to be overridden. Each has a no-op or pass-through default, so
override only the ones you need.

Hook Runs 
--- --- 
validateCreate(data), validateUpdate(id, data) Before the write, to reject bad input 
beforeCreate(data), beforeUpdate(id, data) Before the write; return the data to write 
mapCreateDtoToEntity(data), mapUpdateDtoToEntity(data) To turn a DTO into column values 
afterCreate(entity), afterUpdate(entity) After the write 
beforeDelete(id), afterDelete(id) Around a hard delete 
beforeSoftDelete(id), afterSoftDelete(id) Around a soft delete 
beforeRestore(id), afterRestore(entity) Around a restore 

See Hooks and validation (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/hooks-validation) for the order they run in and how to skip them.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.h: Why not inject the database in a constructor?
chunks.t:
Because the module already did. This is the pattern to avoid:

forFeature passes one argument, the merged config, to the constructor. A constructor that expects
something else gets the config in the wrong parameter, and the service never sees its table or
settings. If a custom method needs Drizzle, this.config.db is the same instance DRIZZLE_DB
holds.

The same goes for @Injectable(): forFeature already registers the class as a provider, so
leave the decorator off.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.h: Do I need to open the connection myself?
chunks.t:
No. DrizzleCrudModule owns the connection. It uses the db you pass to forRoot as is, or builds
a PostgreSQL connection from connectionString and closes it when the module is destroyed. You do
not need OnModuleInit to warm anything up.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.h: When is the empty subclass not enough?
chunks.t:
- A query across several tables. Write a plain Nest service that injects DRIZZLE_DB and uses
Drizzle directly, rather than bending a CRUD service around it.
- Very large result sets. findAll loads a page into memory. Walk the table with
cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination), or inject DRIZZLE_DB and use your driver's
streaming.
- GraphQL. The service methods are plain async functions, so a resolver calls them the same way
a controller does.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.t:
Do the generics of SqlBaseCrudService have defaults?. 
No. All four are required: the row type, the create DTO, the update DTO and the filter type. Pass CrudFilter for the filter type if you do not need a narrower one.

Should a CRUD service have @Injectable()?. 
No. forFeature registers the class as a provider with a factory that passes the config to the constructor, so the decorator adds nothing.

How do I use Drizzle directly inside a CRUD service?. 
Use this.config.db, the same Drizzle instance the module provides as DRIZZLE_DB. Raw queries do not add the soft delete or tenant predicates, so add them yourself.

Can I add my own methods to the service?. 
Yes. Add them to the class body and call this.find, this.findAll or any other CRUD method from them, or use this.config.db for raw Drizzle.

chunks.p: Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.h: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.t:
Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS CRUD. How each defines the schema, queries, migrates and plugs into Nest, and which CRUD layers fit each.

Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS CRUD is a choice between three ways of describing your data. Drizzle declares tables as TypeScript functions and queries with a SQL-like builder. TypeORM maps decorated entity classes and supports both Data Mapper and Active Record. Prisma generates a typed client from its own schema file. All three work with NestJS; they differ in schema style, Nest integration and the CRUD libraries built on top.

Facts checked on 2 November 2026. 
Every statement about an ORM links to its own docs, the NestJS docs or its npm entry, read on 2 November 2026. This page makes no speed or popularity claims, because none of those sources publish numbers that compare the three. nestjs-drizzle-crud supports Drizzle only.

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.h: How do the three ORMs compare?
chunks.t:
Drizzle ORM TypeORM Prisma ORM 
--- --- --- --- 
Schema TypeScript functions such as pgTable (Drizzle (https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/overview)) Classes with @Entity() and @Column() decorators (TypeORM (https://typeorm.io/)) A Prisma schema, from which a type-safe client is generated (NestJS docs (https://docs.nestjs.com/techniques/database)) 
Query style SQL-like builder plus a relational query API (Drizzle (https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/overview)) Data Mapper (repositories) or Active Record (TypeORM (https://typeorm.io/)) Generated client methods (NestJS docs (https://docs.nestjs.com/data/prisma)) 
Code generation step None (NestJS docs (https://docs.nestjs.com/data/drizzle)) None; entities are your own decorated classes Yes, the client is generated 
Migrations Drizzle Kit: drizzle-kit generate, drizzle-kit migrate (NestJS docs (https://docs.nestjs.com/data/drizzle)) Built in, with automatic generation (TypeORM (https://typeorm.io/)) Prisma Migrate (Prisma (https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v7/prisma-migrate)) 
Introspect an existing database drizzle-kit pull (Drizzle (https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/drizzle-kit-pull)) Not covered here Not covered here 
Databases PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SingleStore, MSSQL, CockroachDB (Drizzle (https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/overview)) CockroachDB, Google Spanner, MariaDB, MongoDB, SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SAP HANA, SQLite (TypeORM (https://typeorm.io/)) Prisma 7: CockroachDB, MariaDB, SQL Server, MongoDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite (Prisma (https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v7/reference/supported-databases)) 
Nest package @nestjs/drizzle, maintained by the Nest team @nestjs/typeorm, maintained by the Nest team None; you expose the generated client through a provider 
Latest on npm drizzle-orm 0.45.4 (8 October 2026); 1.0.0-rc.5 on the rc tag typeorm 1.1.2 (8 October 2026) @prisma/client 7.10.1 (15 October 2026) 
License Apache-2.0 MIT Apache-2.0

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.h: How do the three ORMs compare?
chunks.t:
The Nest package row comes from the NestJS database chapter (https://docs.nestjs.com/techniques/database): "The Nest team maintains the @nestjs/typeorm, @nestjs/drizzle, @nestjs/mongoose, and @nestjs/sequelize packages", and Prisma "has no Nest-specific package". npm versions and dates are from the npm registry for drizzle-orm (https://www.npmjs.com/package/drizzle-orm), typeorm (https://www.npmjs.com/package/typeorm) and @prisma/client (https://www.npmjs.com/package/@prisma/client).

"Not covered here" means this page did not check that feature, not that the ORM lacks it.

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.h: What does the same table look like in each?
chunks.t:
One users table with an id, a name and an email.

The row type is inferred from the table, so there is no class to keep in sync.

The class is both the schema and the row type.

The client and its types are generated from this file.

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.h: Which CRUD libraries exist for each?
chunks.t:
A CRUD layer is tied to one ORM, so this choice often decides the ORM, or the other way round.

ORM Library What it covers State as of November 2026 
--- --- --- --- 
Drizzle nestjs-drizzle-crud (this package) Service with reads and writes, query string parser, optional generated controller Version, see the changelog (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/changelog) 
TypeORM @nestjsx/crud (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud) @Crud() generated controllers, TypeORM service, frontend request builder Last stable 4.6.2 (May 2020), latest tag 5.0.0-alpha.3 (February 2021) 
TypeORM nestjs-paginate (https://github.com/ppetzold/nestjs-paginate) Paginated, filtered lists 16.0.1 (19 October 2026) 

This page does not list CRUD libraries for Prisma, because none were checked. The detailed comparisons are on nestjs-drizzle-crud vs @nestjsx/crud (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/vs-nestjsx-crud) and nestjs-drizzle-crud vs nestjs-paginate (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/vs-nestjs-paginate).

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.t: Check the Drizzle version first. nestjs-drizzle-crud declares drizzle-orm from 0.28.0 up to, not including, 1.0.0 as its peer range. The NestJS Drizzle chapter (https://docs.nestjs.com/data/drizzle) installs drizzle-orm@rc, which on 2 November 2026 resolves to 1.0.0-rc.5, outside that range. On drizzle-orm 0.45.x you can open the connection yourself and pass it to DrizzleCrudModule.forRoot as db; the module then uses it as is and never closes it. See forRoot (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-root).

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.t:
Choose Drizzle when:

- you want the schema and its types in plain TypeScript, with no decorators and no generate step,
- you think in SQL and want a query builder that reads like it, or
- you want a CRUD layer such as nestjs-drizzle-crud on top.

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.t:
Choose TypeORM when:

- your team already models data as decorated classes, or uses Active Record,
- you need a database Drizzle does not list, such as Oracle, SAP HANA or Google Spanner, or
- you want @nestjsx/crud or nestjs-paginate, which are built on it.

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.t:
Choose Prisma when:

- you prefer one schema file that drives both the client and migrations,
- you are fine wiring the generated client into Nest with a provider of your own.

Check the version you install: on 2 November 2026 the latest tag of the prisma CLI on npm is 8.0.0-rc.29, a release candidate, and the NestJS Prisma chapter (https://docs.nestjs.com/data/prisma) tells you to install prisma@7 and @prisma/client@7 explicitly.

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
chunks.t:
Does nestjs-drizzle-crud work with TypeORM or Prisma?. 
No. It reads Drizzle table objects and runs Drizzle queries, so it needs a Drizzle schema. It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite.

Does NestJS have an official Drizzle package?. 
Yes. The NestJS database chapter lists @nestjs/drizzle among the packages the Nest team maintains. Its npm version on 2 November 2026 is 0.0.2.

Which ORM is fastest for NestJS?. 
This page does not say, because none of the sources it uses publish a benchmark comparing the three. Measure with your own queries and data.

Can I move an existing database to Drizzle?. 
Yes. drizzle-kit pull introspects an existing database and writes a Drizzle schema file, which you then review and keep in your code.

chunks.p: Drizzle vs TypeORM vs Prisma for NestJS
Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.h: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t:
NestJS Drizzle error handling without a custom filter. Each exception extends a Nest HTTP exception, so a missing row is a 404 and a duplicate a 409.

NestJS Drizzle error handling in nestjs-drizzle-crud works out of the box: every exception the service throws extends a NestJS HttpException subclass, so Nest's default exception filter answers with the right status code and no custom filter. A missing row is a 404, a unique or version conflict is a 409, a missing tenant is a 403, and bad input is a 400. Postgres driver errors caused by bad input are translated at the service boundary instead of reaching the client as a 500.

The exceptions carry a message, not fields. 
The classes take an entity name, a field or an id in their constructor, but only to build the message. They have no entity, field, value or id property. Read getStatus(), message and getResponse() instead.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.h: Which status does each exception return?
chunks.t:
Each class extends the Nest exception that carries its status, and the constructor builds the message:

Exception Extends HTTP Constructor Message 
--- --- --- --- --- 
EntityNotFoundException NotFoundException 404 (entityName, id) users with id 9 not found 
DuplicateEntityException ConflictException 409 (entityName, field, value) users with email 'a@b.co' already exists 
StaleVersionException ConflictException 409 (entityName, id) projects with id 4 was changed by someone else; read it again and retry 
EntityInUseException ConflictException 409 (entityName) teams is still referenced by other records and cannot be deleted 
MissingScopeException ForbiddenException 403 (entityName, key) projects is scoped by "tenant_id", but the context has no value for it 
ValidationFailedException BadRequestException 400 (message) Validation failed: <message 
ForeignKeyViolationException BadRequestException 400 (entityName, field) Invalid reference for users: 'team_id' does not refer to an existing record 
BulkOperationException BadRequestException 400 (message, errors) Mass update errors. 2 error(s) occurred.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.h: Which status does each exception return?
chunks.t:
The entity name is the table name Drizzle reports. Each class also sets name to its own class name, so exception.name is "EntityNotFoundException" and so on. Every class is exported from the package root; see Exports (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/exports).

TransactionException (500, InternalServerErrorException) means the driver cannot run the transaction a call needs. Since 3.7.0 it is thrown on Cloudflare D1 and on synchronous SQLite drivers by the bulk writes, nested creates and attach / detach / sync; see SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1 (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/sqlite). A transaction that fails while it runs still rejects with the error that caused it. DatabaseConnectionException (500) is still exported but deprecated: nothing throws it, and it goes in the next major version.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.h: What does the response body look like?
chunks.t:
Nest's standard body for an HttpException built from a message:

BulkOperationException is the one exception with a richer body. It lists every failed item, with index for massCreate and massUpsert (the position in the input array) and id for the rest:

An item that failed with an HttpException keeps its own status and message. Any other error is reported as status: 500 with the message Internal server error, because a raw driver error can carry SQL and parameters. The original errors stay on the exception's public errors property (Array<{ id?, index?, error } ) for your logs. See Bulk insert and update with Drizzle (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations#what-does-a-failed-bulk-call-return-over-http).

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t:
The service catches Postgres errors by SQLSTATE code (on the error or its Drizzle cause) and throws the matching exception:

SQLSTATE Meaning Becomes 
--- --- --- 
23505 unique violation DuplicateEntityException (409), field and value parsed from the driver detail 
23503 on create or update the row references a parent that does not exist ForeignKeyViolationException (400), column parsed from detail 
23503 on delete other rows still reference this one (ON DELETE RESTRICT or NO ACTION) EntityInUseException (409) 
22001 value too long for its column ValidationFailedException (400) 
23514 check constraint failed ValidationFailedException (400) 
22003 numeric value out of range ValidationFailedException (400) 
22P02 value does not match the column type ("abc" for an integer, an unknown enum label) ValidationFailedException (400) 
22007, 22008 date or time with an invalid format, or out of range ValidationFailedException (400) 
21000 the same key twice in one massUpsert ValidationFailedException (400) 
23502 a required column got no value ValidationFailedException (400), with the column name

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t:
On MySQL, ER_DUP_ENTRY (1062) is a 409 DuplicateEntityException, ER_NO_REFERENCED_ROW_2 (1452) a 400 ForeignKeyViolationException, and ER_ROW_IS_REFERENCED_2 (1451) on a delete a 409 EntityInUseException. Since 3.7.0 the strict mode data errors are a 400 ValidationFailedException too, with the column name from the message:

MySQL errno Meaning 
--- --- 
1048, 1364 a required column got no value 
1406 value too long for its column 
1264 numeric value out of range 
1265, 1366 value does not match the column type 
1292 date or time with an invalid format 
3819 check constraint failed

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t:
On SQLite the constraint kind decides: UNIQUE or PRIMARY KEY is a 409 DuplicateEntityException (SQLite names the column but not the value), FOREIGN KEY is a 400 on create or update and a 409 on delete, and NOT NULL or CHECK is a 400 ValidationFailedException. libSQL and better-sqlite3 report the kind as an extended code such as SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE; D1 only in the message, which is read instead. Since 3.7.2 two type errors are a 400 ValidationFailedException too: a STRICT table refusing a value of the wrong type (extended code 3091, which libSQL reports as UNKNOWN_SQLITE_ERROR_3091, with the column name), and SQLITE_MISMATCH, such as "abc" for an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY.

Any other error passes through unchanged.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.h: Which other 400s does the service throw?
chunks.t:
Plain Nest BadRequestExceptions for input the service cannot use:

- an unknown filter column or operator, an operator on the wrong column type, or an invalid date,
- an invalid cursor, or a findOne with no condition,
- an unknown fullTextSearch column,
- a statement with more bound parameters than the database takes (65,535 on PostgreSQL and MySQL, 32,766 on SQLite, 100 on D1), see how large a bulk call can be (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations#how-large-can-a-bulk-call-be),
- anything outside an allowlist (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists),
- anything parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing) cannot read.

See clamping and fail-fast input (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting#clamping-fail-fast) for which pagination values are clamped and which throw. ValidationFailedException covers an update with no column left to set, a column outside writableColumns, a non-integer version, and whatever your validateCreate or validateUpdate hooks throw.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Reads return null instead of throwing. find, findOne, findAll, exists, count and fullTextSearch return null, false or an empty page for missing rows, and never throw EntityNotFoundException. You decide how to respond. The controller factory (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/controller-factory) does that for you: its GET /:id route answers a missing row with EntityNotFoundException, a 404.

Bad input on a read is a 400, the same as on a write: find("abc") on an integer key, findAll({ status: "archived" }) when the enum has no such label, or { createdAt: { gte: "garbage" } }. A soft-deleted row counts as missing when soft delete is on.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Writes. Method 404 409 400 
--- --- --- --- 
create(dto) unique violation hook rejection, missing FK target 
upsert(dto, upsert) conflict with another tenant's row unique violation on another key hook rejection, missing FK target, unknown conflict target 
update(id, dto) row missing, soft-deleted or outside the scope unique violation, stale version hook rejection, missing FK target, nothing to update 
delete(id) row missing or soft-deleted still referenced, stale version 
forceDelete(id) row missing still referenced 
softDelete(id) row missing or already soft-deleted stale version 
restore(id) row missing stale version 
attach / detach / sync row missing unknown target ids (404 entries), not a many-to-many 

On a scoped entity (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy), a row of another tenant counts as missing everywhere, and a call without the tenant is a 403 MissingScopeException. update and restore return the written row.

softDelete on an entity without soft delete is a 400. 
softDelete and restore throw a BadRequestException (Soft delete is not enabled for this entity) when soft delete is off. Before 3.5.2 this was a plain Error and reached the client as a 500.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.h: Reads return null instead of throwing
chunks.t:
find, findOne, findAll, exists, count and fullTextSearch return null, false or an empty page for missing rows, and never throw EntityNotFoundException. You decide how to respond. The controller factory (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/controller-factory) does that for you: its GET /:id route answers a missing row with EntityNotFoundException, a 404.

Bad input on a read is a 400, the same as on a write: find("abc") on an integer key, findAll({ status: "archived" }) when the enum has no such label, or { createdAt: { gte: "garbage" } }. A soft-deleted row counts as missing when soft delete is on.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Method 404 409 400 
--- --- --- --- 
create(dto) unique violation hook rejection, missing FK target 
upsert(dto, upsert) conflict with another tenant's row unique violation on another key hook rejection, missing FK target, unknown conflict target 
update(id, dto) row missing, soft-deleted or outside the scope unique violation, stale version hook rejection, missing FK target, nothing to update 
delete(id) row missing or soft-deleted still referenced, stale version 
forceDelete(id) row missing still referenced 
softDelete(id) row missing or already soft-deleted stale version 
restore(id) row missing stale version 
attach / detach / sync row missing unknown target ids (404 entries), not a many-to-many 

On a scoped entity (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy), a row of another tenant counts as missing everywhere, and a call without the tenant is a 403 MissingScopeException. update and restore return the written row.

softDelete on an entity without soft delete is a 400. 
softDelete and restore throw a BadRequestException (Soft delete is not enabled for this entity) when soft delete is off. Before 3.5.2 this was a plain Error and reached the client as a 500.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t: massCreate, massUpdate, massUpsert, massSoftDelete, massRestore, massDelete and massForceDelete each run in one transaction. Any failure throws BulkOperationException (400) and rolls back the whole call, so there are no partial writes.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t: executeSqlTransaction wraps a callback in a transaction. On any throw inside the callback, the transaction rolls back and the same error propagates unchanged. Pass { transaction: tx } in the options of any CRUD method to enlist it. See Transactions (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/transactions).

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I write a custom exception filter?
chunks.t:
You only need one to change the body shape. Catch the package's classes and read what an HttpException really has: getStatus(), message, name and getResponse():

Register it with app.useGlobalFilters(new CrudExceptionFilter()) or @UseFilters on a controller. Without a filter, Nest's default one already returns the status codes on this page.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Do I need an exception filter to get 404 and 409 responses?. 
No. The exceptions extend NotFoundException, ConflictException, ForbiddenException and BadRequestException, so Nest's default filter returns the right status on its own.

Does find throw when the row does not exist?. 
No. find and findOne return null, and exists returns false. Only writes throw EntityNotFoundException, as does the controller factory's GET /:id route.

Why does a duplicate email return 409 instead of 500?. 
The service catches the Postgres unique violation (23505) and throws DuplicateEntityException, a ConflictException. The field and value in the message come from the driver's detail text.

How do I get the field name out of DuplicateEntityException?. 
The class has no field property; the field only appears in its message, as in users with email 'a@b.co' already exists. If you need it structured, catch the driver error yourself in an override.

Are SQLite constraint errors mapped to HTTP status codes?. 
Yes, since 3.7.0. A UNIQUE or primary key violation is a 409, a FOREIGN KEY violation a 400 on a write and a 409 on a delete, and NOT NULL or CHECK a 400.

chunks.p: Error handling in NestJS with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Are MySQL errors mapped to HTTP status codes?. 
Yes. ER_DUP_ENTRY is a 409, a missing parent row a 400, a delete blocked by other rows a 409, and since 3.7.0 the strict mode data errors (a value too long, a missing required value, a wrong type) are a 400. Other MySQL errors reach Nest unchanged.

chunks.h: NestJS Drizzle CRUD events and audit logs
chunks.t:
NestJS Drizzle CRUD events fire before and after every write on one CrudEventBus, once per call, bulk included. Use them for audit logs and cache busting.

NestJS Drizzle CRUD events in nestjs-drizzle-crud are module-level notifications raised before and after every write. Turn on hooks.enableGlobalHooks, and every service publishes a before event and an after event on one CrudEventBus for create, update, upsert, soft delete, restore, delete, attach, detach and sync. A mass write raises one pair for the whole batch. Subscribe once and you see every entity, which is what an audit log or a cache needs.

Off by default. 
With enableGlobalHooks off, no events fire. If you set hooks.subscribers without it, the module logs a warning at startup.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle CRUD events and audit logs
chunks.h: What does a subscriber look like?
chunks.t:
An object of optional listener methods. beforeWrite and afterWrite see every operation; the named methods see one:

Method Called for 
--- --- 
beforeWrite, afterWrite every operation 
beforeCreate, afterCreate create, massCreate 
beforeUpdate, afterUpdate update, massUpdate 
beforeUpsert, afterUpsert upsert, massUpsert 
beforeSoftDelete, afterSoftDelete softDelete, massSoftDelete 
beforeRestore, afterRestore restore, massRestore 
beforeDelete, afterDelete delete, forceDelete, massDelete, massForceDelete 
beforeAttach / afterAttach, beforeDetach / afterDetach, beforeSync / afterSync the many-to-many link methods 

entities: ["posts", "authors"] limits a subscriber to those table names. Subscribers run one after another in the order they subscribed, and every listener is awaited. Within one subscriber, beforeWrite or afterWrite runs before the named method.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle CRUD events and audit logs
chunks.t:
Every listener receives one CrudEvent:

A force delete is reported as delete. context is the call's options.context, or the CrudContext (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy#where-does-the-context-come-from) of the request, so an audit row can record the tenant or user.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle CRUD events and audit logs
chunks.h: How do bulk writes raise events?
chunks.t:
Once per call. A mass write raises one before event and one after event with bulk: true, every id in ids and every written row in rows, from inside its transaction. A massUpdate of 500 rows is two events, not a thousand.

With bulkMode: "perItem" each item goes through the single-row method instead, so you get one pair of events per item with bulk: false. See Bulk operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations).

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle CRUD events and audit logs
chunks.h: Can a listener stop a write?
chunks.t: Yes, a before listener can. If it throws, nothing is written and the caller gets the error (a Nest HttpException keeps its status). An after listener that throws inside a transaction rolls the write back. Every mass write runs in a transaction; a single write only does when you pass one in options.transaction.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle CRUD events and audit logs
chunks.h: How do events relate to the per-service hooks?
chunks.t: They are separate and both run. The protected hooks on a service (beforeCreate, afterUpdate and the rest) run per row and follow options.hooks.skipBefore / skipAfter. Events run once per call and follow options.skipEvents instead, so skipping a hook never silently skips the audit trail. See Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/hooks-validation).

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle CRUD events and audit logs
chunks.t:
Do CRUD events fire once per row in a mass write?. 
No. A mass write raises one before and one after event for the whole call, with every id in ids and bulk: true. Only bulkMode: "perItem" raises one pair per item.

Do events fire for reads?. 
No. Events cover writes only: create, update, upsert, soft delete, restore, delete, attach, detach and sync.

Does skipping hooks also skip events?. 
No. hooks.skipBefore and hooks.skipAfter skip the per-service hooks only. Pass skipEvents: true to skip the events of a call.

How do I write an audit row in the same transaction as the write?. 
Insert through event.transaction when it is set. The audit row then commits or rolls back with the write it records.

chunks.t:
Every export of nestjs-drizzle-crud, the classes, functions, decorators, DI tokens, exceptions, types and Drizzle helpers you can import from the package root.

nestjs-drizzle-crud exports 98 names from its package root: 79 of its own (classes, functions, decorators, DI tokens, exceptions, test helpers and types) and 19 Drizzle helpers re-exported unchanged. Import all of them with import {... } from "@avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud". Anything not listed here is internal and can change in any release.

The root is the only public entry point. 
src/index.ts is the public surface. Removing or renaming anything on this page is a major
version, so code that imports only from the root survives every minor and patch upgrade.

Export Kind Description 
--- --- --- 
SqlBaseCrudService abstract class The base class your services extend. See SqlBaseCrudService API reference (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/api). 
DrizzleCrudModule class The Nest module, with forRoot, forRootAsync and forFeature. 
CrudService decorator @CrudService(config) stores per-entity config on a service class. The forFeature config wins over it. 
parseCrudQuery function parseCrudQuery(query, table, options?) turns an HTTP query object into filters, pagination and options. Since 3.4.0. See NestJS query string filters for Drizzle (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing). 
createCrudController function createCrudController(Service, options?) returns a controller class with list, trash, get, create, update, delete, soft delete, restore and bulk routes. Since 3.5.0. See NestJS CRUD controller generator (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/controller-factory). 
CrudContext object run(context, fn), current() and middleware(resolve): the per-request context a scope reads, kept in AsyncLocalStorage. Since 3.5.0. See Multi-tenancy (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy). 
CrudEventBus class The module-level event bus behind hooks.enableGlobalHooks. forRoot and forRootAsync provide it globally; inject it and call subscribe. Since 3.5.0. See Events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events).

Export Kind Description 
--- --- --- 
DRIZZLE_DB string Token for the resolved Drizzle instance. Inject it for hand-written queries outside a service. 
DRIZZLE_CONNECTION string Token for the DrizzleConnection wrapper. 
DRIZZLE_CRUD_CONFIG string Token for the normalized project config. 
DrizzleConnection class Holds db. Builds the PostgreSQL connection from a connectionString, or uses the db you passed, and closes only the connection it opened.

Both decorators need the optional peer @nestjs/swagger, loaded the first time one runs. Since 3.5.0. See NestJS Drizzle Swagger docs for lists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/openapi).

Export Kind Description 
--- --- --- 
ApiCrudQuery decorator ApiCrudQuery(source, options?) documents every list query parameter and each filterable column. 
ApiCrudList decorator ApiCrudQuery plus the 200 page envelope with the row schema.

Every exception extends a Nest HttpException subclass, so the default exception filter maps it to its status without a custom filter, and you can match it with instanceof. See Error handling (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/errors).

Export HTTP When 
--- --- --- 
EntityNotFoundException 404 update, softDelete, restore or delete on a missing row, and per id in a mass write. 
DuplicateEntityException 409 A unique constraint is violated (Postgres 23505). 
StaleVersionException 409 Optimistic locking: a write named a version the row is no longer at. Since 3.5.0. 
EntityInUseException 409 delete while other rows still reference the row (23503). 
MissingScopeException 403 A scoped entity was used without the context value its scope needs. Since 3.5.0. 
ForeignKeyViolationException 400 create or update references a parent row that does not exist (23503). Names the column. 
ValidationFailedException 400 Bad input: a value the column cannot take, an update with nothing to set, a column outside writableColumns. Throw it from your validation hooks too. 
BulkOperationException 400 A bulk method rolled back. The body lists each failed item as { index \ id, status, message }; the errors property keeps the original errors. 
DatabaseConnectionException 500 Deprecated. Nothing throws it. Removed in the next major version. 
TransactionException 500 The driver cannot run the transaction a call needs (Cloudflare D1, synchronous SQLite drivers). Thrown since 3.7.0; it was deprecated before. A failed transaction still rejects with its own error.

Export Kind Description 
--- --- --- 
TestCrudFactory class Static createTestService, createMockDb, createMockTable and createMockEntity. The mocks use jest.fn(), so they need Jest globals. 
BaseCrudSpecHelper class Builds a service on a mock database and returns ready-made find, create, update, delete and list scenarios. 

See Testing (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/testing).
All type-only exports. Import them with import type.

Export Description 
--- --- 
DrizzleCrudConfig The input to forRoot and forRootAsync. 
DrizzleConnectionOptions connection in DrizzleCrudConfig: { poolSize?, idleTimeout?, ssl? } for the connection the module builds. Since 3.7.0. 
DrizzleCrudAsyncOptions The argument of forRootAsync: useFactory, useClass or useExisting, with imports and inject. Since 3.7.0. 
DrizzleCrudOptionsFactory The class shape useClass and useExisting expect: createDrizzleCrudOptions(). Since 3.7.0. 
SqlCrudConfig The merged per-entity config. 
CrudFeature One entry of forFeature: { service, table, config? }. 
CrudFeatureConfig The per-entity config of forFeature. Since 3.3.1. 
SqlOperationOptions The options argument of every method. 
SqlSearchOptions, SqlSearchMode options.search: { term, columns, mode?, language?, queryMode? }, and "ilike" \ "fullText". Since 3.3.1. 
FullTextOptions, FullTextQueryMode { language?, queryMode? } and "plain" \ "websearch". Since 3.7.0. 
FullTextSearchOptions The options argument of fullTextSearch: SqlOperationOptions plus filters, language and queryMode. Since 3.7.0. 
PaginationOptions The pagination argument of findAll and fullTextSearch: { page, limit, sortBy, sortOrder, withCount }. Since 3.3.1. 
ICrudService The interface SqlBaseCrudService implements. 
OperationOptions The options type of ICrudService. Since 3.3.1. 
BulkOperationResult { success, data?, errors? }. Since 3.3.1. 
BulkOperationItemError One entry of a BulkOperationException body: { index?, id?, status, message }. Since 3.3.1. 
RelationConfig, RelationsConfig, RelationType One relation, a record of them, and "belongsTo" \ "hasMany" \ "manyToMany". 
RelationNode, SelectTree The resolved eager-loading plan and the parsed options.select. 
SqlDialect "postgresql" \ "mysql" \ "sqlite". "sqlite" since 3.7.0. 
PrimaryKeyType "serial" \ "bigserial" \ "int" \ "bigint" \ "uuid". The setting that uses it is deprecated. 
SortColumn, SortOrder { column, order? } and "asc" \ "desc". 
SortInput string \ Array<string \ SortColumn, the caller sortBy. Since 3.4.0. 
CrudFilter, FilterGroup The filter object of findAll, findByCursor and count, and its { and?, or?, not? } groups. Since 3.4.0. 
FilterOperators, FilterOperator Every filter operator with its operand, and the operator names. Since 3.4.0. 
ColumnFilter, FilterScalar What one column accepts. Since 3.4.0. 
CursorPaginationOptions, CursorPage The input and result of findByCursor. Since 3.4.0. 
CrudAllowlists The allowlist keys of SqlCrudConfig. Since 3.4.0; writableRelations since 3.5.0. 
UpsertOptions { conflictTarget?, update? }. Since 3.4.0. 
BulkMode "set" \ "perItem". Since 3.4.0. 
ParseCrudQueryOptions, ParsedCrudQuery The options and result of parseCrudQuery and parseQuery. Since 3.4.0. 
CollectionFilter, CollectionQuantifier { some?, none?, every? } on a collection filter, and its keys. Since 3.5.0. 
CrudPage, UncountedCrudPage The findAll envelope, and the one with total: null and hasMore. Since 3.5.0. 
RelationCounts options.counts: string[] \ Record<string, true \ CrudFilter. Since 3.5.0. 
CountByRow { value, count }, one group of countBy. Since 3.5.0. 
CrudScope, CrudScopeValues, CrudContextValue The scope config, its column: value pairs, and the context it reads. Since 3.5.0. 
CrudEvent, CrudEventPhase, CrudSubscriber, CrudWriteOperation Write events and their subscribers. Since 3.5.0. 
CrudControllerOptions, CrudControllerInstance, CrudRouteName, CrudRouteOptions The controller factory's options and result. Since 3.5.0.

The full definitions are on Config types reference (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/config-types).
These are pass-throughs from drizzle-orm, re-exported so a custom method or mapCreateDtoToEntity override needs one import. The package does not wrap or change them.

chunks.t: The module's internal helpers (normalizeConfig, buildEntityConfig, connectionProviders), the DRIZZLE_RAW_CONFIG token, and the service's private methods are not part of the API. If you need one of them, open an issue on the issue tracker: the public API may need a hook.

How many exports does nestjs-drizzle-crud have?. 
98: 79 of its own and 19 Drizzle helpers. Of its own, 25 are runtime values (classes, functions, decorators, tokens, exceptions and test helpers) and 54 are types.

Is the MCP server an export?. 
No. nestjs-drizzle-crud-mcp is a command-line binary in the package, not an import. Run it with npx -p @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud nestjs-drizzle-crud-mcp.

Can I import from a deep path such as dist/core?. 
Deep paths are internal and can change in any release. Import from the package root only.

Why are the Drizzle helpers re-exported?. 
So code that extends a service can build conditions with eq, and or sql from the same import. They are the drizzle-orm functions themselves, unchanged.

Drizzle filtering in NestJS with findAll and count. Pass exact values, arrays, operators such as gte, between and contains, and or, and, not groups.

Drizzle filtering in NestJS works through one plain object: findAll(filters) and count(filters) take an object keyed by column name, and the package compiles it to a Drizzle WHERE. A bare value is an exact match, an array is IN (...), and an object of operators such as gte, between or contains covers everything else. Keys are ANDed, or, and and not group them, and an unknown key is a 400.

Keys are Drizzle keys. 
A filter key is the key of the column in your Drizzle table object (createdAt), not the SQL
column name (created_at). The examples on this page use a users table served by
UsersService, with a belongs-to organization relation and a has-many posts relation.

chunks.h: How do I filter by a column value?
chunks.t:
Pass the value under the column key. null and undefined values are skipped, so a query DTO with empty fields can go straight in.

count takes the same object, so a list and its total always agree:

chunks.h: Can I pass query string values as strings?
chunks.t:
Yes. HTTP query values always arrive as strings, and the package handles them by column type:

Column What a string does 
--- --- 
text, varchar, char Compared with lower(column) = lower(value) while sql.caseSensitive is false, the default. 
integer, uuid, enum and other non-text columns Compared with a plain =, and PostgreSQL casts the string to the column type. { organizationId: "1" } matches organization_id = 1. 
date and timestamp (date mode) Turned into a Date first, so { createdAt: { gte: "2025-01-01" } } works. A string that is not a date is a 400. 

A value the column cannot hold, such as "abc" for an integer or an enum label that does not exist, is a 400 too, never a raw 500. To coerce a whole query string up front (numbers, booleans, bigints, dates), use parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing).

c.s:
await this.users.findAll({ name: { startsWith: "jo" } }); // starts with "jo"
await this.users.findAll({ name: { contains: "doe" } }); // contains "doe"
await this.users.findAll({ name: { ilike: "jo%n" } }); // your own pattern

chunks.h: Can I pass query string values as strings?
chunks.t:
A bare string is an exact match, not a partial one. 
On a text column { name: "jo" } compiles to lower(name) = lower('jo'). The match ignores
case, and %, _ and \ in the value are literal data, never wildcards. For a partial match
use startsWith, endsWith or contains (which escape those characters for you, so
{ contains: "50%" } matches the text "50%"), or like / ilike with your own pattern.

Yes. findOne turns a string into a plain =, whatever sql.caseSensitive says, while findAll, count, countBy and?column= use lower() on text columns by default. With the default setting, findOne({ email: "A@X.IO" }) can return null for a row that findAll({ email: "A@X.IO" }) finds. Pass the stored case to findOne, or use findAll(filters, { limit: 1 }) when case must not matter.

A plain index on the column cannot serve lower(column) = lower($1). Add one on lower(column), or see Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/indexes) for the other options and the index behind every operator.

chunks.h: How do I use operators like gte, between and contains?
chunks.t:
Wrap the value in an object of operator keys. Several operators on one column are ANDed.

An operator the package does not know, such as { roughly: 2 }, is a 400 (Unknown filter operator: roughly) rather than being dropped. An operator whose value is undefined adds nothing.
All 22 operators, as the service and the query parser handle them:

Operator SQL Notes 
--- --- --- 
eq = A plain =, with no lower(). Case-sensitive on PostgreSQL and SQLite even on text columns; MySQL's default collations ignore case. 
neq < Not equal. 
gt / gte / lt / lte = < <= Numeric and date columns. Date strings are parsed. NaN or Infinity is a 400. 
like LIKE You supply the % wildcards. The value is passed as is. On SQLite the package adds ESCAPE '\', so a backslash escapes as it does on the other dialects. 
ilike ILIKE (PostgreSQL), LIKE (MySQL, SQLite) Case-insensitive, you supply the %. MySQL and SQLite have no ILIKE; MySQL's default collations ignore case, and SQLite's LIKE ignores ASCII case. 
in IN (...) The value must be an array, otherwise 400. A list past the database's bound parameter limit (65,535 on PostgreSQL and MySQL, 32,766 on SQLite, 100 on D1, every list in the statement counted) is a 400, see bulk operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations#how-large-can-a-bulk-call-be). 
notIn NOT IN (...) The value must be an array, otherwise 400. 
between BETWEEN a AND b [from, to], both inclusive. Anything other than two values is a 400. Date strings are parsed. 
isNull IS NULL / IS NOT NULL true or "true" gives IS NULL, false or "false" gives IS NOT NULL. Anything else is a 400. 
isNotNull IS NOT NULL / IS NULL The mirror of isNull. 
startsWith / endsWith / contains LIKE 'x%', '%x', '%x%' Text columns and string values only. The value is escaped. Case-insensitive (ILIKE on PostgreSQL) unless sql.caseSensitive is true. On SQLite the case-sensitive forms are GLOB (since 3.7.2), since SQLite's LIKE ignores ASCII case. 
iStartsWith / iEndsWith / iContains ILIKE (PostgreSQL), LIKE (MySQL, SQLite) Always case-insensitive, whatever sql.caseSensitive says. Escaped like the plain forms. 
arrayContains @ PostgreSQL array columns: the column holds every value. { tags: { arrayContains: ["a", "b"] } }. 
arrayOverlaps && PostgreSQL array columns: the column holds at least one of the values. 
jsonContains @ '...'::jsonb PostgreSQL jsonb columns only (not json): { meta: { jsonContains: { plan: "pro" } } }.

A pattern operator on a column that is not text, an array operator on a column that is not an array, a jsonContains on a column that is not jsonb, or any of the three PostgreSQL operators on MySQL or SQLite is a 400 that says so. On MySQL the case-sensitive pattern forms still ignore case for the letters the default collations fold, because its LIKE does. On SQLite they match case exactly since 3.7.2: contains: "Ann" no longer matches ann. The like operator stays plain LIKE, which ignores ASCII case on SQLite.
Put them side by side: every top-level key is ANDed.

chunks.h: How do I OR two filters?
chunks.t:
Put them in an or array. and, or and not are group keys, and each member is a full filter object, so it can hold columns, relation filters, collection filters and more groups.

How the groups behave:

- and and or take an array of filter objects; not takes one filter object. Any other shape is a 400.
- Groups nest, work inside a relation filter ({ organization: { or: [{ name: "Acme" }, { name: "Globex" }] } }) and apply to count too.
- An or with an empty member matches every row, so the whole group adds nothing. An empty and member is skipped.
- A table column (or relation) named and, or or not wins over the group key.
- A filter may nest at most 32 objects deep. A deeper one is a 400, from a query string or from code.

NOT and a missing parent. 
A belongs-to filter inside not compares against a LEFT JOIN. A row whose parent is missing
has NULL there, and NOT (NULL = 'Acme') is not true, so
{ not: { organization: { name: "Acme" } } } also leaves out users with no organization. Add
{ or: [{ not:... }, { organizationId: { isNull: true } }] } if you want them.

chunks.h: How do I filter by a related column?
chunks.t:
Use the relation name as the key and a filter on the related table's columns as the value. You need a relation declared in the entity config (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations); a relation value that is not an object is a 400.

A top-level belongs-to is joined into the main query. A has-many or many-to-many relation becomes an IN (SELECT...) subquery, so a user with three matching posts still appears once and total stays right. With soft delete on, a soft-deleted related row never matches.

When the foreign key is all you need, filter on it directly: { organizationId: 42 } needs no relation at all.

chunks.h: Can I filter through several relations or quantify a collection?
chunks.t:
Yes. Nest the relation names to any depth, and use some, none or every on a has-many or many-to-many relation:

Both compile to EXISTS or NOT EXISTS subqueries, never joins that multiply rows. Filtering by relation in Drizzle (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relation-filters) covers paths, quantifiers and the SQL they produce.

c.s:
await this.users.findAll({ organization: { country: { code: "IN" } } });
await this.users.findAll({ posts: { none: { status: "draft" } } });

chunks.h: How do I add a search box to a list?
chunks.t:
Pass options.search to findAll or count. It searches a term across columns and composes with your filters, pagination, sorting, relation filters and the total count.

mode: "fullText" on MySQL or SQLite is a 400. For results ordered by relevance, call fullTextSearch() instead; full-text search in PostgreSQL (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/full-text-search) compares the two.

chunks.h: What happens with an unknown filter key?
chunks.t:
It is rejected with a 400 (BadRequestException, message Unknown filter column: <key ), the same as an unknown sortBy. Before 3.3.1 the key was dropped, so a typo such as { nmae: "x" } returned every row. The same rule covers a column inside a relation filter ({ organization: { nmae: "Acme" } }, reported as organization.nmae) and an unknown operator.

A key outside filterableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) is a 400 too, so a client can only filter on the columns you mean to expose.

chunks.h: How do I filter from a query string in a controller?
chunks.t: Hand the query to parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing). It splits off pagination, sort and options, coerces the values by column type and rejects unknown keys before any SQL runs.

chunks.h: How do filters work with pagination and sorting?
chunks.t: findAll takes three positional arguments: filters, pagination, options. The filters decide which rows match, and the pagination picks the page. See pagination and sorting (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting) for the full shape.

Is a string filter case-sensitive?. 
A bare string on a text column is not: it compiles to lower(column) = lower(value) while sql.caseSensitive is false, the default. The eq operator is a plain =, which is case-sensitive on PostgreSQL.

How do I do a partial or LIKE match?. 
Use startsWith, endsWith or contains, which escape %, _ and \ in your value. Use like or ilike when you want to write the pattern and its wildcards yourself.

What happens if I misspell a filter key?. 
The call fails with a 400 and the message Unknown filter column: <key. Unknown operators and unknown columns inside a relation filter are rejected the same way, so a typo never returns every row.

Can I OR two conditions?. 
Yes. Put each condition in an or array, as in { or: [{ role: "admin" }, { age: { gte: 30 } }] }. and and not work the same way, and groups nest.

Do array and JSON operators work on MySQL or SQLite?. 
No. arrayContains, arrayOverlaps and jsonContains are PostgreSQL only, and on MySQL or SQLite they are a 400 that says so.

Drizzle forFeature in NestJS binds each CRUD service to its table and merges per-entity config over the project defaults from forRoot, one level deep.

DrizzleCrudModule.forFeature(entities) is the Drizzle forFeature call for NestJS feature modules. It binds each CRUD service to its Drizzle table, builds the service with the project defaults from forRoot merged with any per-entity config, and exports it so your controllers can inject it. Call it once per feature module, with one entry per service.

Do not list the service in providers. 
forFeature already provides and exports the service. Adding it to the module's providers
makes Nest construct it a second time without the merged config, and startup fails. Services
are not @Injectable() for the same reason.

chunks.h: How do I register a service?
chunks.t:
Each entry is a CrudFeature:

Several services can share one call. Each becomes its own provider, built independently:

chunks.h: In what order do the config layers merge?
chunks.t:
Config reaches a service through three layers, and each one overrides the one before:

1. Project defaults. The forRoot or forRootAsync config, with defaults filled in for soft delete, timestamps, pagination and the sql flags.
2. Per entity. The @CrudService decorator metadata, then the config object from forFeature, then the injected db and the table.
3. Service construction. The service constructor spreads the result over its own built-in defaults and validates it.

softDelete, timestamps, pagination and sql merge one level deep at every layer, so an override names only what it changes. pagination: { defaultLimit: 5 } keeps the project's maxLimit, and sql: { caseSensitive: true } keeps useReturning. Every other key replaces the value below it. timestamps: undefined turns timestamps off for that entity.

When behaviour looks wrong, check which layer set the value before you look anywhere else.

chunks.h: What can I override per entity?
chunks.t: The type is CrudFeatureConfig. Defaults marked "project" come from forRoot:

chunks.h: What can I override per entity?
chunks.t:
