versionColumn: { type: "string", description: "An integer column for optimistic locking. A stale version is a 409." },
filterableColumns: { type: "string[]", description: "Columns a caller may filter by. Unset allows all." },
sortableColumns: { type: "string[]", description: "Columns a caller may sort by. Unset allows all." },
selectableColumns: { type: "string[]", description: "Columns a caller may select. Unset allows all." },
searchableColumns: { type: "string[]", description: "Columns search may look in. Unset allows all." },
loadableRelations: { type: "string[]", description: "Relations a caller may load or count. Unset allows all." },
writableColumns: { type: "string[]", description: "Columns create, update and upsert may write; any other column is a 400." },
writableRelations: { type: "string[]", description: "Relations a create body may write, and that attach, detach and sync may change." },
primaryKeyType: { type: "string", description: "Deprecated, no effect. The key type comes from the Drizzle column." },
}}
/

chunks.h: What can I override per entity?
chunks.t: Each of these has its own page: relations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations), multi-tenancy (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy) for scope, optimistic locking (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/optimistic-locking) for versionColumn, and allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) for the column lists.

chunks.h: Does a camelCase schema need extra config?
chunks.t:
Yes, when your keys differ from the defaults. Settings name the key in the Drizzle table object, not the database column. For deletedAt: timestamp('deleted_at') and friends:

The service checks these keys when it is built. A key that is not on the table stops the app with a message that names the right one, for example: softDelete.column is "deleted_at", but the table has no column under that key. The column "deleted_at" is declared under the key "deletedAt"; set softDelete.column to "deletedAt".

chunks.h: Can I put the config on the service class?
chunks.t:
Yes, with @CrudService. Its metadata is the first per-entity layer, so forFeature config wins where both set a key, and the forFeature table wins over the decorator's. The decorator's type asks for dialect, table and primaryKey:

The decorator keeps the config next to the service, and it lets ApiCrudList (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/openapi) and the controller factory's openapi: true read the table and allowlists from the class. For config that varies per module, keep it in forFeature, or in a shared constant you spread into both.

chunks.h: How do I check the merged config?
chunks.t: DRIZZLE_CRUD_CONFIG holds only the project layer: dialect, defaults, sql and hooks.enableGlobalHooks, with defaults filled in. It does not include per-entity overrides. The fully merged config of one entity lives on the service as the protected config property, which a test can read:

c.s:
const posts = moduleRef.get(PostsService);
expect((posts as any).config.pagination).toEqual({ defaultLimit: 5, maxLimit: 100 });

chunks.t:
Should I add the service to the module. 
No. forFeature provides and exports it. Listing it again makes Nest build a second instance without a config, which fails at startup.

Which wins, @CrudService or the forFeature config?. 
The forFeature config. The merge order is project defaults, then decorator metadata, then forFeature config, then the injected db and table.

Does a partial pagination override lose the project maxLimit?. 
No. softDelete, timestamps, pagination and sql merge one level deep, so pagination: { defaultLimit: 5 } keeps the project maxLimit.

How do I turn timestamps off for one entity?. 
Set timestamps: undefined in that entity's forFeature config. An explicit undefined replaces the project value.

Does DRIZZLE_CRUD_CONFIG include per-entity overrides?. 
No. It is the normalized project config only. Each service holds its own merged config.

Configure the NestJS Drizzle module with forRoot. Set the connection, dialect, soft delete, timestamps, pagination and SQL defaults once in AppModule.

DrizzleCrudModule.forRoot(config) sets up the NestJS Drizzle module once, in your AppModule. It takes the dialect and either a connection string or a Drizzle instance, plus project-wide defaults for soft delete, timestamps, pagination, SQL behaviour and write events. The module is global, so every feature module can inject the database and register services with forFeature.

Pass exactly one of connectionString or db. 
With neither, startup fails. When both are set, db wins and connectionString is ignored.
connectionString works for PostgreSQL and MySQL. On SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1, build
the Drizzle instance yourself and pass it as db.

Every option, with the default normalizeConfig fills in (drizzle-crud.module.ts (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/blob/main/packages/nestjs-drizzle-crud/src/modules/drizzle-crud.module.ts), types in drizzle-crud-config.interface.ts (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/blob/main/packages/nestjs-drizzle-crud/src/core/interfaces/drizzle-crud-config.interface.ts)):

c.s: DrizzleCrudModule.forRoot(config: DrizzleCrudConfig): DynamicModule

chunks.t:
", description: "Your Drizzle schema, passed to drizzle() when the module builds the connection from connectionString." },
"defaults.softDelete": { type: "boolean", default: "true", description: "Soft delete for every entity, on a deleted_at column. Turn it on or off per entity in forFeature." },
"defaults.timestamps": { type: "boolean", default: "true", description: "Stamp created_at and updated_at on writes. false turns them off unless an entity sets timestamps in forFeature." },
"defaults.pagination.defaultLimit": { type: "number", default: "20", description: "Rows per page when the caller sends no limit." },
"defaults.pagination.maxLimit": { type: "number", default: "100", description: "The highest limit a caller may ask for. Set one pagination key and the other keeps its default." },
"defaults.sortOrder": { type: '"asc" "desc"', description: "Opt in. Entities without a defaultSort order findAll by their createdAt column in this direction. Unset, findAll orders by the primary key." },
"sql.caseSensitive": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "false compares a bare string filter on a text column with lower() on both sides." },
"sql.useReturning": { type: "boolean", default: "true on PostgreSQL and SQLite, false on MySQL", description: "Read the written row back with RETURNING. MySQL has no RETURNING, so the service turns it off there and warns." },
"sql.jsonSupport": { type: "boolean", default: "true", description: "Deprecated, no effect. Removed in the next major version." },
"sql.enableFullTextSearch": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Deprecated, no effect. Full-text search works on PostgreSQL whatever this is set to." },
"hooks.enableGlobalHooks": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Every service raises a before and an after event for each write on the module's CrudEventBus." },
"hooks.subscribers": { type: "CrudSubscriber[]", default: "[]", description: "Subscribed to the bus when it is created. Called only with enableGlobalHooks: true; without it the module logs a warning." },
}}
/

chunks.h: How do I connect to PostgreSQL?
chunks.t:
Pass the connection string and your schema. The module imports the postgres driver, builds the Drizzle instance and closes the connection on shutdown:

The module opens the client with prepare: false, which keeps it working behind a transaction pooler such as PgBouncer. Shutdown runs in onModuleDestroy, so call app.enableShutdownHooks() in main.ts if you want the connection closed when the process gets a signal such as SIGTERM.

chunks.h: How do I connect to MySQL with a connection string?
chunks.t:
Since 3.7.0, pass dialect: 'mysql' and a mysql:// URL. The module loads mysql2 when it starts, builds a pool, wraps it with drizzle-orm/mysql2 and ends the pool on shutdown. mysql2 is an optional peer, so install it yourself:

With schema set, the module passes mode: 'default' to Drizzle, which is right for MySQL itself. For PlanetScale, build the instance yourself and pass it as db.

chunks.h: How do I set the pool size, SSL or idle timeout?
chunks.t:
Add connection next to connectionString. Each key goes to the driver under its own name, and a key you leave out keeps the driver's default:

Option postgres-js mysql2 
--- --- --- 
poolSize max connectionLimit 
idleTimeout (seconds) idle_timeout idleTimeout, in milliseconds, plus maxIdle one below the pool size 
ssl: true ssl: true ssl: {}, which mysql2 verifies by default 
ssl: {... } passed as is passed as is 
ssl: "require" and the other modes passed as is startup error 

mysql2 only closes idle connections when maxIdle is below connectionLimit, and maxIdle defaults to connectionLimit, so before 3.7.2 idleTimeout did nothing on MySQL. The module now sets maxIdle to the pool size minus one (9 with mysql2's default of 10) whenever you give idleTimeout. One consequence of how mysql2 works: when every connection in the pool is idle, it closes one of them within about a second, and the rest after idleTimeout. With poolSize: 1 the single connection closes about a second after it goes idle.

connection only applies to a connection the module builds. With db, configure the driver yourself. Anything else the driver takes, such as a statement timeout, also means building it yourself.

chunks.h: How do I pass my own Drizzle instance?
chunks.t:
Build it yourself and pass it as db. Use this for SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1, and on PostgreSQL or MySQL when you want a driver option connection does not cover. SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1 (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/sqlite) shows the SQLite setups.

When you pass db, the module does not close it on shutdown. That is your job, and it lets you share the same pool with migrations, raw queries and other Drizzle code.

The module is global, so these tokens are injectable anywhere after forRoot:

Token Value 
--- --- 
DRIZZLE_DB The Drizzle instance, built or passed in 
DRIZZLE_CRUD_CONFIG The normalized project config: dialect, defaults, sql and hooks.enableGlobalHooks, defaults filled in 
DRIZZLE_CONNECTION The connection manager that owns shutdown 
CrudEventBus The bus for write events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events); subscribe to it to react to writes

chunks.h: Which defaults should I change first?
chunks.t:
Two settings trip people up, and both fail loudly at startup since 3.3.1:

- Tables without created_at, updated_at or deleted_at. Set defaults: { softDelete: false, timestamps: false }, then turn them on per entity in forFeature (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-feature) where the columns exist.
- camelCase schema keys such as deletedAt: timestamp('deleted_at'). The settings name the key in your Drizzle table object, so set softDelete.column and the timestamps keys per entity. The startup error names the key to use.

caseSensitive: false applies lower() only to text columns (text, varchar, char). A string filter on an integer, uuid or enum column stays a plain =, so a query string value such as?author_id=1 works. For pattern matching, use the explicit like and ilike operators (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering).

chunks.h: When should I use forRootAsync instead?
chunks.t: When the config depends on another provider, typically ConfigService after env validation, or a secret you fetch at startup. forRootAsync (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-root-async) takes the same DrizzleCrudConfig, returned from a factory.

Can forRoot build a MySQL connection from a connection string?. 
Yes, since 3.7.0. With dialect: "mysql" the module builds a mysql2 pool from the URL and ends it on shutdown. Install mysql2 in your app.

Can forRoot open a SQLite or libSQL database from a URL?. 
No. On dialect: "sqlite" a connectionString is a startup error. Build the Drizzle instance with your driver and pass it as db.

Does the module close the database connection on shutdown?. 
Only when it built the connection from connectionString. A db you pass in is yours to close. Call app.enableShutdownHooks() so a signal triggers the shutdown.

What are the default page size and maximum limit?. 
defaultLimit is 20 and maxLimit is 100. Setting one of them keeps the other at its default.

How does findAll sort when no sortBy is passed?. 
By the entity's defaultSort if set, else by createdAt in the defaults.sortOrder direction if you set one, else by the primary key. The primary key is always the last tiebreaker.

Is hooks.enableGlobalHooks deprecated?. 
No. Since 3.5.0 it turns on module-level write events on the CrudEventBus. Per-service hooks run whether it is on or off.

NestJS Drizzle forRootAsync with ConfigService builds the database config at startup, from useFactory, useClass or useExisting and any provider you inject.

DrizzleCrudModule.forRootAsync({ imports, inject, useFactory }) is the async form of forRoot for NestJS Drizzle apps that read their config from ConfigService. Nest calls your useFactory at startup with the providers listed in inject, and the object it returns (or resolves to) is the same DrizzleCrudConfig that forRoot (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-root) takes, with the same defaults filled in. Since 3.7.0 it also takes useClass or useExisting, the usual Nest way to build options from a class.

Give exactly one of useFactory, useClass or useExisting. 
With none of them, or with more than one, forRootAsync throws when the module is declared,
and the message names what it got. Before 3.7.2 useFactory silently won over the other two.

config", description: "Returns a DrizzleCrudConfig, or a promise of one. Receives the providers in inject, in the same order." },
useClass: { type: "Type ", description: "A class the module registers and instantiates, then asks for the config with createDrizzleCrudOptions(). Its constructor can inject any provider in scope." },
useExisting: { type: "Type ", description: "A provider that already exists, usually exported by a module in imports. The module calls its createDrizzleCrudOptions() and does not create a second instance." },
inject: { type: "any[]", default: "[]", description: "Providers to pass to useFactory, such as ConfigService. Not used with useClass or useExisting." },
imports: { type: "any[]", default: "[]", description: "Modules that export the injected providers. Not needed for a global module such as ConfigModule with isGlobal: true." },
}}
/ 

The module is global, exactly like forRoot, and exports the same tokens (DRIZZLE_DB, DRIZZLE_CRUD_CONFIG, DRIZZLE_CONNECTION, CrudEventBus).

chunks.h: How do I read the config from ConfigService?
chunks.t:
Install @nestjs/config.

Inject ConfigService into the factory. getOrThrow stops startup with a clear error when the variable is missing, instead of failing later on the first query.
getOrThrow stops startup with a clear error when the variable is missing, instead of failing later on the first query.

chunks.h: How do I build my own Drizzle instance in the factory?
chunks.t:
Return db instead of connectionString. Use this on SQLite, libSQL and D1, or for a driver option that connection (pool size, SSL, idle timeout) does not cover:

A db you pass in is yours: the module does not close it on shutdown. Only a connection the module built from connectionString is closed for you.

Yes. Return a promise when you fetch a value at startup, for example a password from a secrets manager:

SecretsModule and SecretsService stand for your own module. Nest waits for the promise before it builds any service, so a rejected promise stops startup.

chunks.h: How do I use a config class with useClass?
chunks.t:
Implement DrizzleCrudOptionsFactory and pass the class as useClass. The module registers it, injects its constructor and calls createDrizzleCrudOptions():

ConfigService resolves here because ConfigModule is global. For a provider from a module that is not global, add that module to imports.

chunks.h: How do I reuse a provider with useExisting?
chunks.t: When the config class is already a provider in another module, export it from there and pass useExisting. The module asks that instance for the config instead of creating its own:

chunks.h: When should I use forRoot instead?
chunks.t:
Use forRoot (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-root) when the config is a plain object you can build when the module file loads. Use forRootAsync when any of these hold:

- The connection string goes through ConfigService and its validation.
- The Drizzle instance is built from config values, such as the pool size.
- The config depends on another provider: feature flags, a secrets manager, a tenant registry.

Does forRootAsync support useClass or useExisting?. 
Yes, since 3.7.0. The class implements DrizzleCrudOptionsFactory and returns the config from createDrizzleCrudOptions(). useClass creates the instance, useExisting reuses one exported by a module in imports.

Do I need imports: [ConfigModule] when ConfigModule is global?. 
No. With isGlobal: true, ConfigService resolves without it. Listing it does no harm.

Can useFactory return a promise?. 
Yes. Nest waits for it before building the connection and the services, and a rejection stops startup.

Are the defaults the same as forRoot?. 
Yes. The object your factory returns goes through the same normalization, so soft delete, timestamps, pagination and the sql flags get the same defaults.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.h: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Drizzle full text search on Postgres in NestJS: fullTextSearch() ranks with ts_rank, takes filters and relations, a language and websearch queries.

For Drizzle full text search on PostgreSQL in NestJS, call fullTextSearch(term, columns, pagination, options) on any service that extends SqlBaseCrudService. By default it matches to_tsvector('english',...) across the columns you name against plainto_tsquery('english', term), orders the rows by ts_rank, and returns the same { data, total, page, limit } envelope as findAll. Since 3.7.0 the options take filters, relations, column selection, another text search configuration and search engine style queries. It works on PostgreSQL only and needs no flag to turn on.

PostgreSQL only. 
Full-text search uses PostgreSQL's tsvector and tsquery types. On MySQL and SQLite the
method throws a 400 BadRequestException (Full-text search only supported in PostgreSQL).

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I run a full-text search?
chunks.t:
Pass the term, the columns to search and, optionally, the page you want:

The envelope always reports the page and limit that were used. Before 3.3.1 an omitted pagination returned every match while the envelope said limit: 20. The data and count queries run together in one Promise.all.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.t:
The columns go into a Drizzle sql template as bound column references, joined with. With more than one column, each is wrapped in coalesce(column, '') (since 3.7.2):

What that means for results:

c.s:
select * from users
where to_tsvector('english', coalesce("name", '')) || to_tsvector('english', coalesce("email", '')) || to_tsvector('english', coalesce("bio", ''))
  @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
  and "deleted_at" is null
order by ts_rank(<same tsvector>, plainto_tsquery('english', $1)) desc, "id" asc
limit 20 offset 0

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.t:
- A NULL column contributes nothing to the vector, so a row still matches on its other columns. Before 3.7.2 the vector was to_tsvector(a) to_tsvector(b) without coalesce, and since x NULL is NULL, a row with any NULL column never matched.
- A single column stays to_tsvector('english', "bio"), without coalesce, so an index on that expression keeps matching.
- A column that already is a tsvector (a generated, stored column) goes in as is, with no to_tsvector around it, since 3.8.0. Next to other columns it is coalesce("search", ''::tsvector).
- The text search configuration is 'english' unless you pass language. The name is written into the SQL as a literal, not as a bound parameter, so an index on to_tsvector('german',...) still matches. That is why it has to pass the identifier check first.
- Rows are ordered by ts_rank descending, then by the primary key ascending, so rows with the same rank keep a stable order across pages.
- With soft delete on, soft-deleted rows are left out of both data and total, as in findAll and count. A tenant scope applies the same way, and so do options.filters.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I search within filters and load relations?
chunks.t:
Pass filters, relations and select in the options. They work exactly as they do on findAll: filters narrow the matches before they are ranked and counted, a belongs-to relation is joined, collections are loaded in one batched query, and select narrows the columns:

Before 3.7.0 the options only carried the transaction and the soft delete flags; filters, relations and select were ignored.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I search in another language or with search engine syntax?
chunks.t:
Set language to the text search configuration and queryMode to "websearch":

queryMode Function post -1 reads as 
--- --- --- 
"plain" (default) plainto_tsquery every word required; -1 is just a number 
"websearch" websearch_to_tsquery post and not 1; quotes make a phrase, or an alternative 

Neither mode raises a syntax error on odd input, so both are safe for a search box. A configuration that does not exist in the database (language: "klingon") passes the identifier check and fails in PostgreSQL, so check the name in your code if it comes from a client.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.h: Do I need to enable it or add an index?
chunks.t:
You do not need to enable it. fullTextSearch() works on any PostgreSQL entity, and the sql.enableFullTextSearch flag is deprecated and has no effect.

An index is your call, and it matters on large tables. Without one, PostgreSQL computes to_tsvector for every row on every search. There are two ways to give it one: a GIN index on the exact expression the query uses, or a stored tsvector column with a GIN index on the column.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.h: Option 1: a GIN index on the expression
chunks.t:
PostgreSQL only uses an expression index whose expression is exactly the one in the query, so repeat the generated vector, in the same column order as your columns array:

An index built on several columns before 3.7.2, without coalesce, no longer matches the query; recreate it as above. Pass language and the index needs the same configuration name.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Compute the vector once per write in a generated column, index the column, and search on it. The service sees that the column is a tsvector and uses it as is, so the index matches whatever the column order or configuration:

On 200,000 rows on PGlite, a search on a stored column with its GIN index took 0.6 ms, against 600 to 900 ms computing to_tsvector per row without an index. Before 3.8.0 a tsvector column failed with function to_tsvector(unknown, tsvector) does not exist. The Drizzle guide to full-text search (https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/guides/postgresql-full-text-search) shows both options on the schema side, and Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/indexes) covers pg_trgm for the default ilike search.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I add search to a filtered list endpoint?
chunks.t:
Use options.search with mode: "fullText" on findAll or count. The match then composes with your structured filters, pagination, sorting, relation filters and the total count. language and queryMode work there too:

The two differ in a few ways:

fullTextSearch() findAll with search.mode: "fullText" 
--- --- --- 
Order ts_rank, strongest match first Your sortBy, not ranked 
Structured filters Yes, in options.filters (since 3.7.0) Yes, plus relation filters 
Unknown column name 400 Skipped 
Empty term Matches no rows Adds no condition 
language, queryMode Yes Yes 
Dialect PostgreSQL only PostgreSQL only 

Use fullTextSearch() when relevance should drive the order. Use findAll(...,..., { search }) when search is one more filter on a normal list. Filtering with Drizzle in NestJS (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering#how-do-i-add-a-search-box-to-a-list) lists every search option.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.t:
- No highlighting. ts_headline is not generated.
- One configuration per call. Rows in different languages need one call per language, or a custom query.
- No raw tsquery or prefix queries. to_tsquery (with: prefixes) and phraseto_tsquery need a custom method. websearch covers phrases, or and negation.
- No MySQL or SQLite. MySQL has MATCH... AGAINST and SQLite has FTS5, but the package generates neither.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.h: How do I write a custom full-text query?
chunks.t:
Drop down to Drizzle in a method on your service. The injected database is this.config.db:

A custom query skips what the service adds for you: add isNull(users.deletedAt) and any tenant condition yourself.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle
chunks.t:
Does fullTextSearch work on MySQL or SQLite?. 
No. It is PostgreSQL only and is a 400 on any other dialect. Use options.search in its default ilike mode for a portable substring search.

Can I change the text search language?. 
Yes, since 3.7.0. Pass language: "german" (or any configuration name, optionally schema qualified) in the options of fullTextSearch or in search on findAll. A name that is not a plain identifier is a 400.

Can fullTextSearch filter and load relations?. 
Yes, since 3.7.0. options.filters takes the same filters as findAll, and relations, select and counts shape the rows as they do there.

Are results ranked?. 
fullTextSearch() orders by ts_rank descending, then by the primary key. findAll with search.mode: "fullText" filters on the same match but keeps your own sort.

Does full-text search return soft-deleted rows?. 
No. With soft delete on, they are left out of both data and total unless you pass withDeleted or onlyDeleted in the options.

chunks.p: Full-text search in PostgreSQL with Drizzle

chunks.t:
Get help with nestjs-drizzle-crud. Ask in GitHub Discussions, report bugs as issues, report security issues privately, and include what to send.

To get help with nestjs-drizzle-crud, ask usage questions in GitHub Discussions, report a bug you can reproduce as a GitHub issue, and report a security vulnerability privately through a GitHub security advisory. A report that includes the package version, the table definition, the entity config and the exact call gets answered fastest.

Never report a vulnerability in public. 
Do not put a security problem in an issue, a discussion or a pull request. Use the private
advisory form described under the security question below, which only the maintainers can see.

Pick the channel by what you need; each one is watched.

You want to Go to 
--- --- 
Ask how to do something GitHub Discussions (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/discussions) 
Report a bug you can reproduce GitHub issues, bug report template 
Request a feature GitHub issues, feature request template 
Report a security vulnerability A private security advisory (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/security/advisories/new) 
Contribute code CONTRIBUTING.md (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) 
Fund the work Sponsor nestjs-drizzle-crud (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/sponsor) 

Blank issues are turned off, so every issue starts from the bug report or feature request template.

chunks.h: What should a bug report include?
chunks.t:
A report with a reproduction usually gets fixed in one round trip. The bug report template asks for most of this; fill in all of it:

1. The nestjs-drizzle-crud version, the dialect, and your Node, NestJS and Drizzle versions.
2. The Drizzle table definition for the entity, trimmed to the relevant columns.
3. The forRoot and forFeature config for that entity.
4. The call you made and what came back, including the exception class and HTTP status.
5. The SQL, if you have it. Drizzle logging (drizzle(client, { logger: true })) prints the statement the service built.
6. The stack trace, if there is one.

Search the existing issues first; the template asks you to confirm the bug is not a duplicate.

chunks.h: How do I report a security vulnerability?
chunks.t:
Report it privately through GitHub's security advisory form (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/security/advisories/new), as the security policy (https://github.com/avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/blob/main/SECURITY.md) says. Include:

- What the vulnerability is and what an attacker could do with it.
- Steps to reproduce, ideally a minimal proof of concept.
- The affected version or versions.

The maintainers acknowledge reports within 72 hours, work with you on a fix and agree a disclosure date. Reporters are credited in the advisory unless they prefer otherwise.

Question Answer 
--- --- 
What is in scope? The published npm package, packages/nestjs-drizzle-crud. 
What is out of scope? apps/api and apps/docs, the private example app and this docs site. Report problems there as normal issues. 
Which versions get security fixes? 3.x. Versions before 3.0 do not.

Community help stays free. If you want the package integrated, a migration done, a feature built or your services reviewed on your own schedule, see commercial support and custom development (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/commercial-support).

Why does findAll return an object instead of an array?. 
findAll returns { data, total, page, limit } because every list is paginated. total comes from a count query with the same filters and search, so it stays correct as you page.

Why is my like filter not matching anything?. 
like and ilike use the wildcards you supply, so { name: { ilike: "jo" } } only matches jo. Write { name: { ilike: "jo%" } }, or use startsWith, which adds and escapes the wildcard for you.

Why does my service fail at startup with a missing column?. 
Soft delete and timestamps are on by default and expect deleted_at, created_at and updated_at. Turn them off with defaults: { softDelete: false, timestamps: false }, or point them at your column keys.

Do I need to inject the database into my service?. 
No. forFeature builds the service and hands it the config, Drizzle instance included. Adding @Injectable() or an @Inject(DRIZZLE_DB) constructor breaks that registration.

Does it work with MySQL?. 
Yes. Pass a mysql:// connection string or your own Drizzle MySQL instance as db, and the package reads written rows back because MySQL has no RETURNING. Full-text search and the array and JSON operators are PostgreSQL only.

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.h: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.t:
Add Drizzle hooks and validation to a NestJS service by overriding validateCreate, beforeCreate, afterUpdate and the DTO mappers on SqlBaseCrudService.

Drizzle hooks and validation in a NestJS service built on SqlBaseCrudService are protected methods you override in your subclass: validateCreate and validateUpdate reject bad input, beforeCreate and beforeUpdate can rewrite it, the two mappers turn a DTO into the row to store, and the after hooks run once the row is written. Each one is optional and defaults to a no-op or a pass-through.

A before hook must return the data. 
beforeCreate and beforeUpdate return the DTO the write continues with. If yours returns nothing, the mapper receives undefined and the write loses every column from the body (an update then fails with a 400, nothing to update). Always end with return data (or a new object).

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.h: In what order do the hooks run?
chunks.t:
Validation first, then the before hook, then the mapper, then the SQL, then the after hook:

update runs the same chain with validateUpdate, beforeUpdate, mapUpdateDtoToEntity and afterUpdate, after it has checked that the row exists (a missing row is a 404 before any hook runs). upsert starts as an insert, so it runs validateCreate, beforeCreate and mapCreateDtoToEntity, but no after hook.

c.s:
validateCreate(data)
  -> beforeCreate(data)          skipped by hooks.skipBefore
  -> mapCreateDtoToEntity(data)
  -> INSERT
  -> afterCreate(row)            skipped by hooks.skipAfter

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.t:
Override validateCreate or validateUpdate and throw. Any throw aborts the write before the SQL runs:

ValidationFailedException is a 400 with the message Validation failed: email is not an address. Any Nest HttpException you throw keeps its own status. In a mass method, the throw for each item is collected into a BulkOperationException (400) that lists the failing items.

Validation always runs: hooks.skipBefore skips the before hooks, not validateCreate or validateUpdate. Keep it to checks on the input itself, and put heavier async work (a lookup in another table) in beforeCreate or beforeUpdate.

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.h: How do I map a DTO to a row?
chunks.t:
Override mapCreateDtoToEntity or mapUpdateDtoToEntity. Both run after the before hook and return the object to write. The defaults return a shallow copy of the input:

Mappers are the right place to:

- normalize input (lowercase emails, trim whitespace),
- set fields the caller cannot control (status: "pending", createdBy),
- strip fields the DTO allows but the table does not have.

What the mapper returns still goes through writableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists#which-columns-can-a-body-write-by-default), so a column it adds must be on that list when the list is set. Timestamps, the version column and the tenant scope (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy) are applied after the mapper.

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.h: How do I run code before or after a write?
chunks.t:
Override the before and after pair for that write. afterCreate, afterUpdate and afterRestore receive the stored row; the delete and soft delete hooks receive the id:

A before hook that throws stops the write. An after hook runs after the SQL, so a throw there only undoes the write when the call runs in a transaction (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/transactions): every mass method does, a single write does when you pass options.transaction.

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.h: Do after hooks run inside the transaction?
chunks.t:
It depends on the method:

Call Where the after hooks run A throw in an after hook 
--- --- --- 
create, update, softDelete, restore, delete without options.transaction After the statement has committed (a nested create commits its own transaction first) Reaches the caller; the row stays written 
Any single write with options.transaction Inside your transaction Rolls everything back when you let it propagate 
massCreate, massUpdate, massSoftDelete, massRestore, massDelete Inside the mass write's transaction, once per row Rolls the whole batch back 

Module-level events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events) follow the same split: a single write raises its after event once the row is written, a mass write raises one before and one after event from inside its transaction. Wrap a single write in a transaction when its after hook must be atomic with it.

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.h: How do I skip the hooks for one call?
chunks.t:
Pass options.hooks:

This suits migrations and admin scripts. Skipping hooks does not skip the module-level CRUD events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events), which follow skipEvents instead, so an audit trail built on them is not lost by accident.

c.s: await users.create(dto, { hooks: { skipBefore: true, skipAfter: true } });

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.h: Should I use hooks or events?
chunks.t: Hooks for logic that belongs to one entity, events for logic that spans all of them. Hooks are protected methods on one service and run per row, even in a mass call. CRUD events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events) (hooks.enableGlobalHooks) fire on one module-level bus for every entity, once per call, which suits audit trails and cache busting. When both are set up, both run.

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.t:
Hook Receives Returns Runs on 
--- --- --- --- 
validateCreate(data) CreateDto void, or throws create, upsert, and per item in massCreate, massUpsert 
validateUpdate(id, data) id, UpdateDto void, or throws update, and per id in massUpdate 
beforeCreate(data) CreateDto the CreateDto to continue with create, upsert, and per item in massCreate, massUpsert 
mapCreateDtoToEntity(data) CreateDto Record<string, any create, upsert, and per item in massCreate, massUpsert 
afterCreate(row) T void create, and per row in massCreate 
beforeUpdate(id, data) id, UpdateDto the UpdateDto to continue with update, and per id in massUpdate 
mapUpdateDtoToEntity(data) UpdateDto Record<string, any update, and per id in massUpdate 
afterUpdate(row) T void update, and per row in massUpdate 
beforeDelete(id) id void delete, forceDelete, and per id in massDelete, massForceDelete 
afterDelete(id) id void delete, forceDelete, and per id in massDelete, massForceDelete 
beforeSoftDelete(id) id void softDelete, and per id in massSoftDelete 
afterSoftDelete(id) id void softDelete, and per id in massSoftDelete 
beforeRestore(id) id void restore, and per id in massRestore 
afterRestore(row) T void restore, and per row in massRestore

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.t: All hooks are protected, so code outside the class cannot call them. Override them in your service subclass.

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
chunks.t:
Does validateCreate run when I pass skipBefore?. 
Yes. hooks.skipBefore skips only the before hooks. validateCreate and validateUpdate run on every create and update.

Does beforeCreate run before or after the mapper?. 
Before. The order is validateCreate, then beforeCreate, then mapCreateDtoToEntity, then the insert, so the mapper sees whatever beforeCreate returned.

Do hooks run per row in a mass update?. 
Yes. massUpdate runs validateUpdate, beforeUpdate and the mapper for each id and afterUpdate for each row, even though the update itself is one statement.

Can a throw in afterUpdate undo the update?. 
Only inside a transaction. A mass write runs its after hooks inside its own transaction, so a throw rolls the batch back. A single update without options.transaction has already committed when afterUpdate runs, so the throw reaches the caller and the row stays updated.

Does upsert run afterCreate?. 
No. upsert and massUpsert run validateCreate, beforeCreate and mapCreateDtoToEntity, but no after hook. Use the afterUpsert event if you need to react to one.

chunks.p: Drizzle hooks and validation in NestJS
Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.t:
Which PostgreSQL indexes nestjs-drizzle-crud queries use: lower() equality, cursor pages, full-text search, pg_trgm contains, relation keys and tenants.

The package never creates indexes for you, so each query shape it sends needs one that fits. The default case-insensitive filter needs an index on lower(column), cursor pages need one on the sort columns plus the primary key, full-text search needs a GIN index, contains needs pg_trgm, and relation loaders need indexes on foreign keys and join-table columns. A tenant column goes first in a composite index.

Measured on 200,000 rows. 
On PGlite (PostgreSQL 18 in WASM) with 200,000 posts: findAll({ title }) took 64 ms without an index that fits and 0.3 ms with one on lower(title). Cursor page 9,000 took 0.6 ms with an index on (created_at, id). A list without its COUNT( ) took 0.6 ms instead of 23 ms. Read the numbers as ratios; a real server is faster across the board.

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: Which index does each query need?
chunks.t: Find the call you make, then create the index next to it. Every example is PostgreSQL; the migration (https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/migrations) that holds them is yours.

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: Which index does each query need?
chunks.t:
Call SQL the package sends Index 
--- --- --- 
findAll({ email: "A@x.io" }), count,?email= on a text column lower(email) = lower($1) (lower(email)), or a citext column, or caseSensitive: true and (email) 
findOne({ email }), { email: { eq } } email = $1 (email) 
findByCursor with sortBy: '-created_at' created_at <= $1 AND (...), ORDER BY created_at DESC, id (created_at DESC, id) 
findAll with sortBy and a page ORDER BY views, id LIMIT... OFFSET... (views, id) 
fullTextSearch(term, ['title', 'body']) to_tsvector(...) \ \ to_tsvector(...) @@... GIN on that expression, or a stored tsvector column 
{ title: { contains: "sql" } }, options.search title ILIKE '%sql%' GIN (title gin_trgm_ops) from pg_trgm 
relations: ['comments'] (has-many), counts WHERE post_id IN (...) (post_id) on the child table 
relations: ['tags'] (many-to-many) join table WHERE post_id IN (...) both (post_id) and (tag_id) on the join table 
any read with soft delete on... AND deleted_at IS NULL add WHERE deleted_at IS NULL to the indexes above 
any read on a scoped entity tenant_id = $1 AND... put tenant_id first in the indexes above

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: Which index does a case-insensitive filter need?
chunks.t:
An index on lower(column). While sql.caseSensitive is false, the default, a bare string on a text column compiles to lower(column) = lower($1) in findAll, count, countBy and?column= over HTTP, and a plain index on the column cannot serve it:

Two other ways get the same effect:

- A citext column. Declare the column as citext (with a Drizzle customType). The package only wraps text, varchar and char columns in lower(), so it sends a plain =, which citext already compares without case, and a normal index on the column works.
- sql.caseSensitive: true. Equality is then a plain = everywhere and a plain index works, but jo@x.io no longer matches Jo@x.io.

findOne and findAll differ on case. 
findOne({ email: "A@X.IO" }) compiles to email = $1 and is case-sensitive, whatever sql.caseSensitive says. findAll({ email: "A@X.IO" }) compiles to lower(email) = lower($1) and is not. So with the default setting findOne can return null for a row that findAll finds. Pass the stored case to findOne, or use findAll({ email }, { limit: 1 }) when case must not matter. An eq operator ({ email: { eq: "A@X.IO" } }) is a plain = in both. Both index shapes above are worth having if you call both.

c.s: CREATE INDEX users_email_lower ON users (lower(email));

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: Which index makes cursor pages fast?
chunks.t:
One on the sort columns followed by the primary key, in the order of sortBy. Each page starts with a bound on the first sort column, so the database seeks to the cursor instead of reading every row before it:

The primary key always comes last and always sorts ascending. An index on (created_at, id) serves the bound of a descending page too; (created_at DESC, id) also matches its ORDER BY exactly. The same index serves offset pages with that sort, up to the OFFSET itself, which still reads every skipped row. See cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination) for the query.

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: Which index does full-text search use?
chunks.t: A GIN index on exactly the vector the query builds, or on a stored tsvector column. Full-text search (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/full-text-search) shows both shapes:

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: How do I speed up contains and search?
chunks.t:
With a trigram index from the pg_trgm extension. contains, startsWith, endsWith, their i forms and options.search compile to ILIKE '%term%' (or LIKE), which a btree index cannot serve, so without one PostgreSQL reads the whole table:

One trigram index per searched column. A search over ['title', 'body'] is title ILIKE... OR body ILIKE..., which PostgreSQL answers with both indexes combined.

c.s:
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE INDEX posts_title_trgm ON posts USING gin (title gin_trgm_ops);

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.t:
The keys the batched loaders look up. PostgreSQL indexes a primary key and a unique constraint, but not a foreign key, so add these yourself:

A belongs-to (posts.author) looks up the referenced primary key, which is indexed already. A relation filter ({ comments: { some: {... } } }) and options.counts use the same foreign key as the loader.

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: Should my indexes skip soft-deleted rows?
chunks.t:
Yes, when most reads leave the trash out. Every read adds deleted_at IS NULL while soft delete is on, so a partial index with the same predicate is smaller and still matches:

A trash view (onlyDeleted: true) then needs its own index, or reads the table.

c.s:
CREATE INDEX posts_live_created_id ON posts (created_at DESC, id)
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: How do I index a multi-tenant table?
chunks.t: Put the tenant column first. A scoped entity (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy) adds tenant_id = $1 to every read, count and write, so each index above works best with the scope columns in front:

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.h: When should I turn off the count or use the cursor?
chunks.t:
On a large table, when nobody needs the total. findAll runs a COUNT( ) next to every page, and on 200,000 rows that count was 97% of the call. Two ways out:

- withCount: false (?withCount=false). total is null and hasMore says whether a next page exists. See pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting#how-do-i-skip-the-count-query).
- findByCursor, which skips the count unless you pass count: true, and whose deep pages stay as fast as the first with the index above. Use it for infinite scroll, exports and sync jobs.

Keep the count for a table that shows page numbers and a total, and give its filters an index so the count can use it.

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries
chunks.t:
Does nestjs-drizzle-crud create indexes for me?. 
No. Indexes live in your Drizzle schema or migrations. This page lists the ones the generated SQL can use.

Why is my filter on an indexed text column slow?. 
A bare string filter on a text column compiles to lower(column) = lower($1) while sql.caseSensitive is false, and a plain index on the column cannot serve that. Add an index on lower(column), use a citext column, or set caseSensitive: true.

Is findOne case-sensitive?. 
Yes. findOne compiles a string to a plain =, while findAll, count and?column= use lower() on text columns by default. Use findAll with limit: 1 when case must not matter.

Which index do cursor pages need?. 
One on the sort columns followed by the primary key, such as (created_at DESC, id) for sortBy: '-created_at'. Each page then seeks to the cursor, so page 9,000 costs about the same as page 1.

Do I need an index for has-many relations?. 
Yes, on the foreign key of the child table. PostgreSQL does not index foreign keys on its own, and the loader looks children up by that key.

chunks.p: Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries

chunks.t:
Set up NestJS with Drizzle ORM. Install nestjs-drizzle-crud with its four peers, then the driver for PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite.

To use NestJS with Drizzle ORM through nestjs-drizzle-crud, install the package and its four
required peers: @nestjs/common, @nestjs/core, drizzle-orm and reflect-metadata. Then add
a database driver. On PostgreSQL that is postgres and on MySQL mysql2 if you let the module
open the connection; on SQLite you install your driver, such as @libsql/client, and pass a
Drizzle instance you built. The package itself has no runtime dependencies.

Before you start. 
You need Node 20 or later and a NestJS 10 or later project with decorators turned on. The
documented version is, published as @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud on npm.

Renamed to @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud. 
From 3.5.1 the package is published under the @avytrix scope. The unscoped
nestjs-drizzle-crud name is deprecated on npm and points to the new one. To move, change the
dependency and the imports; nothing else changes. See
how to switch to the scoped package.

Install the package and its required peers. A NestJS project already has @nestjs/common, @nestjs/core and reflect-metadata, so in
practice you add the package and drizzle-orm.

Add the driver for your database. For PostgreSQL with a connection string, install postgres (postgres.js):

For MySQL, install mysql2. The module builds a pool from a connection string with it, or you
build the Drizzle instance yourself:

For SQLite or libSQL (Turso), install @libsql/client and build the Drizzle instance yourself.
SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1 (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/sqlite) covers the other SQLite drivers.

If you build a PostgreSQL Drizzle instance yourself (node-postgres, PGlite, Neon), install that
driver instead and skip postgres. Which driver do I need? explains
the choice.

Turn on decorators. NestJS reads constructor types through decorator metadata, and the package reads per-service
config from the @CrudService decorator. A project made with the Nest CLI already has both flags.

Add OpenAPI support, if you want it. ApiCrudQuery and ApiCrudList document list routes in Swagger. They need @nestjs/swagger,
which the package loads only the first time one of them runs.

chunks.t:
A NestJS project already has @nestjs/common, @nestjs/core and reflect-metadata, so in
practice you add the package and drizzle-orm.

chunks.h: Add the driver for your database
chunks.t:
For PostgreSQL with a connection string, install postgres (postgres.js):

For MySQL, install mysql2. The module builds a pool from a connection string with it, or you
build the Drizzle instance yourself:

For SQLite or libSQL (Turso), install @libsql/client and build the Drizzle instance yourself.
SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1 (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/sqlite) covers the other SQLite drivers.

If you build a PostgreSQL Drizzle instance yourself (node-postgres, PGlite, Neon), install that
driver instead and skip postgres. Which driver do I need? explains
the choice.

NestJS reads constructor types through decorator metadata, and the package reads per-service
config from the @CrudService decorator. A project made with the Nest CLI already has both flags.

chunks.h: Add OpenAPI support, if you want it
chunks.t:
ApiCrudQuery and ApiCrudList document list routes in Swagger. They need @nestjs/swagger,
which the package loads only the first time one of them runs.

chunks.h: Which peer dependencies does it need?
chunks.t:
Four peers are required and two are optional. These ranges come from the package's
peerDependencies:

Package Version range Needed when 
--- --- --- 
@nestjs/common =10.0.0 Always 
@nestjs/core =10.0.0 Always 
drizzle-orm =0.28.0 <1.0.0 Always 
reflect-metadata ^0.1.13 \ \ ^0.2.0 Always 
postgres =3.0.0 (optional) You pass connectionString with dialect: "postgresql" 
mysql2 =3.0.0 (optional) You pass connectionString with dialect: "mysql" 
@nestjs/swagger =7.0.0 (optional) You use ApiCrudQuery or ApiCrudList 

A SQLite driver is never a peer: the module does not open SQLite connections, so the driver is
your app's own dependency.

It depends on who builds the connection: let the module build it from a connection string
(PostgreSQL and MySQL), or build a Drizzle instance yourself and pass it as db (any dialect).

The module creates a postgres.js client, wraps it with drizzle-orm/postgres-js, and closes it
when the app shuts down. Install postgres.

Build the Drizzle instance with any PostgreSQL driver and pass it as db. The module uses it as
is and leaves closing it to you. postgres is not needed unless that is the driver you chose.

Pass a mysql:// connection string and the module builds a mysql2 pool, wraps it with
drizzle-orm/mysql2 and ends it on shutdown. Install mysql2. MySQL has no RETURNING, so the
package reads written rows back with a SELECT instead.

To build the pool yourself instead, pass db: drizzle(mysql.createPool(...)).

The module does not open SQLite connections, so build the Drizzle instance with your driver and
pass it as db. libSQL works for a local file and for Turso.

connectionString without the driver. 
postgres is an optional peer, so neither npm nor pnpm installs it for you. If you pass
connectionString and it is missing, the app fails at startup when the module imports it.
Install it, or pass your own db.

To read the connection settings from ConfigService instead of process.env, use
forRootAsync (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-root-async). Every forRoot option is on the
forRoot page (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/for-root).

chunks.h: How do I switch to the scoped package?
chunks.t:
Replace the dependency, then the import paths. The API, the config and the behaviour are the
same; only the name changed.

If you copied the agent rules templates or point an MCP client at the package, update those
paths too: node_modules/@avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud/AGENT.md, and
npx -p @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud nestjs-drizzle-crud-mcp for the MCP server. See
AI agents and MCP (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/ai-agents).

c.s:
pnpm remove nestjs-drizzle-crud
pnpm add @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud

chunks.t:
The package follows semver:

- Patch releases fix bugs and do not change the API.
- Minor releases add methods or options and stay backwards compatible.
- Major releases may change or remove public API, such as the deprecated exceptions and
config flags marked for removal.

The changelog (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/changelog) lists what changed in each release. The npm tarball ships the
same CHANGELOG.md.

Is nestjs-drizzle-crud the same package as @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud?. 
Yes. From 3.5.1 the package is published as @avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud and the unscoped name is deprecated. Change the dependency and the imports; nothing else changes.

Which version of drizzle-orm does nestjs-drizzle-crud support?. 
Any drizzle-orm from 0.28.0 up to, but not including, 1.0.0, as declared in the package's peer dependencies.

Do I need the postgres package?. 
Only when you pass connectionString with dialect: "postgresql". If you build the Drizzle instance yourself and pass it as db, install whichever driver you used instead.

Can the module open a MySQL connection from a connection string?. 
Yes, since 3.7.0. With dialect: "mysql" it builds a mysql2 pool from the URL. Install mysql2, which is an optional peer.

Which SQLite driver should I use?. 
libSQL (@libsql/client), for a local file or Turso. It is the driver the package is tested on, and it supports the bulk writes. Cloudflare D1 and synchronous drivers such as better-sqlite3 run the single-row methods only.

Does nestjs-drizzle-crud work with NestJS 10 and 11?. 
Yes. The peer range for @nestjs/common and @nestjs/core is 10.0.0 and later, and the example app in the repository runs on NestJS 11.

A condensed fact sheet of nestjs-drizzle-crud for AI coding agents, with setup, generics, return shapes, filters, relations, errors and anti-patterns.

nestjs-drizzle-crud facts for AI agents fit on one page: register DrizzleCrudModule.forRoot once and forFeature per entity, declare each service as an empty subclass of SqlBaseCrudService with four generics, and call its methods. Lists return { data, total, page, limit }, errors are Nest HTTP exceptions, and every rule below is checked against the package source.

When this page and the types disagree, trust the types. 
The TypeScript declarations shipped in the package are the canonical definition. Generate code
against import type {... } from "@avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud", and use this page for the rules the
types cannot express.

Fact Value

chunks.h: How do I set it up?
chunks.t:
Setup is two module calls and no connection wiring in services.

1. DrizzleCrudModule.forRoot({ dialect, connectionString db, schema?, defaults?, sql?, hooks? }) once in AppModule (or forRootAsync({ imports?, inject?, useFactory })). It is global.
2. DrizzleCrudModule.forFeature([{ service, table, config? }]) in each feature module. It builds each service and exports it.

export class UsersService extends SqlBaseCrudService<
  User,          // typeof users.$inferSelect
  CreateUserDto,
  UpdateUserDto,

> {}

chunks.t:
Services. - Generics: SqlBaseCrudService. All four are required; none has a default. Use CrudFilter for FilterDto when filters come from a query string.
- A service is an empty subclass. No @Injectable(), no constructor, no @Inject(DRIZZLE_DB): forFeature calls new Service(config) itself, and a decorator or extra constructor parameter breaks that.
- The table goes in forFeature, not in the service. Per-entity config goes in forFeature config or @CrudService(config); forFeature wins.
- For a hand-written query inside a service, use this.config.db and this.config.table. Elsewhere, inject DRIZZLE_DB.
- Override protected hooks for custom logic: validateCreate, validateUpdate, beforeCreate, afterCreate, beforeUpdate, afterUpdate, beforeSoftDelete, afterSoftDelete, beforeRestore, afterRestore, beforeDelete, afterDelete, mapCreateDtoToEntity, mapUpdateDtoToEntity. Create runs validateCreate, then beforeCreate, then mapCreateDtoToEntity.
- executeSqlTransaction(async (tx) =...) is protected: call it from a service method and pass { transaction: tx } to each CRUD call that joins it.

Config. - Defaults: softDelete: true on deleted_at, timestamps: true on created_at and updated_at, pagination: { defaultLimit: 20, maxLimit: 100 }, primaryKey: "id", sql.caseSensitive: false, sql.useReturning true on PostgreSQL and SQLite and forced off on MySQL. connection: { poolSize, idleTimeout, ssl } tunes a connection built from connectionString. forRootAsync takes useFactory, useClass or useExisting (a class with createDrizzleCrudOptions()).
- Tables without those columns need defaults: { softDelete: false, timestamps: false }. softDelete.column, timestamps.createdAt / updatedAt and versionColumn name the key in the Drizzle table object (deletedAt for deletedAt: timestamp("deleted_at")); a key the table lacks throws at startup with the key to use.
- softDelete, timestamps, pagination and sql merge one level deep across forRoot, @CrudService and forFeature: pagination: { defaultLimit: 5 } keeps maxLimit. Arrays (allowlists) replace.
- connectionString is PostgreSQL only and schema is optional. primaryKeyType, sql.jsonSupport and sql.enableFullTextSearch are deprecated no-ops.

- Generics: SqlBaseCrudService. All four are required; none has a default. Use CrudFilter for FilterDto when filters come from a query string.
- A service is an empty subclass. No @Injectable(), no constructor, no @Inject(DRIZZLE_DB): forFeature calls new Service(config) itself, and a decorator or extra constructor parameter breaks that.
- The table goes in forFeature, not in the service. Per-entity config goes in forFeature config or @CrudService(config); forFeature wins.
- For a hand-written query inside a service, use this.config.db and this.config.table. Elsewhere, inject DRIZZLE_DB.
- Override protected hooks for custom logic: validateCreate, validateUpdate, beforeCreate, afterCreate, beforeUpdate, afterUpdate, beforeSoftDelete, afterSoftDelete, beforeRestore, afterRestore, beforeDelete, afterDelete, mapCreateDtoToEntity, mapUpdateDtoToEntity. Create runs validateCreate, then beforeCreate, then mapCreateDtoToEntity.
- executeSqlTransaction(async (tx) =...) is protected: call it from a service method and pass { transaction: tx } to each CRUD call that joins it.

- Defaults: softDelete: true on deleted_at, timestamps: true on created_at and updated_at, pagination: { defaultLimit: 20, maxLimit: 100 }, primaryKey: "id", sql.caseSensitive: false, sql.useReturning true on PostgreSQL and SQLite and forced off on MySQL. connection: { poolSize, idleTimeout, ssl } tunes a connection built from connectionString. forRootAsync takes useFactory, useClass or useExisting (a class with createDrizzleCrudOptions()).
- Tables without those columns need defaults: { softDelete: false, timestamps: false }. softDelete.column, timestamps.createdAt / updatedAt and versionColumn name the key in the Drizzle table object (deletedAt for deletedAt: timestamp("deleted_at")); a key the table lacks throws at startup with the key to use.
- softDelete, timestamps, pagination and sql merge one level deep across forRoot, @CrudService and forFeature: pagination: { defaultLimit: 5 } keeps maxLimit. Arrays (allowlists) replace.
- connectionString is PostgreSQL only and schema is optional. primaryKeyType, sql.jsonSupport and sql.enableFullTextSearch are deprecated no-ops.

- findAll(filters?, pagination?, options?) returns { data, total, page, limit }, never a bare array. With withCount: false (or?withCount=false) it skips COUNT( ): total is null and hasMore is a boolean.
- findAll always ends ORDER BY with the primary key ascending. sortBy is one column (direction from sortOrder, default "asc"), a - or + prefixed column, a comma separated string, or a list: ["region.name", "-name"] or [{ column, order }]. In a list, an unprefixed entry is ascending. A dotted entry sorts by a top-level belongs-to column.
- page below 1 becomes 1 and limit is clamped to 1 to maxLimit. A bad sortOrder or unknown sort column is a 400.
- findByCursor(filters, { cursor, limit, sortBy, sortOrder, count }, options) is keyset pagination: { data, limit, nextCursor, total? }. Pass nextCursor back as cursor; count defaults to false. A cursor made for another sort is a 400.
- find(id) and findOne(where) return T null; exists(id) returns a boolean. findOne is a 400 when no condition is left (every value undefined) or a key is not a column; null means IS NULL; its keys skip the allowlists.
- count(filters?, options?) returns a number. countBy(column, filters?, options?) returns [{ value, count }], largest first; the column must be filterable.
- options.search: { term, columns, mode? } works on findAll and count. mode defaults to "ilike", an escaped contains match ORed across columns; "fullText" is PostgreSQL only.
- fullTextSearch(term, columns, pagination?, options?) is PostgreSQL only, returns { data, total, page, limit }, always applies page and limit, and is a 400 for an unknown column.
- Trash: withDeleted: true or onlyDeleted: true on any read. A soft-deleted belongs-to parent comes back as null and never matches a relation filter.

- A key is a column, a relation, or a group (and, or, not). Keys are ANDed.
- Column values: a scalar is an exact match, an array is IN, null and undefined are skipped, an object holds operators: { age: { gte: 18, lt: 65 } }.
- Operators: eq neq gt gte lt lte like ilike in notIn between isNull isNotNull startsWith endsWith contains iStartsWith iEndsWith iContains arrayContains arrayOverlaps jsonContains.
- like and ilike take your own % wildcards (ilike is LIKE on MySQL). startsWith, endsWith and contains escape %, _ and \ and follow sql.caseSensitive; the i forms are always case-insensitive. arrayContains, arrayOverlaps and jsonContains are PostgreSQL only.
- A bare string is an exact match, case-insensitive on text columns while caseSensitive is false. { isNull: false } means IS NOT NULL, and "true" / "false" strings work.
- Date strings are parsed for date columns; an invalid date is a 400. An unknown filter key or operator is a 400, and so is an operator on the wrong column type.
- Groups nest and hold column, relation and collection filters: { or: [{ status: "a" }, { state: { name: "Ohio" } }], not: { tags: { name: "x" } } }. They also apply to count.

- Declare relations in the entity config, then load with options.relations: ["state"]. A dotted path nests (["states.cities"]) and pulls in its parent.
- Belongs-to: { table, localKey, references? }, LEFT JOINed into the main query, resolves to an object or null.
- Has-many: { table, type: "hasMany", foreignKey, parentKey?, orderBy? }, resolves to an array.
- Many-to-many: { table, type: "manyToMany", through, throughLocalKey, throughForeignKey, references?, parentKey?, orderBy? }, resolves to an array without the join key.
- Nested: a relations map on the relation itself. parentKey defaults to the host table's primary key at every level.
- Every collection and every nested level costs one query for the whole result, never one per row. Fifty countries with states and cities is four queries: data, count, states, cities.
- A relation missing its required keys throws when the service is built, with the full path.
- Relation filters use the same operators. A top-level belongs-to uses the join; deeper levels are EXISTS; collections are IN (SELECT...) subqueries, so total and pagination stay right. A collection value may be { some }, { none } or { every }; every is true for a parent with no rows. filterableColumns takes the full dotted path.
- options.select narrows columns, with dotted paths at any depth: ["id", "name", "region.code", "states.cities.name"]. The keys a nested level needs are added back automatically.
- options.counts: ["posts"] adds _count: { posts: n }, one grouped query per relation; soft-deleted related rows are not counted.

- create returns T. update returns T and is a 400 when nothing is left to set. softDelete and delete return a boolean. restore returns T. update, softDelete, restore and delete are a 404 for a missing row.
- delete is a 404 for a row in the trash: purge with forceDelete(id) or massForceDelete(ids). softDelete on an entity with soft delete off is a 400.
- Without writableColumns, create and update drop the soft delete and version columns from the body, and update also drops the primary key and createdAt. With it, any other column is a 400.
- Writes take options.relations and options.counts and return the rows with them loaded.
- An ISO string or a number for a date-mode timestamp / date / datetime column is turned into a Date on every write; a value that is not a date is a 400 naming the column. No DTO transform is needed for it.
- Nested create needs writableRelations: ["posts"] and RETURNING: an array for has-many, an object for belongs-to, ids or objects for many-to-many, all in one transaction.
- Use attach(id, "tags", ids), detach(id, "tags", ids?) and sync(id, "tags", ids) for many-to-many links, never raw inserts into the join table.
- upsert(dto, { conflictTarget?, update? }, options?) and massUpsert(rows,...): ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on PostgreSQL and SQLite, ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE on MySQL. A clash on another unique key is a 409.
- Bulk methods (massCreate, massUpdate, massSoftDelete, massRestore, massDelete, massForceDelete, massUpsert) run in one transaction: one SELECT that checks the ids, plus one statement for the set. Any failure rolls back everything and throws BulkOperationException, a 400 with errors: [{ index id, status, message }]. bulkMode: "perItem" runs the single-row method per item. A statement past the database's bound parameter limit (PostgreSQL and MySQL 65,535, SQLite 32,766, D1 100, counted on the real statement) is a 400 before it runs. On Cloudflare D1 and synchronous SQLite drivers, bulk writes, nested creates and attach / detach / sync throw TransactionException; use libSQL for them.

- Every exception extends a Nest HttpException subclass, so no custom filter is needed: EntityNotFoundException 404, DuplicateEntityException 409, StaleVersionException 409, EntityInUseException 409, MissingScopeException 403, ForeignKeyViolationException 400, ValidationFailedException 400, BulkOperationException 400.
- Postgres data errors (22001, 23514, 22003, 22P02, 22007, 22008, 21000), MySQL strict mode errors (1048, 1364, 1406, 1264, 1265, 1366, 1292, 3819) and SQLite NOT NULL / CHECK / STRICT type errors (3091) / SQLITE_MISMATCH become 400 on reads and writes. SQLite UNIQUE is a 409 and FOREIGN KEY a 400 or 409, as on the other dialects. TransactionException (500) means the driver cannot run a needed transaction. DatabaseConnectionException is deprecated; nothing throws it.
- Full-text search: fullTextSearch(term, columns, pagination, { filters, relations, select, language, queryMode }), PostgreSQL only. language defaults to "english", queryMode: "websearch" uses websearch_to_tsquery. A 400 on MySQL and SQLite.

- Controllers: prefer class UsersController extends createCrudController(UsersService, { dto: { create, update } }) under @Controller("users"). Bulk routes are off until enabled in routes. The:id is parsed from the primary key column (ParseIntPipe for an integer, ParseUUIDPipe for a uuid) unless idType is set; do not add your own pipe. To change a route, turn it off in routes and add your own handler. deleteMode defaults to "hard".
- Hand-written list routes: const q = this.usersService.parseQuery(query), then q.isCursor? findByCursor(q.filters, q.pagination, q.options): findAll(q.filters, q.pagination, q.options). withDeleted and onlyDeleted need allowTrash: true. parseCrudQuery(query, table, options) is the standalone form.
- OpenAPI: @ApiCrudList({ table,...entityConfig }) on a list route, or openapi in the controller options. Needs @nestjs/swagger.
- Tenancy: set scope: (ctx) = ({ tenant_id: ctx.tenantId }) and provide the context with CrudContext.middleware((req) = ({ tenantId })), CrudContext.run(ctx, fn) or options.context. Never add a manual tenant filter or set the column in the body. Another tenant's id is a 404; a missing context value is a 403. skipScope: true only for trusted jobs. A scoped upsert works on PostgreSQL and SQLite and is a 400 on MySQL. A belongs-to key a write sets must point at a row of the same tenant when the related table has the scope columns; another tenant's row is a 400 ForeignKeyViolationException, the same as a missing one.
- Events: hooks: { enableGlobalHooks: true } in forRoot, then inject CrudEventBus and subscribe({ afterWrite(e) {... } }). One event per mass call (bulk: true). Use e.transaction for atomic audit rows. skipEvents: true skips events; hooks.skipBefore / skipAfter do not.
- Optimistic locking: versionColumn: "version" (integer, starts at 1). Clients send the version they read in the update body or as expectedVersion; a stale one is a 409. Never write the version yourself. Mass writes take expectedVersions: { [String(id)]: version }.
- Row locks: lock: "update" "share" or forNoKeyUpdate: true on a read, as FOR... OF <base table on PostgreSQL, so they work with an eager belongs-to. On MySQL, FOR UPDATE or FOR SHARE (forNoKeyUpdate becomes FOR UPDATE). A 400 on SQLite.
- Primary keys: the type comes from the Drizzle column. With uuid keys, route params are strings: never ParseIntPipe. On MySQL, supply uuid keys yourself on insert.

chunks.t:
1. The TypeScript types: import type {... } from "@avytrix/nestjs-drizzle-crud".
2. The package README and AGENT.md on npm, also served by the MCP server.
3. The source on GitHub.
4. The Changelog (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/changelog), for behaviour changes release by release.

Do the SqlBaseCrudService generics have defaults?. 
No. All four, T, CreateDto, UpdateDto and FilterDto, are required. SqlBaseCrudService alone does not compile.

Is mysql2 a peer dependency?. 
An optional one, since 3.7.0. Install it when you pass connectionString with dialect: "mysql"; the module loads it only then. If you build the Drizzle instance yourself and pass it as db, the module never touches it.

Should a service have a constructor or @Injectable()?. 
No. forFeature constructs the service with a factory and passes the merged config to the base constructor. A decorator or an extra constructor parameter breaks registration.

How many queries does eager loading cost?. 
One for the data, one for the count, and one per collection or nested level for the whole result set. A top-level belongs-to rides in the main query as a LEFT JOIN.

Migrating from @nestjsx/crud to Drizzle ORM in NestJS. Convert entities to tables, services and @Crud controllers, and map every filter operator.

Migrating from @nestjsx/crud to nestjs-drizzle-crud means four moves per entity: describe the table in Drizzle instead of TypeORM, replace the TypeOrmCrudService with an empty SqlBaseCrudService subclass, replace the @Crud() controller with createCrudController or your own routes, and update clients from the filter=field $op value syntax to bracket keys such as field[op]=value. You can move one entity at a time.

The schema conversion is yours. 
This package does not read TypeORM entities or convert them. You write (or generate) the Drizzle schema. Drizzle Kit can introspect an existing database into a schema.ts with drizzle-kit pull (Drizzle docs (https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/drizzle-kit-pull), checked 2 November 2026), which is the quickest start when the tables already exist. Review what it generates before you rely on it.
