The closest match to @Crud() is the controller factory, which registers list, get, create, update, delete, soft delete, restore and trash routes, and four bulk routes you can turn on:

The routes do not match @nestjsx/crud one to one:

@nestjsx/crud route nestjs-drizzle-crud route 
--- --- 
getManyBase: GET /users list: GET /users 
getOneBase: GET /users/:id get: GET /users/:id 
createOneBase: POST /users create: POST /users 
createManyBase: POST /users/bulk, body { bulk: [...] } bulkCreate: POST /users/bulk, body is the array itself, off by default 
updateOneBase: PATCH /users/:id update: PATCH /users/:id 
replaceOneBase: PUT /users/:id No equivalent 
deleteOneBase: DELETE /users/:id delete: DELETE /users/:id, hard by default, soft with deleteMode: "soft" 
recoverOneBase (PATCH) restore: POST /users/:id/restore 

If you overrode many routes, a hand-written controller can be simpler. parseQuery does the query string work, so a list route is still short:

See CRUD controller factory (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/controller-factory) for every option.

Clients built for @nestjsx/crud send its syntax (wiki (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/wiki/Requests)): filter=field $condition value, or=, sort=field,ASC, join= and s= with JSON. The table below shows what each becomes. If a client uses RequestQueryBuilder, replace those calls; this package has no client builder.

@nestjsx/crud parameter nestjs-drizzle-crud parameter 
--- --- 
filter=name\ \ $eq\ \ Jo name[eq]=Jo 
filter=a\ \ $eq\ \ 1&filter=b\ \ $eq\ \ 2 (AND) a[eq]=1&b[eq]=2 (keys are ANDed) 
or=name\ \ $eq\ \ Jo&or=name\ \ $eq\ \ Al or[0][name][eq]=Jo&or[1][name][eq]=Al 
filter=...&or=..., meaning (filters) OR (ors) or[0][...]=...&or[1][...]=..., one or member per side 
s={"name": "Jo"} (JSON search) Bracket keys and or, and, not groups; there is no JSON parameter 
fields=id,name fields=id,name 
sort=name,ASC&sort=id,DESC sortBy=name,-id 
join=profile with=profile 
join=profile\ \ bio with=profile&fields=id,name,profile.bio 
filter=profile.bio\ \ $cont\ \ x profile[bio][contains]=x or profile.bio[contains]=x 
limit=10 or per_page=10 limit=10 (capped at maxLimit, 100 by default) 
page=2 page=2 
offset=10 No equivalent; use page, or cursor for keyset pages 
cache=0 No equivalent; the package has no query cache 

or is an array of filter objects, and the top-level keys are ANDed with it, so (a AND b) OR c is or[0][a]=1&or[0][b]=2&or[1][c]=3. See Filtering (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering#how-do-i-or-two-filters).

Every @nestjsx/crud condition from its wiki (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/wiki/Requests) and CondOperator enum (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/blob/master/packages/crud-request/src/types/request-query.types.ts), with the nestjs-drizzle-crud form for name:

@nestjsx/crud nestjs-drizzle-crud Notes 
--- --- --- 
$eq name[eq]=x Plain =, case-sensitive on PostgreSQL 
$ne name[neq]=x 
$gt, $lt, $gte, $lte name[gt]=x, name[lt]=x, name[gte]=x, name[lte]=x Values coerced by column type 
$starts name[startsWith]=x Follows sql.caseSensitive (default false, so case-insensitive) 
$ends name[endsWith]=x Same 
$cont name[contains]=x Same 
$excl not[name][contains]=x A not group 
$in name[in]=a,b or name=a&name=b 
$notin name[notIn]=a,b 
$isnull name[isNull]=true 
$notnull name[isNotNull]=true 
$between name[between]=a,b Exactly two values, inclusive 
$eqL name=x A bare value on a text column is lower(name) = lower(x) while sql.caseSensitive is false 
$neL not[name]=x Same rule, negated 
$startsL, $endsL, $contL name[iStartsWith]=x, name[iEndsWith]=x, name[iContains]=x Always case-insensitive 
$exclL not[name][iContains]=x 
$inL, $notinL No direct equivalent in and notIn compare as stored
The pattern operators escape %, _ and \ in your value. Use like or ilike to write a pattern with wildcards yourself. An unknown column or operator is a 400 with a message that names it.

chunks.h: Update clients for the response shape
chunks.t: A paginated getMany in @nestjsx/crud returns { data, count, total, page, pageCount } (source (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/blob/master/packages/crud/src/interfaces/get-many-default-response.interface.ts)). findAll returns { data, total, page, limit }, plus hasMore when you skip the count with withCount=false. A client that read count can use data.length, and pageCount is Math.ceil(total / limit). See Pagination and sorting (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting).

chunks.h: Lock down what clients may query
chunks.t:
@nestjsx/crud had allow, exclude and join options per controller. The equivalent here is the allowlists in the entity config. With none set, a client may filter, sort and select any column, so add them before you expose the route:

See Allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists).

Does nestjs-drizzle-crud convert TypeORM entities to Drizzle?. 
No. You write the Drizzle schema yourself, or generate it from the existing database with drizzle-kit pull and review the result.

Can I migrate one entity at a time?. 
Yes. DrizzleCrudModule has no dependency on TypeORM, so you can keep TypeOrmModule for the entities you have not moved yet and switch each one when it is ready.

What replaces filter=field $eq value?. 
field[eq]=value for a case-sensitive match, or a bare field=value, which is case-insensitive on text columns while sql.caseSensitive is false, the default.

Is there a PUT replace route?. 
No. The controller factory has PATCH /:id for updates and no PUT route. Add one by hand if your clients depend on it.

What replaces RequestQueryBuilder?. 
Nothing in this package. Clients build the query string themselves, for example with URLSearchParams.

Build a NestJS multi tenant API on Drizzle with one scope key. Every read and write is limited to the caller's tenant; a missing tenant is a 403.

To build a NestJS multi tenant API on Drizzle with nestjs-drizzle-crud, set scope on an entity, for example scope: (ctx) = ({ tenant_id: ctx.tenantId }). Every query the service runs is then limited to the rows that match it: reads, counts, cursors, writes, bulk writes, upserts, soft deletes, restores and force deletes. A create writes the scope onto the new row. Another tenant's row is a 404, and a request without a tenant is a 403.

You cannot forget it in one method. 
The scope is not a filter you add per call. Every read builds its WHERE from the same row scope, and every UPDATE and DELETE from the same write predicate, so no method runs without it.

chunks.h: How do I scope an entity to a tenant?
chunks.t:
Add `scope` to the entity config. The scope reads the call's context and returns the column: value pairs every row must match:

Put the tenant in the request context. CrudContext.middleware resolves the context from the request and runs the rest of the request inside it:

Call the service as usual. projects.findAll() now returns only the caller's projects, and projects.update(id, dto) on another tenant's id is a 404. The example app does exactly this in apps/api/src/projects, reading the tenant from an x-tenant-id header so the e2e suite can switch tenants.
The scope reads the call's context and returns the column: value pairs every row must match:

chunks.h: Put the tenant in the request context
chunks.t: CrudContext.middleware resolves the context from the request and runs the rest of the request inside it:

projects.findAll() now returns only the caller's projects, and projects.update(id, dto) on another tenant's id is a 404. The example app does exactly this in apps/api/src/projects, reading the tenant from an x-tenant-id header so the e2e suite can switch tenants.

chunks.h: What does a scope look like?
chunks.t:
column: value pairs, each an exact match (null means IS NULL). Either a fixed object, or a function of the call's context:

CrudScopeValues null)", description: "The column values every row must match. A function that returns null leaves that call unscoped on purpose." },
"options.context": { type: "Record<string, unknown ", default: "CrudContext.current()", description: "The context a function scope reads, per call. Wins over CrudContext." },
"options.skipScope": { type: "boolean", default: "false", description: "Run a trusted, server-side call without the entity's scope." },
}}
/ 

Returning null leaves that call unscoped on purpose, for an admin or a background job. A key that is not a column of the table throws, and so does a function that returns something other than an object or null. The function runs synchronously, once per call (since 3.8.0; it used to run once per statement and relation), so resolve anything async (the user, their tenant) in middleware or a guard and put the result in the context.

c.s:
scope: { region_id: 1 }                                   // fixed
scope: (ctx) => ({ tenant_id: ctx.tenantId })             // per request
scope: (ctx) => ({ tenant_id: ctx.tenantId, owner_id: ctx.userId })
scope: (ctx) => (ctx.isAdmin ? null : { tenant_id: ctx.tenantId })

chunks.h: Where does the context come from?
chunks.t:
From options.context on the call, or else from CrudContext, which keeps a per-request value in Node's AsyncLocalStorage so it follows the request through every await without being passed by hand. Outside a request, wrap the work yourself:

CrudContext member What it does 
--- --- 
run(context, fn) Runs fn with context as the current context and returns its result. 
current() The context of the running code, or undefined outside one. 
middleware(resolve) An Express style middleware: calls resolve(req) and runs the rest of the request inside the result. A throw in resolve goes to next(error).

The call fails closed. When the scope function returns undefined for a column (no tenant on the request), the service throws MissingScopeException, a 403, instead of running unscoped. A trusted server-side call can opt out with skipScope: true:

c.s: await projects.count({}, { skipScope: true }); // every tenant

chunks.t:
All of them:

Area Methods Another tenant's row 
--- --- --- 
Reads find, findOne, exists, findAll, findByCursor, count, countBy, fullTextSearch, relation counts Not found: null, false, or left out of the page and the total. 
Single writes update, softDelete, restore, delete, forceDelete 404 
Upsert upsert, massUpsert 404 (the conflicting row is not updated) 
Bulk massUpdate, massSoftDelete, massRestore, massDelete, massForceDelete 400 with a 404 entry for that id, nothing written 
Links attach, detach, sync 404 

The scope is ANDed into the existence check and into the UPDATE or DELETE statement itself, so a row cannot change tenant between the two. Since every statement carries tenant_id = $1, put the tenant column first in your composite indexes; Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/indexes#how-do-i-index-a-multi-tenant-table) shows them. On upsert it sits in the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE... WHERE, on PostgreSQL and SQLite alike. MySQL's ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE has no WHERE, so a scoped upsert on MySQL is a 400 (upsert on a scoped entity needs PostgreSQL or SQLite).

chunks.h: What does a create or update do with the scope column?
chunks.t:
create, massCreate and upsert write the scope values onto the row, over whatever the body said, so a client cannot create a row in another tenant. update never sets the scope columns: they are dropped from the SET, so a body cannot move a row to another tenant. An update whose only column was the scope column is a 400 (nothing to update).

With nested create (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations-on-writes), child rows get the scope values too when their table has the same columns, their declared belongs-to keys are checked like the parent's (see below), and attach only links targets in the caller's tenant when the related table has the scope column.

Yes, when the related table has the scope columns. Loaded relations, joins, relation filters (some, none, every and nested columns) and counts only see related rows of the caller's tenant. A belongs-to row of another tenant loads as null, and a filter on it matches nothing. A related table without the scope column is treated as shared and left unscoped.

chunks.h: Can a write point a foreign key at another tenant's row?
chunks.t:
No, since 3.7.2, when the related table has the scope columns. On a scoped entity, create, update, upsert and the mass writes check every belongs-to key they set (localKey of a relation in relations) against the caller's tenant, the way attach checks its targets. A key that points at another tenant's row gets exactly the answer a key pointing at a missing row gets, a 400 ForeignKeyViolationException, so the response does not reveal that the row exists:

The check costs one SELECT per relation for the whole call, whatever the number of rows; a mass write lists the failing items in a BulkOperationException. A related table without the scope columns is shared and not checked, and neither is a call with skipScope: true. A key to a row that does not exist at all is refused the same way, even without a database foreign key.

chunks.h: Can a write point a foreign key at another tenant's row?
chunks.t:
Which key matches is the database's call, as it is for a foreign key. Since 3.8.2 the check joins the keys it was sent against the related table, so the column's type and collation compare them: a citext or SQLite NOCASE key in the caller's own tenant matches in any case, a PostgreSQL text key or a MySQL key under a _bin collation only matches exactly, and a uuid matches in any case. A key the column's type cannot hold, such as "nope" for a uuid, is a 400 on every write, a mass write or one inside your own transaction included. attach and sync check their targets the same way and link each one by its key as stored, so "ann@x.io" and "Ann@X.io" on a citext column give one link.

Since 3.8.1 the same check runs on the rows a nested create (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations-on-writes) writes. A child key is checked when the nested relation declares it in its own relations, with the same 400:

Only declared relations are checked. A child column that no nested relation names is left to the database's foreign key, which knows nothing about tenants, so declare every belongs-to a nested child can set.

chunks.h: Can a write point a foreign key at another tenant's row?
chunks.t: A composite foreign key such as (tenant_id, author_id) still makes the database itself refuse a cross-tenant reference, for writes that do not go through the service.

Does a request without a tenant see every row?. 
No. When the scope function returns undefined for a column, the call throws MissingScopeException, a 403. Only a function that returns null, or a call with skipScope: true, runs unscoped.

What does a client get for another tenant. 
A 404 on a write and null on a read, the same as an id that does not exist. The response never reveals that the row exists in another tenant.

Can a client move a row to another tenant with an update?. 
No. The scope columns are dropped from the SET of every update, and a create always writes the caller's scope values over the body.

Does scoped upsert work on MySQL?. 
No. MySQL's ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE cannot carry the scope condition, so a scoped upsert on MySQL is a 400 rather than a write that could touch another tenant's row.

Are eager-loaded relations filtered by tenant?. 
Yes, when the related table has the scope columns. Loaded relations, joins, relation filters and counts only see the caller's tenant, and a belongs-to row of another tenant loads as null. A related table without the scope columns is treated as shared and is not filtered. Give it its own scoped service if clients query it directly.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle Swagger docs for lists
chunks.h: How do I document a list route?
chunks.t:
Install @nestjs/swagger.

Share the entity config. Put the allowlists and relations in one constant, so forFeature and the decorator read the same facts:

Spread it into the module: DrizzleCrudModule.forFeature([{ service: CountriesService, table: countries, config: countriesCrud }]).

Decorate the route.

Serve the document. The UI is at /docs and the JSON at /docs-json.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle Swagger docs for lists
chunks.t:
Put the allowlists and relations in one constant, so forFeature and the decorator read the same facts:

Spread it into the module: DrizzleCrudModule.forFeature([{ service: CountriesService, table: countries, config: countriesCrud }]).

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle Swagger docs for lists
chunks.t: The UI is at /docs and the JSON at /docs-json.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle Swagger docs for lists
chunks.h: What do I pass as the source?
chunks.t:
The table plus the same allowlists the service uses, so the docs match what the API accepts. There are two shapes:

- A config object with the table: { table, relations, filterableColumns, sortableColumns, selectableColumns, searchableColumns, loadableRelations, allowTrash }. Every key except table is optional. This is the usual pattern, with the shared constant spread in.
- A service class decorated with @CrudService({ table,... }), whose metadata already holds the table and the lists. A class without that metadata throws an error that names what to pass instead.

Config set only in forFeature is not visible when the decorator runs, because decorators run when the class is defined. That is why the shared constant matters.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle Swagger docs for lists
chunks.t:
Each parameter appears only when the entity can use it:

Parameter Documented when 
--- --- 
page, limit, sortBy, sortOrder, withCount, fields always; sortBy and fields list the sortable and selectable columns 
with, counts the entity has relations; with lists the loadable ones 
search searchColumns or searchableColumns is set 
cursor, count unless { cursor: false } 
withDeleted, onlyDeleted allowTrash: true, and not on a trash route ({ trash: true }) 
one parameter per filter column every entry of filterableColumns, or every column when it is unset 

A relation path is written the way a query string sends it: region.name becomes region[name]. Each filter parameter carries the column's OpenAPI type (integer, number, boolean, date-time, uuid, int64 for a bigint, an enum's values) and lists the bracket operators, such as name[startsWith]=In. Every parameter is optional.

ApiCrudList also adds the 200 response: { data, total, page, limit, hasMore, nextCursor }. The row schema comes from the table's columns, nullable columns are marked nullable, and total is nullable because withCount=false skips the count.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle Swagger docs for lists
chunks.h: Does the controller factory document itself?
chunks.t:
Yes, through the openapi option of createCrudController (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/controller-factory). It applies ApiCrudList(source) to the list route and ApiCrudList(source, { trash: true }) to the trash route:

Pass openapi: true instead when the service carries @CrudService metadata. It documents the allowlists of that decorator only: Swagger reads them when the class is defined, before forFeature runs, so allowlists set in forFeature are not shown. In that case pass the entity object, { table,...allowlists }, as above.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle Swagger docs for lists
chunks.t:
Do I need @nestjs/swagger to use nestjs-drizzle-crud?. 
No. It is an optional peer dependency, loaded only when you apply ApiCrudQuery or ApiCrudList. Without the decorators you have nothing extra to install.

Why are my forFeature allowlists missing from the Swagger docs?. 
The decorator runs when the class is defined and cannot see forFeature config. Keep the config in one constant and spread it into both forFeature and the decorator.

How is a relation filter named in Swagger?. 
The way a query string sends it: the allowlist entry region.name is documented as the parameter region[name].

What is the difference between ApiCrudQuery and ApiCrudList?. 
ApiCrudQuery documents the query parameters only. ApiCrudList adds the 200 response with the page envelope and the row schema.

chunks.p: NestJS Drizzle Swagger docs for lists

chunks.t:
Drizzle optimistic locking with a version column in NestJS. Set versionColumn, send the version you read, and a stale write is a 409 conflict.

Drizzle optimistic locking with a version column stops a client from overwriting a change it never saw. Set versionColumn on the entity, send back the version you read, and a write against a row that has moved on since then is a 409 StaleVersionException. The package bumps the version in SQL on every write. It takes no row lock, so it suits the read, edit, save flow of a form.

Who this is for. 
Use a version column when two people can edit the same row and the last save must not silently win. If you need to hold a row while one transaction reads and writes it, use row locks (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/row-locks) instead.

chunks.h: How do I turn on optimistic locking?
chunks.t:
Add an integer column and name it in the entity config.

Add a version column to the table.

Set versionColumn for the entity.

Send the version back on every write. Return the version you read with the update, as shown in the next section. A write against a newer version is a 409.

chunks.h: Send the version back on every write
chunks.t: Return the version you read with the update, as shown in the next section. A write against a newer version is a 409.

It starts at 1 on create, whatever the body says, and goes up by one on every write:

Write Version 
--- --- 
create, massCreate set to 1 
update, massUpdate plus one 
softDelete, massSoftDelete plus one 
restore, massRestore plus one 
upsert, massUpsert 1 on insert, plus one when the row existed 

It is computed in SQL (SET version = version + 1), never taken from a body. The version key is removed from a create or update body before anything else happens, so it is never written directly, even when writableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) lists it.

chunks.h: How do I send the version I read?

c.s:
const project = await projects.find(1);                 // version: 3
await projects.update(1, { name: 'New', version: 3 });  // ok, now version 4
await projects.update(1, { name: 'Late', version: 3 }); // 409

chunks.h: What does a stale write return?
chunks.t:
A StaleVersionException, which extends Nest's ConflictException, so the HTTP answer is a 409:

The UPDATE or DELETE itself carries AND version = <expected, so a write that lands between a read and the write is always caught. When that statement changes no row, the service reads the row once to give the right answer: 404 when it is not there (or belongs to another tenant), 409 when it is at another version. When your service runs a before hook, or a before event is wired, the version is also compared before anything is written, so the hook never runs for a stale write.

chunks.h: What if the client sends no version?
chunks.t: Then there is no check, and the write still bumps the version. That keeps internal writes simple. If every client must send it, make the field required in your update DTO.

chunks.h: How does it work with bulk writes?
chunks.t:
Pass expectedVersions, keyed by the id as a string:

Any id at another version makes the whole call a 400 BulkOperationException with a 409 entry for that id, and nothing is written:

massSoftDelete, massRestore, massDelete and massForceDelete take expectedVersions the same way. See Bulk operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations) for the rest of the error body.

What HTTP status does a stale version return?. 
A 409 Conflict from StaleVersionException. In a mass write the call is a 400 BulkOperationException with a 409 entry for each stale id.

Can a client set the version directly?. 
No. The version key is removed from create and update bodies, and the package sets it in SQL: 1 on insert, plus one on every later write.

Is the version checked when the client does not send one?. 
No. Without a version in the body or expectedVersion in the options, the write is not checked, but the version still goes up.

Does optimistic locking lock the row?. 
No. It compares versions in the WHERE clause and holds no lock. For a lock across a read and a write, use lock: 'update' inside a transaction.

Drizzle pagination in NestJS with findAll: page and limit (20 rows by default, at most 100), withCount: false to skip COUNT(*), and multi-column sorts.

For Drizzle pagination in NestJS, call findAll(filters, { page, limit, sortBy }) on your service. It returns { data, total, page, limit }, not a bare array. page starts at 1, limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100, and total counts every matching row. sortBy takes one column, a list such as ['status', '-created_at'], or a belongs-to column such as author.name. The primary key is always the last sort column, so pages never repeat or skip rows.

Column names are table keys. 
sortBy, defaultSort and the examples on this page name the key in your Drizzle table object (created_at in created_at: timestamp('created_at')), not the SQL column name. The examples use a posts table with snake_case keys and a PostsService.

A page envelope: the rows, the count of matching rows, and the page and limit that were actually used.

total is counted after filters, options.search, the tenant scope and soft delete, but before LIMIT and OFFSET, so it stays the same on every page. The data query and the count query run at the same time.

The pagination argument is optional. Leave it out and findAll returns the first page, up to defaultLimit rows.

chunks.h: How do I skip the count query?
chunks.t:
Pass withCount: false. findAll then runs one query instead of two, total is null, and hasMore says whether another page follows.

hasMore comes from fetching one row more than the page and dropping it, so it costs nothing extra. COUNT( ) is the expensive half of a list on a big table (on 200,000 rows a page took 23 ms with it and 0.6 ms without), and infinite scroll or a "next" button does not need it. From a query string,?withCount=false sets it. For deep pages, cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination) skips both the count and the OFFSET; Database indexes for fast Drizzle queries (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/indexes) lists the index each sort needs.

The return type follows the option:

Call total type hasMore 
--- --- --- 
withCount: false written in the call null boolean, always present 
withCount left out or true number absent 
A value known only at run time (the output of parseQuery) number \ null boolean \ undefined

c.s:
const page = await this.postsService.findAll({}, { page: 3, limit: 20, withCount: false });
// { data: [...20 rows], total: null, page: 3, limit: 20, hasMore: true }

chunks.h: How do I sort by one column?
chunks.t:
Pass the column as a string. A single string sorts in sortOrder, which defaults to 'desc'.

A - prefix forces descending and a + prefix forces ascending, whatever sortOrder says.

chunks.h: How do I sort by several columns?
chunks.t:
Pass a list. In a list, each entry sorts ascending unless it starts with -. An entry can also be a { column, order } object, where order defaults to 'asc'. A comma separated string means the same list.

sortOrder does not apply to list entries. A column listed twice is sorted once, by its first entry.

chunks.h: How do I sort by a related column?
chunks.t:
Write it as relation.column. It works for a top-level belongs-to relation, which is joined for the data query only. The count query stays unjoined unless a filter needs the relation.

These are a 400:

- a has-many or many-to-many column, because a row has many of them,
- a column that does not exist on the table or the relation,
- a column outside sortableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) when that allowlist is set.

Over HTTP, parseQuery (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing) reads?sortBy=author.name,-created_at. It always hands the service a list, and an unprefixed column sorts ascending unless?sortOrder=desc is set:?sortBy=views and findAll({}, { sortBy: 'views' }) are both views ASC. Before 3.5.2 the second was views DESC.

c.s:
await this.postsService.findAll({}, { sortBy: ['author.name', '-created_at'] });
// LEFT JOIN authors ... ORDER BY authors.name ASC, posts.created_at DESC, posts.id ASC

chunks.h: Why does every query end with the primary key?
chunks.t: So that pages are stable. Postgres returns rows that tie on the sort columns in no fixed order, and without any ORDER BY the order can change between two queries. Offset pagination over an unstable order repeats some rows and skips others. Since 3.3.1 the primary key is always the last ORDER BY column (ascending), unless it is already in the list.

chunks.h: How do I set a default sort for an entity?
chunks.t:
Set defaultSort in the entity's forFeature config. It is an ordered list: the first column is the primary sort and the rest are tiebreakers. It applies whenever the caller passes no sortBy.

sortBy replaces defaultSort. 
An explicit sortBy replaces the entity's defaultSort entirely. Only the primary key tiebreaker is still added.

Each entry's order defaults to 'asc'. An unknown column in defaultSort is a config mistake, not a request error, so it never throws. The column is skipped, and each query that falls back to defaultSort logs [nestjs-drizzle-crud] defaultSort references unknown column "<col "; skipping. A caller sortBy with an unknown column is a 400 instead.

chunks.h: Can every entity sort by created_at by default?
chunks.t:
Yes. Set defaults.sortOrder in forRoot. Every entity that has no defaultSort of its own and has a timestamps.createdAt column then sorts by that column in this direction.

Leave defaults.sortOrder out and entities without a defaultSort sort by the primary key alone.

chunks.h: How do I change the page size limits?
chunks.t:
Set pagination under defaults in forRoot for every entity, or in an entity's forFeature config for that entity alone.

Either key can be set on its own: pagination: { defaultLimit: 5 } keeps maxLimit at 100, because the settings merge one level deep. Before 3.3.1 a per-entity override with one key dropped the other, and the query ran with no limit at all.

The cap cannot be turned off. 
The cap applies on every call, so a client cannot ask for a million rows. For an export endpoint that needs every row, walk the table with cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination), or write a custom service method over this.config.db.

chunks.h: Which inputs are clamped and which are a 400? [#clamping-fail-fast]
chunks.t:
Pagination input is clamped to a safe value and never throws. Sort and filter input that cannot be right is a BadRequestException (400).

Clamped, never throws:

Input Becomes 
--- --- 
page missing or NaN 1 
page < 1 1 
limit missing or NaN defaultLimit 
limit <= 0 1 
limit maxLimit maxLimit 
A fraction, such as limit: 10.7 Rounded down: 10 

A LIMIT 0 or a negative OFFSET never reaches SQL. The same clamp (resolvePagination) runs in findAll, findByCursor and fullTextSearch.

A BadRequestException (400):

chunks.h: Which inputs are clamped and which are a 400? [#clamping-fail-fast]
chunks.t:
Input Why 
--- --- 
A caller sortBy that is not a column of the table or of a belongs-to relation A typo surfaces at once instead of returning rows in the wrong order. 
A caller sortBy outside sortableColumns See allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists). 
A sortBy list entry that is neither a string nor { column, order } The shape is checked before any SQL runs. 
A sortOrder other than 'asc' or 'desc' Before this check, anything other than 'desc' silently sorted ascending. 
{ gt, gte, lt, lte } with NaN or Infinity It would reach SQL as an opaque 500. 
A filter key that is not a column or relation, or an unknown operator Dropping it would return every row for a typo. See unknown filter keys (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering#what-happens-with-an-unknown-filter-key). 
A date filter value that is not a date For example { created_at: { gte: 'garbage' } }. 

For the full per-method table of 400, 404, 409 and 500 responses, see errors (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/errors).

chunks.h: When should I use cursor pagination instead?
chunks.t: When people scroll deep into a list, or the list changes while they read it. findAll is offset based: page 500 still reads and throws away 499 pages of rows, and a row inserted on page 1 shifts every later page by one. findByCursor returns a nextCursor instead of a page number and avoids both. See cursor pagination with Drizzle (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination).

What is the default page size?. 
20 rows, from pagination.defaultLimit. A caller can ask for up to pagination.maxLimit rows, which is 100 unless you raise it in forRoot or forFeature.

Does a limit above maxLimit throw an error?. 
No. It is lowered to maxLimit, and the response's limit field shows the value that was used.

Why is total null in my response?. 
The call passed withCount: false (or?withCount=false), which skips the COUNT( ) query. Use hasMore to decide whether to show a next page.

Does sortBy add to defaultSort or replace it?. 
It replaces it. Only the primary key tiebreaker is still added at the end.

Can I sort by a has-many relation column?. 
No. A row has many values for that column, so the sort is a 400. Only top-level belongs-to columns, written as relation.column, can be sorted on.

chunks.p: Drizzle UUID primary keys in NestJS
chunks.h: Drizzle UUID primary keys in NestJS
chunks.t:
Use a Drizzle uuid primary key in NestJS, or serial and bigint. The key type comes from the column; on MySQL you send the uuid on create.

A Drizzle uuid primary key works in NestJS with no extra config: declare uuid('id').primaryKey().defaultRandom() and the service reads the key type from the Drizzle column. Serial, integer and bigint keys work the same way. The only setting is primaryKey, the key of the column, which defaults to id. On MySQL, which has no RETURNING, send the uuid in the create body so the service can read the new row back.

Do not use ParseIntPipe on uuid routes. 
With a uuid key, route params are strings, and @Param('id', ParseIntPipe) rejects every valid
request with a 400. Use ParseUUIDPipe, or service.parseId(raw), which picks the right check for
the key column.

The primary key is also the last ORDER BY column of every findAll, which keeps offset
pagination stable when other sort columns tie. See
pagination and sorting (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting#why-does-every-query-end-with-the-primary-key).

Register the service. primaryKey defaults to 'id', so a uuid column under that key needs nothing more. This table has

Parse the route param as a uuid.

On PostgreSQL. It works fully. create inserts with RETURNING and hands back the row with the uuid the database

chunks.p: Drizzle UUID primary keys in NestJS
chunks.h: How do I parse the id route param?
chunks.t:
Call service.parseId(raw). It applies the same check a Nest pipe would, chosen from the key
column, and throws a 400 on bad input. service.idKind() tells you which one applies.

idKind() Key column parseId does 
--- --- --- 
"int" integer, serial, or a bigint in number mode ParseIntPipe 
"bigint" bigint or bigserial in bigint mode Checks the digits and returns a BigInt 
"uuid" uuid ParseUUIDPipe 
"string" anything else, including numeric and decimal Returns the string as is 

The controller factory (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/controller-factory) uses the same logic for its:id routes.

chunks.p: Drizzle UUID primary keys in NestJS
chunks.h: What if the key is not named id?
chunks.t:
Set primaryKey to the key of the column in your Drizzle table object:

Every method that takes an id (find, update, softDelete, restore, delete and the mass
variants) matches against that column.

chunks.p: Drizzle UUID primary keys in NestJS
chunks.h: Can different entities use different key types?
chunks.t:
Yes. Each service reads its key type from its own table, so serial, bigserial and uuid keys can sit
side by side in one forFeature call with no extra config. The methods accept the id as any, so
check the type at the route with a pipe or parseId.

chunks.p: Drizzle UUID primary keys in NestJS
chunks.t:
No. Every CRUD method assumes a single-column key (find(id), update(id,...)). For a table with
a composite key, write a custom service method that builds the where clause with raw Drizzle on
this.config.db. See Define a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/defining-services#how-do-i-add-custom-methods).

chunks.p: Drizzle UUID primary keys in NestJS
chunks.t:
serial / bigserial uuid 
--- --- --- 
Index size Smaller Larger 
Joins Faster Slightly slower 
Debugging Easy to read and compare Harder to read 
Merging data from several databases Keys can collide No collisions 
Exposed in URLs Easy to guess the next id Not guessable 

For internal tables (join tables, audit logs), serial is usually fine. For rows whose ids appear
in URLs or in other systems, uuid is the safer default.

chunks.p: Drizzle UUID primary keys in NestJS
chunks.t:
Do I need to configure anything for a uuid primary key?. 
No, not when the column key is id. The service reads the key type from the Drizzle column. primaryKeyType is deprecated and has no effect.

Why does my uuid route return 400?. 
The route probably uses ParseIntPipe. Use ParseUUIDPipe, or call service.parseId(raw), which picks the check from the key column.

Do uuid keys work on MySQL?. 
Yes, if you send the uuid in the create body. MySQL has no RETURNING, so the service reads the new row back by that value.

Are composite primary keys supported?. 
No. The CRUD methods take a single-column key. Write a custom method with raw Drizzle for a table with a composite key.

NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.h: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.t:
Parse NestJS query string filters for Drizzle with parseQuery. It turns ?age[gte]=18&status=active into typed filters, pagination and options.

To turn NestJS query string filters into Drizzle queries, call service.parseQuery(query) in the controller. It reads a query such as?population[gte]=1000000&region[name]=Asia&sortBy=-name&page=2, coerces each value by its Drizzle column type, and returns the filters, pagination and options that findAll, findByCursor and count take. Unknown columns, operators and relations are a 400 before any SQL runs.

One line per list endpoint. 
parseQuery reads the entity's own table, relations, primary key and
allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists). Outside a service, the standalone parseCrudQuery(query, table,
options) export does the same work with the config you pass.

chunks.p: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.h: What does the query string look like?
chunks.t:
Each filter is a key: a bare value for an exact match, or brackets for an operator. A relation name filters by a related column.

A relation filter can go on through the related table's own relations, and a collection takes some, none or every as the next key. filterableColumns is checked against the full dotted path (state.country.code). See filtering by relation (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relation-filters).

c.s:
GET /countries?status=active                 exact match
GET /countries?population[gte]=1000000       operator
GET /countries?region_id[in]=1,3             list operand, comma separated
GET /countries?code=IN&code=NP               repeated key: IN (...)
GET /countries?region[name]=Asia             belongs-to column (region.name=Asia works too)
GET /countries?states[name]=Kerala           has-many or many-to-many column
GET /cities?state[country][code]=IN          a path through relations (state.country.code=IN too)
GET /countries?states[none][name]=Kerala     some / none / every on a collection
GET /countries?states[some]=                 has at least one state
GET /countries?or[0][code]=IN&or[1][code]=NP OR group
GET /countries?not[region][name]=Asia        NOT group
GET /countries?sortBy=region.name,-name&page=2&limit=20
GET /countries?fields=id,name,region.name&with=region
GET /countries?search=nep
GET /countries?cursor=                       first keyset page
GET /countries?withCount=false               skip the COUNT(*)
GET /countries?counts=states,tags            _count on each row

chunks.p: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.h: How do operators and lists work in brackets?
chunks.t:
All 22 filter operators (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/filtering#operator-reference) work in brackets, and each one expects a particular shape of value:

Operators Query value Example 
--- --- --- 
eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte One value, coerced by column type age[gte]=18 
like, ilike, startsWith, endsWith, contains, iStartsWith, iEndsWith, iContains One value, kept as text name[startsWith]=Ne 
in, notIn, between, arrayContains, arrayOverlaps Comma separated list, each element coerced id[in]=1,3, created_at[between]=2025-01-01,2025-12-31 
isNull, isNotNull true, false, 1, 0, or empty for true archived_at[isNull]= 
jsonContains JSON meta[jsonContains]={"size":"L"} 

Use a repeated key (name[in]=a&name[in]=b) or name[]=a&name[]=b when a value contains a comma. between needs exactly two values, and a single-value operator given twice is a 400.

The parser reads both Express 5's default flat keys (age[gte]) and the nested objects of the qs parser (app.set('query parser', 'extended')), so it works whichever one your app uses.

chunks.p: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.t: These keys are read by the parser itself. Every other key is a filter.

chunks.p: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.t:
Parameter Becomes Notes 
--- --- --- 
page, limit pagination.page, pagination.limit Positive integers, otherwise a 400. An empty value is ignored. The parser does not cap limit; findAll clamps it to pagination.maxLimit (100 by default). 
sortBy pagination.sortBy Comma list. -name sorts descending, +name or name ascending, region.name sorts by a belongs-to column. A has-many column is a 400. 
sortOrder direction of the unprefixed sortBy entries asc (the default) or desc. Anything else is a 400. 
fields options.select Comma list, dotted paths for relation columns. 
with options.relations Comma list of relation paths. 
search options.search Searches searchColumns, or the entity's searchableColumns, in the default ilike mode. Without either it is a 400 (Search is not enabled for this resource). 
cursor / after pagination.cursor Sets isCursor. Empty means the first page. See cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination). 
count pagination.count true asks findByCursor for a total. 
withCount pagination.withCount false makes findAll skip the count: total is null and hasMore is set. See skipping the count query (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting#how-do-i-skip-the-count-query). 
counts options.counts Comma list of has-many or many-to-many relations to count under _count. Checked against loadableRelations; a belongs-to is a 400. See aggregates (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/aggregates). 
withDeleted, onlyDeleted options.withDeleted, options.onlyDeleted Only with allowTrash: true. Otherwise they are read as filter columns, so a 400 unless the table has such a column. See soft delete (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/soft-delete).

chunks.p: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.t: The flags (count, withCount, withDeleted, onlyDeleted) accept true, 1 or an empty value for true, and false or 0 for false.

chunks.p: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.t:
By the Drizzle column, so the service gets the type it expects:

Column Query value Result 
--- --- --- 
integer, serial, real, double, numeric in number mode "18" 18. Not a number: 400. 
bigint in bigint mode "9007199254740993" 9007199254740993n, exact. 
numeric / decimal in string mode "10.50" Checked as a number, kept as the exact string. 
boolean "true", "false", "1", "0" true / false. Anything else: 400. 
timestamp, date (date mode) "2025-01-01" A Date. Not a date: 400. 
timestamp, date (string mode) "2025-01-01" Checked as a date, kept as the string. 
text, varchar, uuid, enum "Asia" Left as a string. PostgreSQL checks uuid and enum values, and a bad one is a 400. 
array operands "red,blue" Each element coerced by the array's element type.

chunks.p: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.t:
The same things the service rejects, caught before any SQL runs:

- an unknown column, relation, operator, sort column, fields entry, with path or counts name
- a value the column cannot hold
- a malformed key such as a[b, or two keys that conflict (age=1&age[gt]=2)
- a key given twice where one value is expected (page=1&page=2)
- anything outside an allowlist (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists)

Keys containing __proto__, constructor or prototype are refused outright.

chunks.p: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.t:
Pass them as the second argument:

parseQuery copies the entity's relations, primary key and five read allowlists into these options, then spreads yours on top, so an option you pass replaces the entity value for that call. parseCrudQuery(query, table, options) takes the same options and fills in nothing.

chunks.p: NestJS query string filters for Drizzle
chunks.t:
A ParsedCrudQuery, with the three findAll arguments ready to pass and the parts split out for your own use:
