chunks.p: Test a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service
chunks.t:
Can I test a CRUD service without a Postgres server?. 
Yes. PGlite runs Postgres in memory inside the test process, so the real module and real SQL run with no server, container or credentials.

Does TestCrudFactory work outside Jest?. 
No. createMockDb calls the global jest to build its mock functions, so it only works inside a Jest test file.

Does createMockTable take my Drizzle table?. 
No. It takes no arguments and returns a fixed object with id, name, email, created_at, updated_at and deleted_at. Pass your real table to createTestService instead if you need its columns.

Why does createTestService throw about a missing column?. 
The service checks its soft-delete and timestamp keys when it is built. Set them to keys your table has, or turn them off in the config you pass.

chunks.p: Test a NestJS Drizzle CRUD service

chunks.t:
Set Drizzle createdAt and updatedAt columns in NestJS. The package stamps them on every write, or the database owns them with defaultNow.

Drizzle createdAt and updatedAt columns in NestJS can be set two ways. By default the package stamps them itself: create writes both, and update, softDelete and restore move updated_at, all with the application clock. Or you turn package timestamps off and let the database own them with defaultNow(), $onUpdate() or a trigger. Pick one per entity; the database is the more reliable source of time.

The settings name keys, not SQL columns. 
timestamps.createdAt and timestamps.updatedAt are keys in your Drizzle table object,
created_at and updated_at by default. A camelCase schema needs them set, and since 3.3.1 a key
the table does not have stops the service at startup.

chunks.h: What does the package write, and when?
chunks.t:
The package writes a JavaScript new Date() into the configured keys on writes that go through the
service:

Operation created_at updated_at 
--- --- --- 
create, massCreate Set to now Set to now 
update, massUpdate Left alone Set to now 
softDelete, massSoftDelete, restore, massRestore Left alone Set to now 
upsert, massUpsert (insert) Set to now Set to now 
upsert, massUpsert (conflict, row updated) Kept from the existing row Set to now 
delete, forceDelete (row removed) (row removed) 

Two more rules keep the values honest:

- The body cannot override them. On create, the package writes both keys after mapping the
body, so a client-sent created_at is replaced. On update, created_at is dropped from the body
(unless writableColumns names it), so a row cannot move its creation date by accident.
- An empty update is a 400. update() with no column to change throws
ValidationFailedException. It does not bump updated_at on its own.

chunks.h: How do I set it up with package-managed timestamps?
chunks.t:
Add the columns to the schema.

Leave the project default on.

Point camelCase keys at the right columns. With keys like createdAt: timestamp('created_at'), tell the entity which keys to use:

The entity setting merges with the project default one level deep, so naming only updatedAt
keeps the default createdAt.

chunks.h: Point camelCase keys at the right columns
chunks.t:
With keys like createdAt: timestamp('created_at'), tell the entity which keys to use:

The entity setting merges with the project default one level deep, so naming only updatedAt
keeps the default createdAt.

chunks.h: Why does my service fail at startup with a timestamps error?
chunks.t:
Because a configured key is not on the table. Before 3.3.1 the package wrote updated_at into the
values, Drizzle ignored the unknown key, and updatedAt silently never moved. The service now checks
both keys when it is built and stops with a message that names the key to use when the column exists
under another name.

Fix it one of three ways:

- Set the keys, as in the step above.
- Turn timestamps off for that entity with config: { timestamps: undefined }.
- Turn them off for the project with defaults: { timestamps: false }.

Application clock, package writes only. 
Package-managed timestamps use the application server's clock, not the database's, and only
writes through the service set them. Raw SQL, migrations and other services do not. For
timestamps that hold on every write path, let the database manage them.

chunks.h: How do I let the database manage createdAt and updatedAt?
chunks.t:
Define the defaults in your Drizzle schema and turn the package's timestamps off.

Define the columns with database defaults. - defaultNow() lets the database set created_at on insert.
- $onUpdate(() = new Date()) makes Drizzle set updatedAt on every update it builds, including
the package's own update().

Add a trigger for writes outside Drizzle. $onUpdate runs in Drizzle, so a script that runs UPDATE users SET name =... directly skips it.
For an updated_at that holds even then, add a PostgreSQL trigger or a MySQL
ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP clause:

Turn package timestamps off. The package then leaves the timestamp columns to the database. Leaving it on would overwrite the
database default with the application clock on every create and update.

chunks.h: Define the columns with database defaults
chunks.t:
- defaultNow() lets the database set created_at on insert.
- $onUpdate(() = new Date()) makes Drizzle set updatedAt on every update it builds, including
the package's own update().

chunks.h: Add a trigger for writes outside Drizzle
chunks.t:
$onUpdate runs in Drizzle, so a script that runs UPDATE users SET name =... directly skips it.
For an updated_at that holds even then, add a PostgreSQL trigger or a MySQL
ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP clause:

The package then leaves the timestamp columns to the database. Leaving it on would overwrite the
database default with the application clock on every create and update.

Aspect Package-managed Database-managed 
--- --- --- 
Clock Application server Database 
Coverage Writes through the service only Every write, including raw SQL (with a trigger) 
Clock control in tests Fake timers on Date Needs database time control 
Setup defaults: { timestamps: true } defaultNow() and $onUpdate(), or triggers 

Package-managed timestamps fit when:

- Every write goes through the service, so coverage is not a concern.
- Tests need fixed times, since a faked Date controls the values.

Database-managed timestamps fit when:

- Several writers touch the table: other services, scripts, manual SQL.
- Several app servers write, and you want one clock instead of each server's.
- You run in production and want the database to have the last word on time.

chunks.h: Can findAll sort by created_at by default?
chunks.t:
Yes, as an opt-in. Set defaults.sortOrder: 'desc' in forRoot, and every entity without its own
defaultSort sorts findAll by its timestamps.createdAt key. An entity with timestamps off gets
no fallback. See pagination and sorting (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/pagination-sorting) for the full sort rules.

Does the package set createdAt and updatedAt automatically?. 
Yes, by default. create sets both, and update, softDelete and restore set updated_at, using the application clock.

How do I use camelCase createdAt and updatedAt keys?. 
Set timestamps: { createdAt: 'createdAt', updatedAt: 'updatedAt' } in the entity's forFeature config. The settings name keys in the Drizzle table object, not SQL column names.

How do I turn timestamps off for one entity?. 
Pass config: { timestamps: undefined } in forFeature. For the whole project, set defaults: { timestamps: false } in forRoot.

Does an upsert change created_at?. 
Only when it inserts. When the row already exists, the update keeps its created_at and sets updated_at to now.

Run Drizzle transactions in NestJS across several service calls. Open one with executeSqlTransaction or db.transaction and pass the handle to each call.

To run Drizzle transactions in NestJS, open a transaction and pass its handle to every call as { transaction: tx }. Inside a service, this.executeSqlTransaction(async (tx) =...) opens it; anywhere else, inject DRIZZLE_DB and call Drizzle's db.transaction. The transaction commits when the callback resolves and rolls back when it throws, so every call that received tx succeeds or fails together.

A call without the handle is outside the transaction. 
Only calls that receive { transaction: tx } join the transaction. A call that leaves it out runs outside the transaction, commits on its own, and is not rolled back when the callback throws.

chunks.h: How do I run several writes in one transaction?
How do I start a transaction outside a service?
chunks.t:
Inject DRIZZLE_DB, the Drizzle instance the module built, and call db.transaction yourself. This suits an orchestrating provider that coordinates several CRUD services:

DrizzleCrudModule.forRoot registers DRIZZLE_DB globally, so any provider can inject it. Your CRUD services themselves must not inject it: forFeature builds them and hands them the database already (see Defining services (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/defining-services)).

Every read and write method takes SqlOperationOptions as its last argument, and transaction is one of its fields:

Some methods open their own transaction when you do not pass one, and join yours when you do:

Method Without transaction With transaction 
--- --- --- 
massCreate, massUpdate, massUpsert, the other mass writes Opens its own transaction, with no savepoint on the happy path Joins yours, with savepoints inside it 
attach, detach, sync Opens its own transaction Joins yours 
create with nested relations Opens its own transaction Joins yours 
find, findAll, create, update, delete and the other single-row calls Runs on the pool, no transaction Joins yours

So a single update is not wrapped in a transaction of its own. Since 3.8.0 it is usually one statement: on PostgreSQL and SQLite, update, softDelete, restore, delete and forceDelete send the write with the whole check in its WHERE (primary key, tenant scope, expected version, and the soft delete state the call needs) and use RETURNING to tell a miss, which then gets the same 404 or 409 as before. The existence check still runs first, as a second statement, when something you can observe runs between the check and the write: a before hook, validateUpdate or mapUpdateDtoToEntity your service overrides, or a before event on the event bus (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events). It always runs first on MySQL, which has no RETURNING. Either way the write re-checks everything, so a row deleted or changed in between is not written. Pass a transaction when the hooks and the write must see the same snapshot.

chunks.h: Can I mix package methods with raw Drizzle?
chunks.t: Yes. tx is the standard Drizzle transaction handle, so anything you can do with db you can do with tx, inside the same transaction:

chunks.h: What happens when I nest transactions?
chunks.t:
It depends on what you pass:

Inside a transaction callback you call Result 
--- --- 
A package method with { transaction: tx } Runs in the same transaction. 
this.executeSqlTransaction(cb, tx) Runs cb in the same transaction. No savepoint. 
this.executeSqlTransaction(cb) without tx Opens a second, independent transaction. It commits or rolls back on its own. 
tx.transaction(cb) (Drizzle) Opens a savepoint. A throw inside rolls back only the savepoint, if you catch it. 

For most requests, one top-level transaction with tx passed everywhere is the right shape.

chunks.h: Which SQLite drivers can run a transaction?
chunks.t: executeSqlTransaction needs an interactive transaction that can wait for async work. On SQLite, libSQL (@libsql/client) has one. Cloudflare D1 has no interactive transactions, and synchronous drivers (better-sqlite3, bun:sqlite, sql.js) cannot wait inside theirs, so on those executeSqlTransaction throws a TransactionException before it opens anything. That also covers every bulk write, nested create and attach / detach / sync. See SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1 (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/sqlite).

The transaction rolls back and the error reaches your caller:

Failure Behaviour 
--- --- 
The callback throws Rolled back. The error propagates. 
A massCreate inside throws BulkOperationException Rolled back. The exception propagates as a 400. 
An after-event subscriber throws Rolled back, because events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events) fire inside the transaction. 
The connection drops mid-transaction The database rolls back. The driver error propagates.

chunks.h: When should I use a transaction?
chunks.t:
Use one when several writes must succeed or fail together:

- Cross-service atomicity. Creating a user and its profile as one unit.
- Read, decide, write. Read a row, decide based on its value, write back. Add a row lock (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/row-locks) so no one changes the row in between.
- Bulk writes plus related changes. A massUpdate and the audit rows that go with it.

Skip it for read-only queries, which need no transaction, and for writes that can succeed or fail independently. Keep network calls, queue publishes and other slow awaits out of the callback: a transaction holds its locks until it ends.

Can I call executeSqlTransaction from a controller?. 
No. It is a protected method, so call it from a method on your service. Outside a service, inject DRIZZLE_DB and call db.transaction.

Do bulk methods need my own transaction?. 
No. Every mass write opens its own transaction. Pass { transaction: tx } only when the bulk call must commit together with other writes.

Does a nested executeSqlTransaction create a savepoint?. 
No. Without the second argument it opens a separate transaction, and with it the callback runs in the same transaction. Use Drizzle's tx.transaction for a savepoint.

Do hooks and events run inside the transaction?. 
Yes, when you pass one. Hooks and module-level events run during the call while the transaction is open, and the event payload carries it, so a subscriber can write in the same transaction.

Upsert rows with Drizzle in NestJS in one statement. upsert and massUpsert insert a row or update the one that holds its unique key.

To upsert with Drizzle in NestJS, call upsert(dto, { conflictTarget }) on your service. It inserts the row, or updates the existing row that already holds the same unique key, in one statement, and returns the row as stored either way. On PostgreSQL that statement is INSERT... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE; on MySQL it is INSERT... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE. massUpsert does the same for many rows in one transaction.

The conflict target needs a unique constraint. 
conflictTarget must name a column (or columns) with a unique constraint or unique index in the database. Without one, PostgreSQL refuses the ON CONFLICT clause.

chunks.h: How do I upsert a row?
chunks.t:
Call upsert with the row and the unique column that decides "already exists":

On PostgreSQL this runs:

The signature is upsert(data, upsertOptions?, options?). The second argument is UpsertOptions, the third is the usual SqlOperationOptions (transaction, relations, counts).

UpsertOptions has two fields, and both are optional:

The default update list includes updatedAt, because the insert sets it, so the timestamp moves when an existing row is updated. createdAt keeps its original value.

chunks.h: How do I get or create a row without changing it?
chunks.t:
Pass update: []. The existing row stays as it is and still comes back, which turns upsert into a get-or-create:

With nothing to overwrite, the package sets the conflict target to its own value so that the database still returns the row. On an entity with a version column (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/optimistic-locking), the version still goes up by one when the row existed.

validateCreate, beforeCreate and mapCreateDtoToEntity run, because the statement starts as an insert, and writableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) applies to the body. The after hooks (afterCreate, afterUpdate) do not run: the package cannot tell an insert from an update without an extra query.

With global hooks on, upsert raises one before and one after event (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events) with the operation name upsert.

chunks.h: Does upsert work with tenant scope, versions and relations?
chunks.t:
Yes, on PostgreSQL:

Feature What upsert does 
--- --- 
Tenant scope (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy) Writes the scope onto the inserted row and adds it to ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE... WHERE. A conflict with another tenant's row updates nothing and is a 404. 
Soft delete (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/soft-delete) A conflict with a row in the trash updates nothing and is a 404, the same as update on that row. Restore it first. 
Version column (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/optimistic-locking) Sets the version to 1 on insert and adds one on update. The version is never taken from the body. 
Scope and version columns Never overwritten from the body, even if you list them in update. 
options.relations, options.counts Loaded onto the returned row, the same as after create. See Relations on writes (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relations-on-writes).

Upsert maps driver errors the same way create does:

Cause Status 
--- --- 
A unique violation on a different key than the conflict target 409 
A value the column cannot hold (too long, wrong type, failed check) 400 
A foreign key that points at no row 400 
An unknown conflictTarget or update column 400 
On a scoped entity, the key belongs to another tenant 404 
The key belongs to a row in the trash 404 

The full mapping is on the errors page (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/errors).

c.s:
// sku is unique too: moving row 1 onto row 2's sku is a 409
await items.upsert({ id: 1, sku: 'A2', name: 'Lamp' }, { conflictTarget: 'id' });

chunks.h: How do I upsert many rows at once?
chunks.t:
Call massUpsert(rows, upsertOptions?, options?). It sends one INSERT... ON CONFLICT for the whole batch, inside a transaction:

When the statement fails, the failing items are named in a BulkOperationException (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations#what-does-a-failed-bulk-call-return-over-http), each by its index in the input array, and nothing is written.

Two rows of the same batch with the same conflict key are a 400 on PostgreSQL ("the same key appears more than once in one upsert"), because one statement cannot update a row twice. Remove duplicates before you call it.

Yes. SQLite has the same INSERT... ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE... WHERE as PostgreSQL, and RETURNING, so upsert and massUpsert behave as described above, the tenant scope guard included. massUpsert needs a driver with async transactions, such as libSQL; see SQLite, libSQL and Cloudflare D1 (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/sqlite).

chunks.h: How does upsert differ on MySQL?
chunks.t:
MySQL uses ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, and three things change:

- Any unique key triggers the update. MySQL does not let you choose the key, so conflictTarget does not pick it there.
- The rows are read back. MySQL has no RETURNING, so the package selects the rows by the conflictTarget columns after the write. Send a value for every conflict target column, otherwise the call is a 400.
- Scoped entities are refused. ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE has no WHERE, so it cannot keep the update inside one tenant. Any upsert on a scoped entity (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy) is a 400 ("upsert on a scoped entity needs PostgreSQL or SQLite") rather than a risk of overwriting another tenant's row.

What does upsert use as the conflict target by default?. 
The primary key. Pass conflictTarget to use another unique column, or a list of columns for a composite unique constraint.

Does upsert tell me whether it inserted or updated?. 
No. It returns the row as stored in both cases, and the after hooks do not run, because telling the two apart would cost an extra query.

Can I upsert without overwriting the existing row?. 
Yes. Pass update: [] and the existing row comes back unchanged, which works as a get-or-create.

Does upsert work on a multi-tenant entity?. 
On PostgreSQL and SQLite, yes: the scope is written onto new rows and a conflict with another tenant's row is a 404. On MySQL an upsert on a scoped entity is a 400.

nestjs-drizzle-crud vs nestjs-paginate compared. One is a CRUD layer for Drizzle ORM, the other a TypeORM helper for paginated, filtered lists.

nestjs-drizzle-crud vs nestjs-paginate is mostly a question of ORM and scope. nestjs-paginate is a pagination and filtering helper for TypeORM repositories and query builders: it reads a list request and returns one page with metadata and links. nestjs-drizzle-crud is a full CRUD layer for Drizzle ORM: lists, pagination and filtering are one part of it, next to create, update, delete, soft delete, upsert and bulk writes.

How this page was checked. 
Facts about nestjs-paginate come from its README (https://github.com/ppetzold/nestjs-paginate) and npm entry (https://www.npmjs.com/package/nestjs-paginate), checked on 2 November 2026 against version 16.0.1. Facts about nestjs-drizzle-crud come from the package source at version.

chunks.h: How do the two libraries differ at a glance?
chunks.t:
nestjs-drizzle-crud nestjs-paginate 
--- --- --- 
ORM Drizzle ORM (drizzle-orm from 0.28.0 up to, not including, 1.0.0) TypeORM (peer typeorm ^1.0.0 in 16.0.1, npm (https://registry.npmjs.org/nestjs-paginate)) 
Databases PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite (since 3.7.0) PostgreSQL, CockroachDB, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite appear in its JSONB support matrix (https://github.com/ppetzold/nestjs-paginate#jsonb-support) 
Scope Reads and writes Reading paginated lists 
Entry point SqlBaseCrudService subclass per table paginate(query, repository, config) and the @Paginate() decorator 
Offset pagination Yes, { data, total, page, limit } Yes, { data, meta, links }, which the README says conforms to JSON:API 
Cursor pagination Yes, opaque cursor over any sortable columns Yes, on numeric and date columns (README (https://github.com/ppetzold/nestjs-paginate#cursor-based-pagination)) 
Filter allowlist Optional; unset allows every column Required: operators are whitelisted per column in filterableColumns 
Unknown filter Always a 400 Ignored by default, 400 with throwOnInvalidFilter: true 
Boolean logic or, and, not groups as bracket keys A filter= expression with AND, OR, NOT and parentheses 
To-many filters some, none, every $any, $all, $none 
Swagger ApiCrudList, ApiCrudQuery (optional @nestjs/swagger) @PaginatedSwaggerDocs, @ApiPaginationQuery, @ApiOkPaginatedResponse 
License MIT MIT

chunks.h: How do the two libraries differ at a glance?
chunks.t: Its npm page shows 16.0.1 published on 19 October 2026, and the GitHub repository (https://github.com/ppetzold/nestjs-paginate) had a push on 30 October 2026, as of November 2026. It is actively released.

Several things, each from its own README (https://github.com/ppetzold/nestjs-paginate):

- Secure filtering by default. A column cannot be filtered at all unless it is in filterableColumns, with its operators listed. In nestjs-drizzle-crud the allowlists are opt-in: with none set, any column can be filtered, sorted and selected. See Allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists).
- Response links. Each page carries links.first, previous, current, next and last, plus meta.totalPages. findAll returns total, page and limit and leaves link building to you.
- A text filter language. filter=(color=$eq:black OR color=$eq:white) AND NOT name=$eq:Leche reads like a sentence and has a complexity cap (100 nodes by default).
- JSONB paths, virtual columns and polymorphic (~) columns for sorting, searching and filtering.
- More databases through TypeORM, such as MariaDB and CockroachDB.
- It works with your existing TypeORM repositories, so there is nothing to migrate if you are on TypeORM.

chunks.h: What does nestjs-drizzle-crud do that nestjs-paginate does not?
chunks.t:
nestjs-paginate covers the read side only; its README documents no create, update or delete helpers. nestjs-drizzle-crud adds:

- Writes: create, update, upsert, softDelete, restore, forceDelete, and mass versions that run in one transaction. See Bulk operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations) and Upsert (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/upsert).
- Generated routes: createCrudController registers list, get, create, update, delete, soft delete, restore and trash routes. See CRUD controller factory (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/controller-factory).
- Safety on writes: writableColumns, optimistic locking, tenant scopes and typed exceptions that map to 404, 409 and 400.
- Relation counts and grouped counts with?counts= and countBy. See Aggregates (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/aggregates).
- Drizzle ORM. If your schema is in Drizzle, nestjs-paginate cannot read it, because it works on TypeORM repositories and query builders.

chunks.h: How do the query strings compare?
chunks.t:
The same list request in each, as each library documents it:

Intent nestjs-drizzle-crud nestjs-paginate 
--- --- --- 
Page and size page=2&limit=5 page=2&limit=5 
Sort sortBy=-color sortBy=color:DESC 
Exact match color=white filter.color=white or filter.color=$eq:white 
Operator age[gte]=3 filter.age=$gte:3 
Range age[between]=4,6 filter.age=$btw:4,6 
Negation not[id][in]=2,5,7 filter.id=$not:$in:2,5,7 
Null seen_at[isNull]=true filter.seenAt=$null 
Starts with summary[startsWith]=term filter.summary=$sw:term 
Search box search=i (searches searchableColumns; a 400 without them) search=i (searches searchableColumns) 
Columns fields=id,name,color select=id,name,color 
Soft-deleted rows withDeleted=true (needs allowTrash) withDeleted=true (needs allowWithDeletedInQuery) 
Cursor cursor= then cursor=<nextCursor cursor=<value with paginationType: PaginationType.CURSOR 

See Parse query strings into filters (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing) for the nestjs-drizzle-crud side.

Choose nestjs-paginate when:

- your project uses TypeORM,
- you only need paginated, filtered list endpoints and write the other routes yourself,
- you want strict per-column operator whitelists by default, response links, or the filter= expression language, or
- you need JSONB path filters or virtual columns.

Choose nestjs-drizzle-crud when:

- your schema is in Drizzle ORM on PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite,
- you want reads and writes from one service, not only list pages,
- you want generated routes, soft delete, upsert, bulk writes or tenant scopes without writing them, or
- you want cursor pagination over text columns as well as numbers and dates.

Set the allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) before you expose a list route, so a client can only touch the columns you name.

Does nestjs-paginate work with Drizzle ORM?. 
No. Its README describes it as a helper for TypeORM repositories or query builders, and version 16.0.1 lists typeorm as a peer dependency.

Does nestjs-drizzle-crud return pagination links?. 
No. findAll returns data, total, page and limit, plus hasMore when the count is skipped. Build links from those values if your clients need them.

Which one rejects unknown filters?. 
nestjs-drizzle-crud always answers 400 for an unknown column or operator. nestjs-paginate ignores them by default and answers 400 when throwOnInvalidFilter is true.

Can nestjs-drizzle-crud whitelist filter operators per column?. 
It whitelists columns, not operators: filterableColumns names the columns a filter may use, and any operator works on a listed column.

nestjs-drizzle-crud vs @nestjsx/crud compared. One builds CRUD on Drizzle ORM, the other on TypeORM, with a different query syntax and release history.

nestjs-drizzle-crud vs @nestjsx/crud comes down to your ORM and how current you need the library to be. @nestjsx/crud generates REST controllers with a @Crud() decorator and ships a TypeORM service and a frontend request builder. nestjs-drizzle-crud gives you a CRUD service for Drizzle ORM tables, a query string parser and an optional controller factory. The last stable @nestjsx/crud release is from May 2020.

How this page was checked. 
Facts about @nestjsx/crud come from its own README, wiki, source and npm entry, checked on 2 November 2026, with a link next to each one. Facts about nestjs-drizzle-crud come from the package source at version. If something here has changed upstream, the linked source wins.

chunks.h: How do the two libraries differ at a glance?
chunks.t: They solve the same problem (stop writing the same list, get, create, update and delete code per entity) from opposite ends: @nestjsx/crud starts from the controller, nestjs-drizzle-crud starts from the service.

chunks.h: How do the two libraries differ at a glance?
chunks.t:
nestjs-drizzle-crud @nestjsx/crud 
--- --- --- 
ORM Drizzle ORM (drizzle-orm from 0.28.0 up to, not including, 1.0.0) TypeORM, through @nestjsx/crud-typeorm (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud#packages) 
Databases PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite (dialect: "postgresql" \ "mysql" \ "sqlite") Through TypeORM; the README lists no databases of its own 
Entry point SqlBaseCrudService subclass per table @Crud() decorator on a controller 
Generated routes Optional, with createCrudController Always, from @Crud() 
Query string age[gte]=18&sortBy=-name&with=region filter=age\ \ $gte\ \ 18&sort=name,DESC&join=region (wiki (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/wiki/Requests)) 
Frontend query builder No Yes, RequestQueryBuilder in @nestjsx/crud-request (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud#packages) 
Replace (PUT) route No Yes, replaceOneBase (wiki (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/wiki/Controllers)) 
Soft delete Yes, on by default, with restore, trash and force delete Yes, query.softDelete plus a recover route in the source (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/blob/master/packages/crud/src/interfaces/query-options.interface.ts) 
Keyset (cursor) pagination Yes, findByCursor Not documented 
Optimistic locking, tenant scopes, upsert Yes Not documented 
License MIT MIT

chunks.h: How do the two libraries differ at a glance?
chunks.t: "Not documented" means the README (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud) and wiki (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/wiki) do not describe it. It does not mean it is impossible to build on top.

chunks.h: What is the current state of @nestjsx/crud?
chunks.t:
As of November 2026 the npm and GitHub records show no release since early 2021:

Fact Value Source 
--- --- --- 
Latest version on npm (latest tag) 5.0.0-alpha.3, published 11 February 2021 npm registry (https://registry.npmjs.org/@nestjsx/crud) 
Last non-prerelease version 4.6.2, published 14 May 2020 npm registry (https://registry.npmjs.org/@nestjsx/crud) 
Last commit on master 7 December 2022 commit history (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/commits/master) 
Repository archived No GitHub (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud) 
Open issues and pull requests 290 GitHub (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud/issues) 
Packages @nestjsx/crud, @nestjsx/crud-request, @nestjsx/crud-typeorm README (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud#packages) 

A community fork, @dataui/crud (https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dataui/crud) (gid-oss/dataui-nestjs-crud (https://github.com/gid-oss/dataui-nestjs-crud)), last published 5.3.4 on 9 April 2024, also as of November 2026.

Three things, all documented in its own README (https://github.com/nestjsx/crud):

- A frontend request builder. RequestQueryBuilder from @nestjsx/crud-request builds the query string in the browser, so client code does not concatenate strings by hand. nestjs-drizzle-crud has no client package.
- Controllers first. One @Crud() decorator registers every route, including PUT replace and POST /bulk. In nestjs-drizzle-crud the bulk routes are off until you turn them on, and there is no PUT.
- TypeORM. If your entities are TypeORM classes and you do not plan to move, nestjs-drizzle-crud cannot use them: it reads Drizzle table objects.

chunks.h: What does nestjs-drizzle-crud do that @nestjsx/crud does not document?
chunks.t:
Everything below is in the nestjs-drizzle-crud source today:

- Keyset pagination with findByCursor and?cursor=, beside offset pages. See Cursor pagination (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/cursor-pagination).
- Collection filters with some, none and every on has-many and many-to-many relations, compiled to subqueries so total stays right. See Relation filters (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/relation-filters).
- Allowlists for filter, sort, select, search, load and write, each one a 400 when broken. See Allowlists (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists).
- Writes beyond create and update: upsert, massUpdate, massSoftDelete, restore, forceDelete, optimistic locking and row locks.
- Tenant scopes read from a per-request CrudContext. See Multi-tenancy (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy).
- Typed exceptions that map to 404, 409 and 400 without a custom filter. See Errors (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/errors).

chunks.h: How do the query strings compare?
chunks.t:
Both libraries read filters, sort, pagination, field selection and relations from the URL, with different syntax. The same request in each:

Intent nestjs-drizzle-crud @nestjsx/crud 
--- --- --- 
Exact match name=Asia filter=name\ \ $eq\ \ Asia 
Operator population[gte]=1000000 filter=population\ \ $gte\ \ 1000000 
OR or[0][code]=IN&or[1][code]=NP or=code\ \ $eq\ \ IN&or=code\ \ $eq\ \ NP 
Sort sortBy=-name,id sort=name,DESC&sort=id,ASC 
Page page=2&limit=20 page=2&limit=20 
Fields fields=id,name fields=id,name 
Relation with=region join=region 
Relation column filter region[name]=Asia join=region&filter=region.name\ \ $eq\ \ Asia 

In nestjs-drizzle-crud a bare value on a text column (name=Asia) is case-insensitive while sql.caseSensitive is false, the default; name[eq]=Asia is a plain =. The full operator mapping is on Migrating from @nestjsx/crud (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/migrate-from-nestjsx-crud). Note that in nestjs-drizzle-crud an unknown column or operator is always a 400, never ignored. See Parse query strings into filters (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/query-parsing).

Choose @nestjsx/crud when:

- your project is on TypeORM and will stay there,
- you already run it in production and it does what you need, or
- you want the RequestQueryBuilder client and the generated PUT route.

Check that its peer and transitive dependencies fit your NestJS and TypeORM versions first, given that the last stable release dates from May 2020.

Choose nestjs-drizzle-crud when:

- your schema is in Drizzle ORM, or you are moving to it,
- you want the CRUD logic in a service you can call from code, jobs and controllers alike,
- you need cursor pagination, upsert, tenant scopes or optimistic locking without writing them, or
- you want a library with recent releases (see the changelog (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/changelog)).

It is not the right pick on TypeORM or Prisma, or on a database other than PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite.

Can nestjs-drizzle-crud use my TypeORM entities?. 
No. It reads Drizzle table objects such as pgTable(...), so you need a Drizzle schema for each table first. Drizzle Kit can pull one from an existing database.

Is @nestjsx/crud still maintained?. 
As of November 2026 its latest npm version is 5.0.0-alpha.3 from February 2021, the last stable one is 4.6.2 from May 2020, and the last commit on master is from December 2022. The repository is not archived.

Does nestjs-drizzle-crud have a query builder for the frontend?. 
No. Clients write the query string themselves, as in age[gte]=18&sortBy=-name. The @nestjsx/crud-request package has RequestQueryBuilder for that job.

Does nestjs-drizzle-crud generate controllers like @Crud()?. 
Yes, with createCrudController(Service, options). It is optional: the service works on its own, and you can write the controller by hand.
